trasa-rēṇum +++(=sūryakiraṇē dr̥śyamānaṁ kaṇam)+++ api hi tatō'ṇiṣṭhatayā 'bhimata-dravyāntarāpēkṣayā 
mahima-guṇa-śālīti vadanti ।  
na ca tryaṇukādiṣu brahma-śabda-prayōgaḥ ।+++(5)+++ 

ēvaṁ sarvatra prayōga-darśanāt  

paṅka-ja--śabda-vyavasthāpaka--  
kumudādi-vyāvr̥tta--tāmarasānuvr̥tta--  
padmatva-jātivat  

brahma-śabda-prayōga-viṣaya--  
pañcaṣa-vyakty--anuvr̥tta--  
anya-vyāvr̥ttākārādarśanād  
anēka-śakti-kalpanē prāptē,  

an-anyathā-siddhasya prayōgasya śakti-kalpakatvāt,  
brahma-śabda-prayōga-viṣayēṣv anyēṣu ca br̥hattva-guṇa-lēśa-yōgēna prayōgasyānyathā-siddhatvāc ca,  
nānēka-śakti-kalpanaṁ yuktam । 

tasmāt  
puruṣōttama ēva pravr̥tti-nimitta-pauṣvalyavati mukhyatvam, anyatraupacārikatvaṁ ca । aupacārikastu prayōgaḥ saṅkōcasaha iṣṭaḥ,  
na tu sārvatrika iti ।  

**śruta-prakāśikā - bhagavacchabdayōgaḥ**—
tam imaṁ nyāyam abhiprētya  
bhagavacchabdasya puruṣōttama ēva  
mukhyatvam anyatrāmukhyatvaṁ ca bhagavatā parāśarēṇōktam । 

tathā hi-jñānādimātraṁ vā  
niraṅkuśa-jñānādikaṁ vā  
bhagavac-chabda-pravr̥tti-nimitam ?  
ādyē, pipīlikādāvapi bhagavacchabdaḥ prayujyēta ।  
dvitīyē tu sarvatra niravadhika-jñānādy-abhāvāt pravr̥tti-nimittāsiddhēr  
naika-śaktyā sarvatra mukhyatvam ।  
anēka-śakti-kalpanaṁ cāyuktam ; prayōgānyathā+++(→gauṇa-vr̥tti)+++-siddhēr  
iti bhagavat-paraśarābhiprāyaḥ ॥ 

> nanu, 
> 
> > “utpattiṁ pralayaṁ caiva  
> bhūtānām āgatiṁ gatim ।  
> vētti vidyām avidyāṁ ca  
> sa vācyō bhagavān iti" 
> 
> iti granthōktēṣv aupacārika-bhagavac-chabda-prayōga-yōgyēṣu  
> yat alaukikārtha-sākṣāt-kāritvam asti  
> tadēva pravr̥tti-nimittī-kr̥tya  
> bhagavac-chabdaḥ sarvatra mukhyaḥ syāt ॥ 

naivam -  
a-laukikārtha-sākṣāt-karaṇa-mātrasya prayōgāviṣaya-vyāvr̥ttatvābhāvāt ।  
na hi samādhi-paryanta-yōga-kāṣṭhā-niṣṭhēṣu  
kēśi-dhvaja--khāṇḍikya--prahlādādiṣu bhagavac-chabdaḥ prayujyatē ।  

kiñca pratyakṣa-mūla-vyutpattyā  
gavādi-śabdānām iva  
āgama-mūla-vyutpattyā  
samagra-ṣāḍguṇyādimaty ēva  
tasya mukhyatvāvagamāt 

> "jñāna-śakti-balaiśvarya-  
> vīrya-tējāṁsy aśēṣataḥ ।  
> bhagavac-chabda-vācyāni  
> vinā hēyair guṇādibhiḥ" 

[[20]]  
iti nirdōṣatva-paryantānāṁ jñānādīnāṁ pravr̥ttinimittatayā vācyatvam ucyatē ।  
nirdōṣatvaś ca nimittatayā vācyatvēnōcyatē ;  
anyathā tad-uktivaiyarthyāt ।  
na hy avācyaṁ sarvaṁ niṣēddhavyam ।  
anuktyaiva hy avācyatvaṁ siddhayati ।  

na ca jñāna-śakty-ādiṣv aikaikasya pravr̥tti-nimittatvam ;  
kintu jñānādi-samudāyasyaiva tat ।  
anyathā *aśēṣata* iti padavaiyarthyāt ।  
aiśvaryasya samagrasyēty uktatvāt  
gavādiṣv atiprasaṅgabhayāc ca  
prakarṣa-viśēṣavatāṁ jñānādīnāṁ samudāyasyaiva  
pravr̥tti-nimittatvam uktam ity abhyupēyam ।+++(4)+++  

ēvaṁ nyāya-siddhārthasyā''gama-siddhārthō  
bhāṣyē dr̥ṣṭāntī-kr̥taḥ bhagavac-chabdavad iti ।  

**śruta-prakāśikā - pārāśaryōktiḥ**—
tathā [ca] bhagavatā pārāśaryēṇa,  

> “paraṁ jaiminir mukhyatvāt”,

> “syāc caikasya brahma-śabdavat" 

ity-ādi-sūtrēṣu  
brahma-śabdasya bhagavaty ēva mukhyatvam uttaratrōktam ।  
atō yathōkta ēvārthaḥ ।  

+++(ēvam asnin nyāyē brahmasūtralēkhasyābhiprāya uktaḥ, tat-pitur api! 5)+++

**śruta-prakāśikā - purāṇa-pramāṇam**—
tathā ca spaṣṭīkr̥taṁ śrīmati gāruḍē purāṇē, 

> "vēdē bhūri-prayōgācca  
> guṇa-yōgācca śārṅgiṇi ।  
> tasminn ēva brahma-śabdō  
> mukhyavr̥ttō mahāmunē" 

ityārabhya 

> " yasmin prayujyamānē tu  
> guṇayōgaḥ supuṣkalaḥ ।  
> tatraiva mukhyavr̥ttō'yam  
> anyatra tūpacārataḥ" 

iti । 

ēvaṁ śabda-sāmarthyam upapāditam ।  

atha brahma-śabdasyānēkārtha-mukhya-vr̥ttatvē 'py ētat-sūtrasthasya tasyārtha-svābhāvyāt puruṣōttama-paratvam ucyatē । 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tāpatrayāturair a-mr̥tatvāya  
sa ēva **jijñāsyaḥ** ।  
atas **sarvēśvara** ēva  
jijñāsā-karma-bhūtaṁ **brahma** ।  

**Thibaut**—
The Lord only is enquired into, for the sake of immortality, by all those who are afflicted with the triad of pain. Hence the Lord of all is that Brahman which, according to the Sūtra, constitutes the object of enquiry. 

**śruta-pradīpikā**—
athārthasāmarthyamupapādayati - tāpēti । na hi kārāgr̥hanigalitō nigalamōcanāya yācyaḥ ; kintu yacchāsanānnigalanaṁ tannivr̥ttau sa ēvētyabhiprayantī tamēvam ityādiśrutirihānustriyatē । nigamayati - ata iti ; ataḥ śabdavaśādarthavaśāccētyarthaḥ ।

**śruta-prakāśikā - sa ēva jijñāsyaḥ**—
tāpatrayāturairiti ।  
"saḥ ēva amr̥tattvāyēti" padaiḥ,  

> " tam ēvaṁ vidvān amr̥ta iha bhavati  
> nānyaḥ panthāḥ" 

ity-ādi-śruty-arthō vivakṣitaḥ ।  
ata ēva hi 'puruṣōttamō'bhidhīyatē' ity uktam ।  
śrutēr api pūrvōkta--hēya-pratyanīkatva--  
kalyāṇa-guṇākaratva-viśiṣṭa ēva  
tāpa-trayāturair upāsyaḥ,  
na tu tēṣv anyatama iti ।  
na hi kārāgāra-nigalita ēva tan-mōcanārthibhir abhyarthanīyaḥ ।+++(4)+++  

tathā ca vaiṣṇavē purāṇē  
nirdōṣa-kalyāṇa-guṇākarasyaiva mumukṣūpāsyatvamuktam,  

“sa sarvabhūta-prakr̥tiṁ vikārān",  
"samasta-kalyāṇaguṇātmakō'sau" ityādinā,  
"tad jñānam ajñānam atō'nyad uktam" ityantēna । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - ataḥ**—
brahma-śabda-vyākhyāṁ nigamayati ata iti ।  
**ataḥ** nirdōṣamaṅgalaguṇākarasya sarvēśvarasyaiva tāpatrayāturair jijñāsyatvād atra tāpatrayātura-jijñāsyatayōktaṁ brahma  
**sarvēśvara** ēvētyarthaḥ । 

yadvā **ataḥ** - ukta-śabda-sāmarthyād artha-sāmarthyāc cēty arthaḥ ।  

**śruta-prakāśikā - brahma-śabdārtha-vyutpattiḥ**—
> nanu brahma-śabdō  
> vyutpannō+++(=ghaṭita-śabdārtha-sambandhaḥ)+++ 'vyutpannō vā bhagavati mukhyaḥ ? 
>
> a-vyutpannatvē bōdhakatva-virahiṇas tasya  
na kvacin mukhyatvam ।  
> 
> nāpi vyutpannaḥ sa mukhyaḥ ; alaukikē'rthē vyutpaty-asambhavāt ।  
> 
> katham apratītē vyavahārāviṣayē buddhi-pūrvikā, yādr̥cchikī ca vyutpattiḥ sambhavati? 

ucyatē ।  

yathā kāminī-candana-bhavanādiṣu  
prayōgēṇa sukha-viṣayatayā vyutpannasya svarga-śabdasya  
“yasmin nōṣṇam" ity-ādy-arthavāda-pada-samabhivyāhārēṇa +alaukika-sukha-viśēṣa-viṣayatayā vyutpattiḥ,  

yathā lōkē kvacid apy avyutpannatvē 'pi yūpa-āhavanīya-raphya-kapāla1-caṣāla cātvālādi-śabdānāṁ vākyāntara-padāntara-samabhivyāhārāt tat-tad-artha-viṣayatayā vyutpattiḥ, 

ēvaṁ brahmātmēśvarādi-śabdānāṁ  
lōkē kēṣucid arthēṣu prayōgād  
vyutpattau satyām a-satyām api,   

> "yatō vā imāni bhūtāni jāyantē",  
> "satyaṁ jñānamanantaṁ brahma" 

ity-ādi-prasiddhārtha-vākyāntara-padāntara-samabhivyāhārāt  
alaukika-paramātma-viṣayatva-vyutpattir upapadyatē । 

1\. kapālēti । aṣṭākapālam ity-ādau yajñōpayujyamānē vilakṣaṇākr̥ti-dravyē   
viśēṣa-rūpēṇa vā itara-sādhāraṇa-rūpēṇa vā lōka-prasiddhir nēti bhāvaḥ । 

atō brahmaśabdasyōktarītyā bhagavatyēva mukhyatvaṁ yuktam । 

#### 5 jijñāsā

**vi॰pra॰**—
jñātumicchā - jijñāsā।  
icchāyā iṣyamāṇa-pradhānatvād  
iṣyamāṇaṁ **jñānam** iha **vidhīyatē**  
+++(lakṣaṇayā - yatō na hīcchā vidhātum arhā। sannantaprayōgō rāgataḥ prāptiṁ jñāpayitum।)+++। 

**Thibaut**—
The word 'jijñāsā' is a desiderative formation meaning 'desire to know.'  
And as in the case of any desire the desired object is the chief thing, the Sūtra means to enjoin knowledge – which is the object of the desire of knowledge.  

**śruta-pradīpikā**—
prakr̥tipratyayavibhāgēna dvitīyaṁ padaṁ vyācaṣṭē - jñātumiti ।  

icchāyāḥ kāryatvē pratītē'pi  
snātvā bhuñjīta itivad aprāptē'ṁśē vidhir ity arthaḥ ।  
sannanta-nirdēśō vicārasya rāga-prāptatva-jñāpanāya ।+++(5)+++  

tathāca dharmajijñāsā ity-atrāpi jñānaṁ vicāra-rūpaṁ vidhēyam ।  
vicāraḥ kartavyaḥ ity anyatrōktēḥ । 

pramitis tu phalatayā artha-siddhā ।  
mīmāṁsā hīyam ।  

iha -upakrama-sūtrē ।  
anēnāsya sūtrasya jijñāsya-viśēṣa-paratva-vyudāsaḥ । ārambhaṇīyatvē siddhē hi jijñāsya-viśēṣa-nirṇayaḥ । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - yaugikārthaḥ**—
[[21]] 

atha jijñāsā-śabdasya vyākhyēyatva-sphōraṇāya  
prakr̥ti-pratyaya-vibhāgaṁ darśayati **jñātumicchā jijñāsē**ti ।  

**śruta-prakāśikā - kiṁ vidhēyam?**—
> viṣaya-vailakṣaṇyādhīnāyā icchāyāḥ  
kathaṁ vidhēyatvam 

(1 vidhēyatvaṁ prayatnasādhyatvam ।  
tat vicārātmaka-jñānē sustham । )

ityatrāha -  
**icchāyā** iti ।  
jñānasya vidhānārhatām āha **iṣyamāṇa-pradhānatvād** iti ।  

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
vidhānārhatām iti ।   
iṣyamāṇa-padēnāniṣpannatva-jñāpanāt  
niṣpādanārhatvam ucyata iti bhāvaḥ ।  
iṣyamāṇa-pradhānatvād  
iti karmaṇaḥ prādhānyam uktam

san-vācyāyā icchāyā dhātv-arthaḥ karma;  
karmaṇaś ca kriyā śēṣa-bhūtā;  
tat-siddhy-arthatvāt tasyāḥ ।  
yathā yāgīya-vrīhy-ādēḥ prōkṣaṇādiḥ (pū. mī. 2-1-4)।  

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
udāhr̥tyōpapādayati - yathā yāgīyēti । tathā ca guṇa-pradhānayōr madhyē  
pradhānē tad-anvayō yukta iti bhāvaḥ ।  
*iṣyamāṇa-pradhānatvād* ityasya iṣyamāṇa-siddhy-arthatvād iti vā'rthaḥ - tathā vivaraṇāt । 

kartuḥ kriyayā āptum iṣṭatamatvaṁ hi *karmatvam* ।  
ataḥ prakr̥ty-arthabhūta-jñāna-karmikēcchā tat-siddhayarthā ।  
ata icchāyā iṣyamāṇa-jñāna-pradhānatvād  
iṣyamāṇaṁ jñānaṁ vidhēyam ityarthaḥ । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - aprāpta-vidhānam**—
> jijñāsāyāḥ kartavyatvē pratīyamānē  
kathaṁ jñānasya vidhēyatvam ?

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
śābdasyāsambhavaṁ śaṅkatē - jijñāsāyā iti ।  
"saviśēṣaṇē hī"ti nyāyō'tra bhāvyaḥ +++(=??)+++। 

ucyatē ।  
yathā,  
'snātvā bhuñjīta',  
'prāṅmukhō bhuñjīta'  

ity-atra bhuji-dhātōr vidhi-pratyayāntatvād  
bhōjanasya kartavyatvē pratītē'pi  
snāna--prāṅ-mukhatva--niyamayōr ēva vidhēs tātparyam  
iti artha-sva-bhāvād abhyupagamyatē -  
tayōr aprāptatvāt,  
"aprāptē hi śāstram arthavat";+++(5)+++  
tatra bhōjanaṁ cānyataḥ prāptam anūdyatē -  
ēvam icchāyā vidhēyatvāsambhavāt  
tad-viṣaya-bhūtaṁ vicārātmakaṁ jñānam ēva tātparyatō vidhīyatē । 

"iṣyamāṇaṁ jñānam ihābhiprētam"  
iti hi +++(vēdānta-)+++sārē'bhihitam ।  

**śruta-prakāśikā - sannanta-prayōgaḥ**—
sann-anta-nirdēśaś ca,  
"nididhyāsitavyaḥ", "vijijñāsitavyaḥ", "tadvijijñāsasva"  
ity-ādi-śruty-anusārēṇa kriyatē ।  
śrutiś ca upāya-daśā-prabhr̥ti-bhagavaj-jñānasya prīti-rūpatvēna icchā-viṣayatvāt  
tathā nirdiśati ।+++(5)+++  

yadvā, brahma-jijñāsēti sann-anta-nirdēśō  
vicārasya rāga-prāptatva-jñāpanārthaḥ ।  
ēvamētra, “dharma-jijñāsā" ityatrāpi ।  

**śruta-prakāśikā - tarka-rūpaṁ jñānaṁ vihitam**—
atra tarka-rūpaṁ jñānaṁ vidhēyam;  
tarkānugr̥hīta-vākya-janya--pramiti-rūpajñānaṁ tu  
phalatvān na vidhēyam - +++(4)+++  

> 'pramiti-rūpaṁ jñānaṁ vidhēyam,  
tarka-rūpaṁ jñānam ārtham' 

ity api parair uktam,  
antar-nīta-vicāram ākṣipatīti । 

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
2 jñānaṁ vidhēyamiti ।  

> 'brahmātma-bhāvōpāyō jñānam ēṣitavyam ।  
> nirṇayātmaka-tad-icchā-mukhēna mīmāṁsāyāṁ pravartyatē' 

iti bhāmaty-uktēr iti bhāvaḥ ।  

> atra ēṣitavyamiti tavya-pratyayaḥ anuvādatva-vyāvr̥ttayē  

iti kalpataruḥ ।  
atō jñāpyatva-rūpa-vidhēyatva-siddhiḥ । 

> 'nirṇayaśca vicāra-sādhya  
iti tat-kartavyatā'rthād gamyatē ।  
ārthikē cāsminnarthē kartavya-padādhyāhāraḥ ।  
śrautas tu brahmajñānēcchā bhavituṁ yuktētyēṣa ēva' 

iti ca kalpataruḥ । 

ity apīti apiśabdēna, 

> 'tarka-rūpa-jñānasyāpi sautra-jñā-dhātunā grahaṇaṁ tad-iṣṭam ;  
> 
>> 'avagati-paryantaṁ jñānaṁ san-vācyāyā icchāyāḥ karma' 
>
> iti nirṇayōpadhāyaka-jñānārthakatvasya śāṅkara-bhāṣya-sva-rasa-labdhatvāt' 

iti sūcyatē । 

tatōpi prāg-uktapakṣaḥ sādhīyān । 

vēdāntārtha-vicārātmaka-nyāya-nibandhana-rūpaṁ hi śāstraṁ  
brahma-mīmāṁsēti prasiddhiḥ । pramitiś ca phalam ।  
ata ēva hi brahma-vicāraḥ kartavya  
iti mādhyē vakṣyatē ।  

sann-antasyāsya jñā-dhātōr jñāna-sāmānya-vācinō viśēṣākāṅkṣāyāṁ  
samucita-viśēṣa-paryavasānaṁ hi nyāyyam । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - iha**—
brahmaṇō jijñāsā kartavyā;  
na tu kapila-sugatādy-abhimatānāṁ pradhānādi-tattvānām  
iti jñātavya-viśēṣa-nirṇayaparam idaṁ sūtraṁ  
vyākhyātaṁ yādava-prakāśācāryaiḥ ।  
tadvyāvr̥ttyartha **iha**-śabdaḥ ।  
iha-asmin upakramasūtra ityarthaḥ । 

[[22]]  
brahmaṇō jijñāsyatvamātrē siddhē hi  
tasyaiva jijñāsyatva-siddhiḥ ।  
na cōbhayaṁ sūtra-pratipādyam ;  
"brahma jijñāsyam ēva",  
"brahmaiva jijñāsyam" iti vākyabhēdapraṅgāt ।  

> nanu brahmaṇō mumukṣubhir niyamēna jijñāsyatvaṁ  
tantrāntara-siddhānāṁ pradhānādīnām ajijñāsyatvēna vinā  
na siddhyatīti  
brahma-jijñāsyatva-samarthanē  
pradhānādīnām ajijñāsyatva-samarthana-maryādā ''patatīti  
na vākya-bhēdaprasaṅga 

iti cēt - na;  
adhīta-kramēṇa vēdārthē nirūpyamāṇē  
pūrva bhāga-vicārasya  
pradhānādi-nirāsa-nirapēkṣatvāt ।  
na hy ēkasya prabandhasyaikadēśē nirūpitē  
tad-ēkadēśāntara-nirūpaṇasya prabandhāntara-pramēya-nirāsa-sāpēkṣatā bhavati ।  
na hi pūrvaṣaṭkē nirūpitē sati  
uttaraṣaṭkanirūpaṇaṁ kapila-sugatādi-mata-vyudasanēna vinā na sambhavati ।  

yadi 

> vēdāntārtha-śraddhā-draḍhimnē tad-itara-pakṣa-nirasanam apēkṣitam iha kriyata  

iti matam, tad anupapannam ; kr̥ta-karatva-prasaṅgāt ।  
ētad uktaṁ bhavati —  
iha pradhānādīnām ajijñāsyatvaṁ  
kiṁ vēdāntānām atat-parasyōpapādanēna samarthyatē,  
uta kapila-sugatādy-āgamāprāmāṇya--tat-pramēya-daussthya-pratipādanēna samarthyatē ? ।  
na prathamaḥ ;  
īkṣaty-adhikaraṇādibhir vēdāntānām a-tat-paratvasya vakṣyamāṇatayā  
atra vaktavyatvābhāvāt ।  
na dvitīyaḥ  
vēda-viruddha-smr̥tīnām a-prāmāṇyasya  
pūrva-mīmāṁsāyām ēva samarthitatvāt ;  
sāṅkhya saugatādy abhimata-pramēya-dausthyasya  
tarka-pādē pratipādayiṣyamāṇatvāt । 

“vipratiṣēdhāc cāsamañjasam ", "itarēṣāṁ cānupalabdhēḥ ",  
"ētēna yōgaḥ pratyuktaḥ ",  
"udāsīnānāmapi caitraṁ siddhiḥ ", "antyāvasthitēś cōbhayanityatvād aviśēṣaḥ "  
ityādibhiḥ sūtrais  
tad-ukta-mōkṣa--tad-upāya-nirāsasyāpi  
kariṣyamāṇatayā cātra vaktavyābhāvāt । 

kiñ ca,  
"ētēna sarvē vyākhyātā vyākhyātāḥ" ityatra,  
"anāvr̥ttiḥ śabdād anāvr̥ttiḥ śabdāt ”  
iti śāstrāntē ca,  

> "sūtrābhyāsa-phalam anuktāṁśa-jñāpanam ;  
anuktāṁśaśca sāṅkhya-yōgāvagamyaḥ " 

iti vadatām,  
mōkṣasya sāṅkhya-yōga-samuccaya-sāpēkṣatvaṁ ca pratipādayatāṁ  
saugatādivat sāṅkhyādi-nirāsēna  
śārīrakasyaivārambhaṇīyatva-pratijñānam  
atīva vyāhatam ॥ 

> sāṅkhya-yōgayōr viruddhāṁśābhiprāyam anādaraṇīyatva-kathanam 

iti cēn na ;  
viruddhāṁśānādaraṇīyatvasya virōdhādhikaraṇa-nyāya-siddhatvādēva ।  
atō yādava-prakāśakr̥taṁ sūtra tātparya - varṇanam anupapannam iti ihaśabdābhiprāyaḥ । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - vidhīyatē**—
vidhīyata iti ।  
ajñāta-jñāpanaṁ vidhir iha vivakṣitam ;  
na sva-pravr̥tta-pravarttanam ;  
rāgataḥ pravr̥ttēr vakṣyamāṇatvāt । 

rāgataḥ pravr̥ttasyāpi  
pūrva-pakṣa-yuktyā 'nārambhaṇīyatā-buddhau satyām ārambhaṇīyatva-jñāpanam ।  

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
> nanu vicārē rāgataḥ pravr̥ttir asti cēt,  
tasya jñātatvam apy asti;  
a-jñātē pravr̥tty-ayōgāt ।  
ataḥ ajñāta-jñāpanaṁ katham 

ityatra vivakṣitam āha  
ārambhaṇīyatva-jñāpanam iti ।   
ētad-bhāṣya-sandarbha-vyākhyāna-rīty-antaraṁ bhāṣyārtha-darpaṇē draṣṭavyam । 

hi ajñāta-jñāpanam ।  
atō **vidhīyata** ityasya  
svayamēva pravartata iti vakṣyamāṇa-granthēnāvirōdhaḥ । 

**vi॰pra॰**—
mīmāṁsā-pūrva-bhāga-jñātasya karmaṇō  
'lpāsthira-phalatvād  
uparitana-bhāgāvasēyasya brahma-jñānasyānantākṣaya-phalatvāc ca,  
pūrva-vr̥ttāt karma-jñānād anantaraṁ,  
tata ēva hētōr,  
brahma jñātavyam  
ity uktaṁ bhavati ।  

**Thibaut**—
The purport of the entire Sūtra then is as follows: 'Since the fruit of works known through the earlier part of the Mīmāṁsā is limited and non-permanent, and since the fruit of the knowledge of Brahman – which knowledge is to be reached through the latter part of the Mīmāṁsā--is unlimited and permanent; for this reason Brahman is to be known, after the knowledge of works has previously taken place.'--

**śruta-pradīpikā**—
sa cōttaratra īkṣatērnāśabdam ityārabhya kriyatē । atha vākyārthaṁ yōjayati- mīmāṁsēti । pūrvavr̥ttādityādi pratijñā । anyadupapādakam । pūrvabhāgōparitanabhāga śabdābhyāṁ vyākhyānasya kramaniyamānanvitabhāgādhyayanātmakatvaṁ darśitam । taddhētubhūtaṁ vyākhyēyasya tathātvaṁ pūrvaṁ padayōjanāyāmuktam । ubhayatrōbhayaṁ vācyam । granthalāghavāyaivamuktiḥ । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - saṅgatiḥ**—
itthaṁ padārthā vyākhyātāḥ ।  
atha sūtrasya  
vākyārtham āha mīmāṁsēti ।  
atra 

> pūrvavr̥ttāt karma-jñānād anantaraṁ  
tata ēva hētōr  

iti **athāta** śabdārtha uktaḥ ।  
brahma jñātavyam iti brahmajijñāsāpadārthaḥ ।  
jñātavyaṁ vicārayōgyam । 

tata ēvēty ēva-kārēṇa śāstrāntarādhigama-nairapēkṣyam atha-śabda-phalitam abhiprētam ।  

uktaṁ bhavatīti -  
śabdatō'rthataś cēti bhāvaḥ ।  

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
1 ēvakārēṇēti ।  
advaitinaḥ, athētyanēna yad ānantaryam ucyatē,  
tasyaiva hētutvam ataḥśabdēnōcyatē  
iti svarasapratītaṁ parityajya,  
atha = sādhana-catuṣṭaya-sampattyanantaram  
ataḥ = vēdēnaiva karmaṇām anitya-phalakatva-bōdhanād  
ity arthaṁ varṇayanti,  
tat-khaṇḍanamapy ēvakārēṇēti dhyēyam ।  
tattvaṭīkōktamapi jñēyam । 

**śruta-prakāśikā**—
[[23]] 

> katham asya sūtrasyāyam artha 

iti śaṅkāyāṁ  
tad-upapādayati mīmāṁsētyādinā ।  
athāta ityādipadānāṁ yathōkta ēvārthaḥ;  
karma-brahma-mīmāṁsayōr aikaśāstrarūyāt ।  
aikaśāstryaṁ ca  
niyata-paurvāparyabhāga-dvayātmaka--  
vēdākhyaika-prabandha-vyākhyāna-rūpatvād ity arthaḥ ।  
atra vyākhyēyasya pūrvāpara-bhāvēnāvasthita-bhāga-dvaya-rūpatvam,  
tad-dhētukaṁ vyākhyānasya paurvāparya-viśēṣa-viśiṣṭa-bhāgadvaya-rūpatvaṁ cōbhayaṁ  
padayōjanāyāṁ vākya-yōjanāyāṁ ca vaktavyam -  
tathāpi grantha-lāgha-vārthaṁ  
pada-yōjanāyām ' adhīta-sāṅga-saśiraska-vēdasya' iti vyākhyēyasya  
niyata-paurvāparya-bhāga-dvaya-rūpatvam uktam ।  
atra tu vākya-yōjanāyāṁ vyākhyānasya niyata-paurvāparya-bhāga-dvaya-rūpatayaikaśāstryam uktam ।  
ubhayatrōbhayam anusandhēyam ।  

**bhāga**-śabdābhyāṁ mīmāṁsā-dvayasya  
ēkāvayavitvaṁ sūcitam । 

**pūrvōparitana**-śabdābhyāṁ krama-niyama uktaḥ ।  

**karma-brahma**-śabdābhyāṁ vr̥tta-vartiṣyamāṇa-kathanam । 

**alpāsthira-phalatvānantasthira-phalatvābhyāṁ**  
tayōr hētu-hētumad-bhāvōpapādanam । 

mukty-upāyōpayōgitayā  
karmaṇāṁ sva-rūpēṇōpādēyatā-pratītir ananta-sthira-phalāpāta-pratīty-antarbhūtā ।  
ataḥ pr̥thag anuktiḥ  
ēvaṁ krama-viśēṣa-viśiṣṭaika-vyākhyēya-vyākhyāna-rūpatayā  
karma-brahma-mīmāṁsayōr aikaśāstryāt  
sūtrasya yathōkta ēvārtha ityarthaḥ । 

#### +6 jijñāsōtpatti-kramaḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
athātō brahmajijñāsā ॥ 1-1-1॥

**Thibaut**—
1. Then therefore the enquiry into Brahman.

##### 1 aikaśāstryam

**viśvāsa-ṭippanī**—
aikaśāstrya-sthāpana-prayōjanāni - 

- sūtra-vyākhyānam
- karmōpādēyatā-sthāpanam (advaiti-nibhās tyaktukāmāḥ)
- pūrva-mīmāṁsā-nyāya-sañcāraṇam agrē। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tad āha vr̥ttikāraḥ-  

>"vr̥ttāt karmādhigamād anantaraṁ  
brahma-vividiṣā"  

iti ।  
vakṣyati ca karma-brahma-mīmāṁsayōr aika-śāstryaṁ -

> "saṁhitam ētac chārīrakaṁ  
> jaiminīyēna ṣōḍaśa-lakṣaṇēna  
> +iti śāstraikatva-siddhiḥ"

+iti।  

**viśvāsa-ṭippanī**—
16-lakṣaṇaṁ jaiminīyam = karma-mīmāṁsā 12-lakṣaṇam + dēvatādhikaraṇam 4-lakṣaṇam।  
dēvatādhikaraṇaṁ kālē luptam,  
paścāt kāśakr̥tsna-kr̥taṁ tat-sthānam abhajata।  
tac cāpi luptam, kiñca tatra tatra +uddhriyatē। 

**Thibaut**—
The same meaning is expressed by the Vr̥ttikāra when saying 'after the comprehension of works has taken place there follows the enquiry into Brahman.' And that the enquiry into works and that into Brahman constitute one body of doctrine, he (the Vr̥ttikāra) will declare later on 'this Sārīraka-doctrine is connected with Jaimini's doctrine as contained in sixteen adhyāyas; this proves the two to constitute one body of doctrine.' 

**śruta-pradīpikā**—
tanmatānusārēṇēti pratijñāṁ vr̥ttigranthēna saṁvādayati - tadāhēti ।  

karmacintānantaryākṣēpakarmaikaśāstryaṁ ca vr̥ttau darśayati - vakṣyati cēti । lakṣaṇam adhyāyaḥ । saṁhitam ēkavyākhyēyavyākhyānarūpatayā sambaddhamiti bhāvaḥ । śārīrakaṁ brahmamīmāṁsā ; jagaccharīrakabrahmaviṣayatvāt । ṣōḍaśalakṣaṇēna ; ṣōḍaśādhyāyēna ।

**śruta-prakāśikā - vr̥ttikārālambanam**—
pūrva-pratijñātaṁ vr̥ttikāra-matānusāraṁ  
vr̥ttigranthēna saṁvādayati tadāhēti ।  

karmādhigamasyaiva pūrvavr̥ttatvaṁ  
na kēvalaṁ kaṇṭhōktam,  
aika-śāstryōkty-ākṣiptaś cēty abhiprayann āha - vakṣyaticēti । 

"vr̥ttād" ityādiḥ,  
"saṁhitam" ityādiś ca vr̥ttigranthau ।  

**śruta-prakāśikā - śārīrakaṁ 16-lakṣaṇam**—
**śārīrakaṁ** brahmamīmāṁsā ।  
jagac-charīra[ka]ḥ paramātmā **śārīraḥ** ।  
“tasyaiṣa ēva śārīra ātmā" iti śrutēḥ ।  

tad-viṣayaṁ śāstraṁ śārīrakam  
ity ucyatē ।  
**ṣōḍaśa-lakṣaṇēna** ṣōḍaśādhyāyēna । 

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
2 śārīrakam ।  
śārīraṁ kāyati pratipādayatīti śārīrakam ।  
kai gai śabdē ।  
'ātō'nupasargē kaḥ'  
iti kapratyayē gōda itivat siddhiḥ ।  
śārīram adhikr̥tya pravr̥ttaṁ śāstraṁ  
śārīrakam iti cānandamayādhikaraṇa-bhāṣyam ē tat-tātparyakam ।  

yadvā śārīramācaṣṭē iti nāma-dhātau kvipi  
kartrartha-ṇvul-antam ।  
śārīra-bhūta-paramātmākhyāna-karam ityarthaḥ । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - saṁhitam**—
**saṁhitam** iti ।  
niyata-paurvāparyaika-vyākhyēya-vyākhyāna-rūpatayā saṅgatam  
iti bhāvaḥ ।  
“arthaikatvād ēkaṁ vākyam"  
iti nyāyēna pradhāna-pratipādyaikyāt vyākhyēyasya vēdasyaikaprabandhatvaṁ bhavēt ।  
taccōpapadyatē - 
puruṣārthaparatvād vēdasya,  
brahmaparatvād vā;  
“sarvē vēdā yat padam ānanti”,  
“vēdaiśca sarvair aham ēva vēdyaḥ"  
iti hi śrutismr̥tī । 

vēdārtha-vicārasyānugatatvān  
mīmāṁsāyā ēka-prabandhatvam ।  
anēnaikaśāstryēṇa (gha)  
karmādhigamasya pūrvavr̥ttatvam ākṣiptam ॥ 

**śruta-prakāśikā - pratijñā-bhēdaḥ - 1**—
[[34]] 

> nanu yadi aikaśāstryaṁ karma-brahma-vicārayōḥ,  
tarhi +++(pūrvamīmāṁsābhāgasya)+++ upakramē sādhāraṇārthaḥ pratijñāyēta,  
'athātō vēdārthajijñāsē'ti ।  
na caivaṁ pratijñātam ।  
kintu pūrvabhāgāsādhāraṇa ēvaṁ pratijñātaḥ,  
'athātō dharmajijñāsē 'ti ॥ 

atra brūmaḥ – 

athātō brahmajijñāsēty ēvōbhaya-bhāga-sādhāraṇārtha-pratijñā ।+++(5)+++  
karmavicāras tu brahma-mīmāṁsā-tr̥tīya-lakṣaṇa-caturtha-pādē saṅgataḥ ।  

brahmavicārāntarbhāvē 'pi pr̥thakkaraṇam upapadyatē ;  
yathā nigrahāntarbhūta-cchala-jātyōr āhnika-bhēdēna pr̥thag uktiḥ (nyāyadarśanē),  
yathā ca nigrahāntarbhūta-hētv-ābhāsānām adhyāya-bhēdēna pr̥thag uktiḥ ।  

pr̥thak-karaṇaṁ ca bahu-granthapratipādyatvāt ।  

tatra [ca] pūrva-bhāvitvam upajīvyōpajīvakamācādi-vakṣyamāṇa-hētu-nibandhanam ।  
ētad uktaṁ bhavati -  
arthakramād brahmamīmāṁsā  
tr̥tīya-lakṣaṇa-caturtha-pādēna karma-vicāraḥ saṅgataḥ ।  
pratipatti-saukarya-lakṣaṇa-kramāttu  
karma-vicārasya pūrva-bhāva iti ॥+++(5)+++ 

**śruta-prakāśikā - pratijñābhēdaḥ - 2**—
ēvaṁ vā -  
sādharmya-vaidharmya-samayōr jātyōḥ kathanēna  
yathā pratidharma-samā +++(jātiḥ)+++ ubhayānuyāyinī artha-siddhā ।  
ēvaṁ bhāga-dvayāsādhāraṇārtha-pratijñā-dvayē kr̥tē  
sādhāraṇārtha-pratijñānam ārthaṁ syāt ।  
sādhāraṇārthē pratijñātē 'py 
asādhāraṇārthas tu pr̥thagēva pratijñātavyaḥ ।  
dharma-jijñāsāyāṁ pratijñātāyām api,  
"athātaḥ śēṣa-lakṣaṇam",  
"athātaḥ kratv-artha-puruṣārthayōr jijñāsā"  
ityādī hy asādhāraṇārtha-pratijñā kr̥tā ।  
atō bhāgadvayāsādhāraṇārtha-pratijñānēna  
tad-anugata-sādhāraṇārtha-pratijñānam ārthaṁ syād iti  
prathamam, 'athātō dharmajijñāsē'ti pratijñātam ;  
na tu vēdārthajijñāsēti ॥ 

**śruta-prakāśikā - pratijñābhēdaḥ - 3**—
athavā -athātō dharmajijñāsēty ēva sādhāraṇa-pratijñā ।  
alaukika-śrēyaḥ-sādhanaṁ hi dharmaḥ ;  
tad-anuyāyi pratipādyam ।  
dharmaśca sādhya-siddha-bhēdēna dvividhaḥ ।  
siddharūpē vastuni dharma-śabda-prayōgō  
mahābhāratē dr̥ṣṭaḥ ।  
yathā, 

> "yē ca vēdavidō viprā  
yē cādhyātma-vidō janāḥ ।  
tē **vadanti** mahātmānaṁ  
kr̥ṣṇaṁ dharmaṁ sanātanam" 

iti । 

tathā'bhiyuktaiś ca  
alaukikatvē sati śrēyaḥsādhanatvaṁ dharma-śabda-pravr̥tti-nimittaṁ manvānaiḥ  
siddha-rūpē'rthē dharmaśabdaḥ prayuktaḥ,  

> "dravya-kriyā-guṇādīnāṁ  
dharmatvaṁ sthāpayiṣyatē ।  
tēṣām aindriyakatvē'pi  
na tādrūpyēṇa dharmatā" 

ityādau ।  
tatra dravyādi-sad-bhāvē'pi  
kriyā-prādhānyāt sādhya-dharma-paraḥ pūrvabhāgaḥ ;  
upāsana--tad-aṅga--sad-bhāvē 'pi  
brahma-pradhānatvāt siddha-dharmapara ūrdhva-bhāgaḥ ।  
ata ubhaya-bhāga-vicāra-sādhāraṇī prathamap-ratijñā ।  

tatra dharma-śabdasya sādhya-dharma-viṣayatayā prasiddhi-prācuryēṇa buddhi-sthatvāt,  
pūrva-bhāga-pratipannatvēna prāthamyāt,  
dharma-jijñāsāpadēnaiva  
tantrēṇa vā arthatō vā  
pratijñātatvōpapattēś ca  
tal-lakṣaṇam uktaṁ cōdanāsūtrē । 

siddha-rūpa-dharma-viśēṣasya ca  
sādhāraṇa-pratijñayaiva  
arthataḥ pratijñātatvēpi  
tasya bahu-grantha-vyavadhānāt,  
2 śabdābōdhyatvaśaṅkā parijihīrṣayā ca punaḥ pratijñā kr̥tā;  
tasya lakṣaṇam uktaṁ janmādi-sūtrē - - iti yuktamaikaśāstryam ।  

(2 śabdābōdhyatvaśaṅkā siddhē vyutpatty-abhāva-bhrāntimūlā । )

**śruta-prakāśikā - dharma-jijñāsā - karma-prādhānyē'py avirōdhaḥ**—
> nanu pūrvabhāgasya sādhya-dharma-pradhānatōktir  
udāhr̥ta-vacanēna +++("yē ca vēdavidō viprā …")+++ virudhyatē -  
tatra +++(vacanē)+++ pūrvabhāgē +++(←"vēdavidō viprā")+++ 'pi siddha-rūpasya parasya  
karmārādhyatayā pradhāna-pratipādyatvāvagamāt ।  
tasmin vacanē "vēda-vic"-chabdō hi  
pūrva-bhāgābhijña-paraḥ,  
gō-balīvarda-nyāyāt ;  
> 
> > "viṣṇu-nāmā sa vēdēṣu  
vēdāntēṣu ca gīyatē" 
> 
> ity anēnaikārthyācca ।  
> 
> na ca "guṇabhāvēna karmaṇaḥ (nāṁ) pratipādyatvam"  
ity avirōdhaḥ ;  
prādhānyēna pratipādyatvasya jaiminēr abhimatatvāt, bhavadbhirapi tathōktatvācca । 

satyam । vastutaḥ prādhānyaṁ paramātmana ēva ;  
yathā rājñastātparyagōcaratvalakṣaṇam ।  
śābdaṁ prādhānyaṁ tu karmaṇa ēva;  
yathā rājapuruṣasya ।+++(5)+++  
taccātiraskr̥tam -  
tatra tasya paramātmārādhana-rūpatvāvagamāt ।  
na ca tad-avagamō'vaśyaṁ sampādyaḥ ।  
antavat-svargādi-phala-pradatvē  
karmaṇāṁ paradēvatā-jñāna-nairapēkṣyaṁ hi  
śruti-smr̥tibhyām avagamyatē ।  

> "yō ha vā ētad akṣaraṁ gārgi !  
> aviditvā'smilm̐ lōkē juhōti, yajatē, tapastapyatē bahūni varṣasahasrāṇi,  
> antavad ēvāsya tadbhavati" 

iti,  

> "ahaṁ hi sarvayajñānāṁ bhōktā ca prabhurēva ca ।  
> na tu māmabhijānanti takhēnātaśvyayanti tē" 

iti ca । 

atas tan-nairapēkṣya-lakṣaṇam api prādhānyam asti karmaṇaḥ ।  

ataḥ pūrvabhāgē karmaṇaḥ prāg-avagataṁ prādhānyaṁ  
paścād-avagantavya-paramātmārādhana-rūpatvaṁ cāviruddham ।  
ataḥ pratijñōpapattēḥ śāstraikyaṁ yuktam । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - pūrva-kalpita-taḍāgavat**—
[[25]]  

yady api karmabrahmamīmāṁsayōr aikaśāstryam  
avivakṣitaṁ jaimininā -  
tathāpi tadaṅgīkr̥tya  
tad-ēkaśāstratayā bādarāyaṇēna brahmasūtra-praṇayanaṁ yuktam,  
yataḥ 1 

> "a-tad-arthatayā klr̥ptam  
api yōgyam apēkṣitam ।  
tādarthyam arhati - +++(nūtana-)+++grāmē  
kalpyē pūrva-taṭākavat " । 

vivakṣitatva-sambhavaśca darśitaḥ ।  
ataḥ (taśca ) śastraikyaṁ yuktam । 

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
1 atadarthatayāklr̥ptāmati । na taditi samāsaḥ ।  
tadatiriktakāryārthatayaiva klr̥ptamityarthaḥ ।  
anyadīyaślōka iha svavākya-cchāyayā'nūditaḥ ।  

ataḥ "yata" ityasya tādarthyam arhatītyatrānvayaḥ ।  
vivakṣitatvaṁ sambhavaścēti pāṭhē  
dharmajijñāsāsūtrasya sādhāraṇatayā vyākhyānāt vivakṣitatvamuktam । 

karma-brahma-jñānayōḥ sāpēkṣatvaṁ vyākhyēyaikyādi ca  
śāstraikya-sambhavōpapādakam uktam ityarthaḥ । 

kiñca pūrva-mīmāṁsā-grathānārūḍha-jaiminy-uktārtha-prasaṅgēṣu  
sarvatra bādarāyaṇō jaimini-nāmnā nirdiśati ।  
tatra kiñcit svānabhimatam api ;  
jaimininā'pi vimarśāyōpasthāpita-mātram api bhavēt ।+++(4)+++  

nirvivādaṁ sat pūrvamīmāṁsōktaṁ tu,  
tad-uktam iti vākyēna darśayati ।  
tat aikagranthyābhiprāyēṇaiva ।  

ata ēva śāṅkara-bhāṣyādau apaśūdrādhikaraṇa-śarīri-bhāvādhikaraṇādau  
paunar-uktya-śaṅkā-parihāra-pravr̥ttir upapadyata  
ityādi draṣṭavyam ।  

śāstraikya-sambhavasyōpari vistarēṇōpapādanād  
atra vivakṣitatva-sambhava iti pāṭha ēva śrēyān । 

**viśvāsa-ṭippanī - kāraṇāntarāṇi**—
svādhyāyō'dhyētavya ity akhilō'pi vēdō gr̥hītaḥ,  
tathā lakṣyaikyē sati,  
tad-upakāraka-nyāya-sūtraikyam api sidhyati। 

> aikaśāstryē sati,  
> apaśūdrādhikaraṇaṁ, smr̥tyadhikaraṇaṁ ca kutaḥ punar uktaṁ?

pūrva-pakṣa-bhēdāt।  

**vi॰pra॰**—
ataḥ pratipipādayiṣitārtha-bhēdēna,  
+++(pūrva-mīmāṁsāyāṁ viṣaya-gata+adhyyāya-)+++ṣaṭka-bhēdavad,  
+++(tatraiva)+++ adhyāya-bhēdavac ca  
pūrvōttara-mīmāṁsayōr bhēdaḥ।

**Thibaut**—
Hence the earlier and the later Mīmāṁsā are separate only in so far as there is a difference of matter to be taught by each; in the same way as the two halves of the Pūrva Mīmāṁsā-sūtras, consisting of six adhyāyas each, are separate [#fn_1]; and as each adhyāya is separate.  

[#fn_1]: 5:1 The first six books of the Pūrva Mīmāṁsā-sūtras give rules for the fundamental forms of the sacrifice; while the last six books teach how these rules are to be applied to the so-called modified forms.

**śruta-pradīpikā**—
śāstraikyapratyanīkamarthavirōdhaṁ pratipādyabhēdaṁ prayōjanabhēdaṁ kartr̥bhēdaṁ cāśaṅkyāha - ata iti । ataḥ; ēkavyākhyēyavyākhyānarūpatayā prabandhaikyasiddhēḥ । pratipipādayiṣitaḥ ; pratipādayitumiṣṭaḥ, tātparyaviṣaya ityarthaḥ । dēvatānirākaraṇādikaṁ dēvatājñānānapēkṣaphalapradatvarūpakarmaprāśastyādyarthāntaraparam ; na tu dēvatānirāsādau tātparyam । anyārthaṁ tu jaiminiḥ paraṁ jaiminirmukhyatvāt ityādau jaiminērbrahmābhyupagamadarśanāditi bhāvaḥ । dravyadēvatāsāmānyē dravyabalīyastvamapi pramāṇadvārā, na svarūpataḥ । dravyasvarūpaṁ hi pratyakṣaṁ havissvarūpaṁ, dharma ēva hi śāstragamyaḥ, dēvatāyāstu svarūpaṁ phalapradatvamapi śāstraikagamyamityādyanusandhēyam । atō viruddhārthē tātparyābhāvānnārthavirōdhaḥ । pūrvōttarakāṇḍābhiprāyēṇa ṣaṭkabhēdavadadhyāyabhēdavadi tyuktam । anēna prayōjanapratipādyabhēdau parihr̥tau । ṣaṭkadvayacintitaprakr̥tivikr̥tirūpārthatatphalabhēdasya śāstrabhēdakatvābhāvāt । kartr̥bhēdaparihārastu sphuṭatayā nōktaḥ । asti hi vaiyākaraṇapūrvōttaravr̥ttyādau kartr̥bhēdaḥ । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - ṣaṭka-bhēdaḥ**—
> nanv idam ayuktam aikaśāstryaṁ  
śārīraka-śabda-sūcitāt pradhāna-pratipādya-bhēdāt,  
jaiminīya-śabda-sūcitāt kartr̥-bhēdāt,  
tad-ubhaya-phalitāt prayōjanam-ēbhēdāt,  
arthavirōdhāc ca

ity āśaṅkāṁ pariharati ataḥ pratipipādayiṣitēti ।  
ataḥ vr̥ttikārōktāt ēka-vyākhyēya-vyākhyāna-rūpa [tva] sambandhādityarthaḥ । 

ṣaṭkabhēdaḥ pūrvamīmāṁsāyām, adhyāya-bhēdas tatrōttaratra ca nidarśanārthamuktau ।  
arthabhēdābhāvē  
hyēkaṁ ṣaṭkamēkō'dhyāyō vā syāt ।  
ata ēkāvayavitvē siddhē sati  
avāntarārthabhēdō na mahāvākyaikatva-virōdhī,  
yathā padārtha-bhēdō vākyārthakatvāvirōdhīti bhāvaḥ ।  
anēna pratipādyabhēdaḥ parihr̥taḥ ।  

prayōjana-bhēdaś cārthāt parihr̥taḥ  
ṣaṭkadvaya-cintita-prakr̥ti-vikr̥ti-prayōjana-bhēdasya śāstra-bhēdakatvābhāvāt ।  

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
2 prakr̥tivikr̥tīti । upadēśaṣaṭkamati dēśaṣaṭkamityapi vyavahāraḥ prasiddhaḥ ।  
adhyāya bhēdahētus tudvādaśānāmadhyāyānām - 

> 'mānaṁ bhēdaḥ śēṣabhāvaḥ prayuktiḥ paurvāparyañcādhikārō'tidēśaḥ । sāmānyēnāthō viśēṣātidēśa ūhō bādhastantramēvaṁ prasaṅgaḥ' 

ityarthabhēdō 'smābhir api darśitaḥ ।  

upari caturadhyāyī saṅkarṣakāṇḍaḥ । tadarthabhēdaś cādhikaraṇa-cintāmaṇau, 

> "tata upari caturlakṣaṇī dēvatārthā" 

ityadhikaraṇasārāvali-vivaraṇāvasarē, 

> "svarūpamādau tadbhēdastadupāsanapūrvakam । phalanna dēvatākāṇḍē dēvatānāṁ tu kathyatē" 

iti dēvatāsvarūpa-tadbhēdatadupāsana-tatphalarūpēṇa darśitaḥ । 

tad idam atra kāśakr̥tsnīya-saṅkarṣakāṇḍaika-saṅgrahapakṣē ।  

yadā tu jaiminīya ēva saṅkarṣakāṇḍaś caturadhyāyī gr̥hyatē;  
kāśakr̥tsnīyastu jaiminy-ukti-viśadānavagamya-dēvatā-viśōdhana-pravr̥ttaḥ, tac-chēṣaḥ syād  
iti tadā tasya dvādaśādhyāya-yuktārthēṣu kēṣāñcid asphuṭānām ākr̥ṣya saṅkalayya  
vicārarūpatvāt tatra hōma-pāda--yūpa-pāda--iṣṭakā-pāda--  
avadāna-pāda--varaṇa-pādētyādi-  
pāda-nāma-nirdēśāc cānyādr̥śa ēvārtha-bhēdō bhāvya ity alam ।  
vistaraḥ paramārthabhūṣaṇē । 

**vi॰pra॰**—
mīmāṁsāśāstram -  
"athātō dharmajijñāsā" (pūrva.mī.1.1.1) ity ārabhya  
"anāvr̥ttiś śabdād, anāvr̥ttiś śabdāt" (bra.sū.4.4.22.) ity ēvam-antaṁ  
+++(sūtrēṣu)+++ saṅgati-viśēṣēṇa viśiṣṭa-kramam । 

**Thibaut**—
The entire Mīmāṁsā-sātra – which begins with the Sūtra 'Now therefore the enquiry into religious duty' and concludes with the Sūtra '(From there is) no return on account of scriptural statement'--has, owing to the special character of the contents, a definite order of internal succession. 

**śruta-pradīpikā**—
astvaikaśāstryam ; brahma-cintā pūrvaṁ kiṁ na syādityatrāha - mīmāṁsēti । saṅgativiśēṣāḥ vakṣyamāṇāḥ - pāṭhakramaḥ, cētanānāṁ trivargē prathamaṁ prāvaṇyarūpō'rthakramaḥ, padārthavākyārthabhāvaḥ, dr̥ṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikabhāvaḥ, upajīvyōpajīvakabhāvaśca । ēvaṁ paurvāparyaniyāmakasaṅgativiśēṣēṇa viśiṣṭakramaṁ kramaviśēṣavadityarthaḥ ।

##### 2 adhyayanam

###### vidhiḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
tathā hi  
prathamaṁ tāvat 

> svādhyāyō'dhyētavyaḥ (yajur-āraṇyakē.2.pra. 15.anu.) 

ity +++(uccāraṇānūccāraṇa-rūpēṇa)+++ adhyayanēnaiva  
svādhyāya-śabda-vācya-+++(sva-śākhāgata-)+++vēdākhyākṣara-rāśēr grahaṇaṁ vidhīyatē   
+++(na tad arthaparyantam - rāgatas tat prāptam iti)+++॥

**English**—
This is as follows.  
At first the precept  

> 'one is to learn one's own text (svādhyāya)' 

enjoins the apprehension of that aggregate of syllables which is called 'Veda,'  
and is here referred to as 'svādhyāya.'  

**śruta-pradīpikā - tathā hi**—
aikaśāstryakarma-vicāra--tad-anantara-bhāvi--brahma-vicārāpēkṣōpayōgitvēna  
adhīta-sāṅga-saśiraska iti prāk pratijñāta-sāṅga-kr̥tsna-vēdādhyayana-kartavyatāyāṁ  
pramāṇatayā svādhyāya-vidhim upanyasyan  
tasyārtha-jñāna-paryantatva-nimittāṁ brahma-vicārānārambha-śaṅkāṁ  
vādi-vipratipatti-nimitta-saṁśayaṁ ca vyudasyati - **tathāhīti** ।  

vidhērakṣaragrahaṇaparyantatvē siddhē hyārambhaṇīyatvasiddhiḥ । anyathā adhītya snāyāt ityarthajñānē karmaśēṣatayā viniyuktē satyavahantavyavrīhivat jñātavyātmanō'pi karmaśēṣatvāt ayamātmā brahma ityātmabrahmaśabdayōstulyārthatvācca karmasu kartr̥tayāvaklr̥ptajīvasvarūpaparā vēdāntā iti tadatiriktāprāmāṇikēśvaravicārarūpaśāstrasyānārambhaṇīyatāpattēḥ ।

**śruta-pradīpikā - prathamam**—
tatra bhāṭṭābhimatāṁścaturō'rthān gurukumārilānabhimatamēkaṁ ca saṅgrahēṇa pratijānītē - **prathamam** iti ।  
prathamaṁ tāvat ; prathamata ēva । prāthamyōktyā śāstrāntarēṇa sādhanacatuṣṭayasiddhyayōgaḥ phalitaḥ । śāstrāntarādhigamāyōgyadaśāpēkṣayā prāthamyam ; garbhāṣṭamōpanītasya hyadhyayanam । ata ēva aṣṭavarṣam ityuktakālaviśēṣō'pyupanayanadvārādhyayanāṅgamiti phalitam । anēnōpanayanasyādhyayanāṅgatvaṁ, svādhyāyavidhivākyōpādānēnādhyayanasya svavidhiprayuktatvam, adhyayanēna iti nirdēśēna saṁskāravidhitvam, ēvakārēṇa niyamavidhitvaṁ ca dyōtyatē । akṣararāśimātrasya svādhyāyaśabdavācyatvavyudāsāya vēdākhya śabdaḥ । vēdākhyētyanēna kr̥tsnādhyayanasya vihitatvamapyabhiprētam । na hi vēdaikadēśaḥ svādhyāyaśabdārthaḥ । nāsāvarthāvabōdhanaparyantō vidhirityabhiprāyēṇa akṣararāśigrahaṇamityuktam । vidhērakṣaragrahaṇaparyantatayā adhītyābhisamāvr̥tya adhītya snāyāt ityatrārthajñānasya karmaśēṣatvābhāvēna jñātavyātmanō'vahantavyavrīhyādivat karmaśēṣatvābhāvēna karmasu karturjīvādanyasminpramāṇasambhāvanayā tadvilakṣaṇēśvaravicārarūpaśāstramārambhaṇīyam iti phalitamityabhiprāyaḥ ।

###### niyamāḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
tac cādhyayanaṁ kiṁrūpaṁ kathaṁ ca kartavyam ity apēkṣāyām  

**English**—
Next there arises the desire to know of what nature the 'Learning' enjoined is to be, and how it is to be done. 

**śruta-pradīpikā - tacca**—
ayaṁ cārthaḥ adhyayanamātravataḥ iti vakṣyamāṇasūtrārthaḥ pratipattisaukaryāyātra darśitaḥ ; prāthamyaṁ sāṅgatvaṁ ca nātra pratītam ; adhyāpanavidhiśravaṇāt ; tatprayuktatā ca pratīyata iti śaṅkāyāmāha - taccēti । caḥ śaṅkānivr̥ttau । 

**śruta-pradīpikā - kiṁrūpam**—
kiṁ-rūpam?  
svatantrōccāraṇa-rūpaṁ paratantrōccāraṇa-rūpaṁ vā,  
sakr̥d-ukti-rūpam, a-sakr̥d-uktirūpaṁ vēty-arthaḥ ।  
katham ?  
kim-aṅgakam ?

**vi॰pra॰**—
> aṣṭavarṣaṁ brāhmaṇam upanayīta, tam adhyāpayēt +++(←ajñāta-śruti-srōtaḥ - sūtrēṣu tu vartatē)+++ 

ity anēna,

**English**—
Here there come in certain injunctions such as

> 'Let a Brahnmana be initiated in his eighth year' 

and

> 'The teacher is to make him recite the Veda';

**śruta-pradīpikā - māṇavaka-śēṣatvam**—
aṣṭavarṣatvamupanayanadvārā adhyayanaśēṣam ।  
"dvādaśāhēna prajākāmaṁ yājayēt" itivad adhyayanaśrutiḥ ।  
na hi tatra yajanaṁ yājanavidhiprayuktam ।  
atra "brāhmaṇam" iti dvitīyāśrutyā  
māṇavaka-śēṣam upanayanam  
antaraṅgatva-liṅgāt tad-gatādhyayanāṅgam ।  

**śruta-pradīpikā - upanīya**—
"upanīya" iti ktvāśrutistu vilambadvayahatā ;  
sā hi smr̥tir anuvādarūpā ca ।  
ataḥ śrutērliṅgaṁ prabalam । 

**śruta-pradīpikā - "kartrabhiprāyē kriyāphalē" na**—
na ca 

> kartrabhiprāya-phalātmanēpada-vaśād  
upanayanam upanētr̥-gatādhyāpanāṅgam 

iti vācyam,  
akartrabhiprāyārthēna "sammānana…"-ityādi-sūtrēṇātmanēpadasya vihitatvāt ।  

**śruta-pradīpikā - "sammānana…"-ityādinā nāvadhāraṇa-rūpa-niyama-niṣēdhaḥ**—
> "kartary **ēva** phalānvayaḥ kartrabhiprāyatvam"  
> iti +++("sammānana…"-ityādi-sūtrēṇa)+++ tan-nivr̥ttau phalasyōbhayānvaya-sambhavēna  
> +upanayana-phalasya guru-gatatva-sambhavād  
> adhyāpanāṅgatvam 

iti śaṅkā ca nirastā,  
"agnīnādadhīta" ityatra svarita-ityādisūtrēṇa vihitē'py ātmanēpadē  
phalasyōbhayānvaya-darśanāt ।  

ataḥ kartrabhiprāyatvaṁ na kartaryēva phalānvayaḥ ;  
kintu phalasya kartr-anvaya-mātram  
iti tan-nivr̥ttau  
kartari phalānvayō na sidhyēd  
iti nācāryē phalānvayaḥ । 

na ca cētana-dvayānanvayaḥ kartr-abhiprāyatvam  
"r̥tvijō vr̥ṇītē" ityatra phalasyōbhayatrānvayāt ।

**śruta-pradīpikā - avyavahitaphalānvayō na**—
na ca

> avyavahita-phalasya kartranvayaḥ kartr-abhiprāyatvam  
ity ācāryaka-vyavahitatvād ātmanē-padāprāptau  
sammānana-ityādi-sūtrēṇa vyavahita-phalasya kartranvayē 'py ātmanēpadaṁ vidhīyata  
iti vyavahitācāryaka-niṣpatty-arthatayōpanayanasyādhyāpanāṅgatvaṁ kartrabhiprāyatvavirōdhi 

iti vācyam,  
uttara-kratu-vidhīn praty ādhānasyēva  
+adhyāpanaṁ praty-aṅgatvābhāvē 'py  
upanayanasya tad-upakārakatva-mātrēṇa  
+ācāryaka-niṣpādakatvōpapattēḥ ।  
ata upanayanaphalaṁ nācāryānvayīti na tadadhyāpanāṅgam ।

**śruta-prakāśikā - "kartr-abhiprāyē kriyāphalē" iti na**—
kiñca "svarita-ñitaḥ kartr-abhiprāyē kriyāphalē" ity ātmanēpadē prāptē'pi,  
"sammānanōtsañjanācārya-karaṇa--jñāna-bhr̥ti-vigaṇana-vyayēṣu niyaḥ" iti punar-vidhānasyākartr-abhiprāyārthatvād  
upanayanasya nādhyāpanāṅgatvaṁ yuktam ।  
"akartrabhiprāyārthō'yam ārambhaḥ" iti hi tad-vr̥tti-kāraḥ +++(←kāśikāyām)+++। 
। 

**vīrarāghavaḥ**—
1 +++("sammānanōtsañjanācārya-karaṇa…" ityatra)+++ ācāryakaraṇēti । svam ācāryaṁ karōtīti yat tat ācārya-karaṇam ।  
nāyaṁ niyō vācyārthaḥ; apitu paścād-gamyaḥ ।  
ētad-dhētuḥ māṇavakasya sva-samīpa-prāpaṇaṁ vācyārthaḥ ।  
tat-phalam adhyayanaṁ māṇavaka-niṣṭham ।  
tasmin niṣpannē ācāryatva-siddhir iti  
tat-siddhi-hētutva-mukhēna samīpa-prāpaṇam upalakṣyatē ।

**śruta-prakāśikā - punar-vidhānē nāvadhāraṇa-niyamaḥ**—

> nanu kartr-abhiprāyatvaṁ = kartary **ēva** phalasyābhiprētatvam ।

ataḥ phalam ubhayānvayi ।  
atō māṇavaka-dvārēṇācāryānvayy-upanayana-phalam  
iti adhyāpanāṅgatvaṁ yuktam

kartr-abhiprāyatva-mātrasya niṣēdhārthatvāt ।  
atō nādhyāpanāṅgatvam ॥

ādadhītēty atra  
dhāñ-dhātōḥ ñittvāt ātmanēpadam ।  
tatra phalasya agni-puruṣōbhayānvayitayā  
na kartr̥-mātrābhiprāyatva-rūpatva-sambhavaḥ ।

phalasya kartr̥-vyatirikta-cētanānvaya-darśanēna

ataḥ kartr-abhiprāya-mātra-niṣēdhārthaṁ punar-vidhānam  
iti nādhyāpanāṅgam upanayanam ॥ 

**śruta-prakāśikā - punar-vidhānē na vyavahita-phala-sambandha-kalpanam**—
> nanu kriyā-phalaṁ nāma kriyānantara-bhāvi-phalam ।  
tasya kartary anvitatvaṁ kartr-abhiprāyatvam ।  
ata +++(prathamōpākarma-pratīkṣasya śikṣaṇasya=)+++ācāryakasyōpanayana-kriyānantara-bhāvitvābhāvād

a-vyavahita-phalasyākartr-abhiprāyatvē 'py ātmanē-padaṁ  
sammānanētyādi-sūtrēṇa vidhīyatē ।  
atō 'kartr-abhiprāyārthatvē'pi  
vyavahitācāryaka-niṣpatty-arthatayā  
'dhyāpanāṅgatvam upanayanasyāviruddham 

iti cēt — naivam;  
"agnīn ādadhītē"ty-atra svaritēti-sūtra-vihitē 'py ātmanē-padē  
agni-saṁskāra+++(←karma-mantrādibhir)+++-vyavahitasyā''hitāgnitvāpatti-rūpa-phalasya kartr-anvayitva-darśanāt ।  
atō'kartr-abhiprāyārthaṁ sammānanētyādi-sūtraṁ  
phala-mātrasya kartr-anvaya-nivāraṇārtham ॥  

**śruta-prakāśikā - kartr-abhimata-phalaṁ bhinnam**—
> saṁskāra-viśiṣṭāgniḥ phalam +++(na tv āhitāgnitā)+++  
ity ādhāna-kartari  
na vyavahita-phalānvaya

iti cēt —  
tarhy upanayana-saṁskāra-viśiṣṭa-māṇavaka-siddhir ēvāvyavahitaṁ phalam  
iti kartrabhiprāya-sūtrēṇaivātmanē-pada-siddhēr  
akartrabhiprāya-sūtra-vaiyarthyaṁ syāt ॥

> yady ēvaṁ vyavahitam avyavahitaṁ vā phala-mātraṁ kartrabhiprāya-sūtrēṇa nivāryatē,  
tarhy upanētuḥ pravr̥ttir nōpapadyatē ;  
yataḥ "prayōjanam anuddiśya na mandōpi pravartatē" iti ॥ 

naivam ।  
upanayana-phalasya māṇavakānvayitvē 'py  
"ācāryāya varō dēya" iti vidhy-antara-prāpta-dakṣiṇā-phala-lipsayā pravr̥tty-upapattēḥ ।  
na caitēnākartrabhiprāyatva-virōdhaḥ;  
a-sādhāraṇa-phalānanvaya-viṣayatvād a-kartr-abhiprāya-sūtrasya ॥ 

> a-vyavahita-kriyā-phalasya kartur abhimatatvaṁ kartr-abhiprāyatvam,  
tad-anabhimatatvam a-kartr-abhiprāyatvam  

ity apy ayuktam ;  
kriyā-phalasya kartr-anabhimatatva-vyāghātāt  
+++(nāma - )+++ ācāryaka-niṣpatty-upayōginō māṇavaka-saṁskārasya  
+acāryānabhimatatvānupapattēḥ +++(yēna svaritētyādi-sūtrata ēvātmanēpaditā syāt)+++। 

ataḥ upanayanam adhyēṣyamāṇa-māṇavakāsatti+++(=sānnidhya)+++-mukhēna nādhyāpanāṅgam ;  
api tv adhyayanāṅgam ēva । 

**śruta-prakāśikā - adhyayana-vidhi-prādhānyam**—
adhyayanaṁ ca nādhyāpanavidhiḥ prayuṅktē +++(- api tv adhyētā 'dhyāpakam anviṣyati)+++।  
adhyāpayēd iti tu "dvādaśāhēna prajā-kāmaṁ yājayēd" ityādivad ity uktam ।  
yady api prajā-kāmam annādy-a-kāmam itivat  
tat-prayōjya-vyāpārasyādhyayanasyādhikāri-viśēṣaṇaṁ phalaṁ na śrūyatē—  
tathāpi svādhyāya-siddhir adhikāri-viśēṣaṇaṁ syāt ;  
"svādhyāyō'dhyētavyaḥ" iti svādhyāyasyādhyayana sādhyatvāvagamāt ।  
yathā agnīn ādadhītēty-atrāgnīnām ādhāna-sādhyatvāvagamād  
agni-siddhir adhikāri-viśēṣaṇam, tadvat ।

na ca sva-vidhi-prayuktatvē 'dhyayana-vidhēr anuṣṭhātr-abhāvaḥ ।  
santi hi prabuddhādhyētāraḥ ।  
tathā''ha bhagavān āpastambaḥ,  
"tasminn abhijana-vidyā-samudētaṁ samāhitaṁ saṁskartāram īpsēt" iti ।  
tēṣu para-vidhi-prayuktatvē sati  
adhyayanaṁ nōpapadyatē ।  

a-prabuddha-viṣayē tu  
sva-tantrasyādhyayana-vidhēr  
māṇavaka-viṣayatvaṁ jñātvā  
hitaiṣiṇō māṇavakam adhyayanādi kārayanti ।  
ataḥ prabuddhēṣv aprabuddhēṣu ca  
svavidhiprayuktatvam adhyanayasya yuktam ।+++(5)+++  

para-vidhi-prayuktatvē nityasyādhyayanasya kāmya-vidhi-prayuktatvaṁ syāt ।  
tataś cānuṣṭhāna-niyamō na syāt ।  

ācāryaka-kāmō hy adhyāpakaḥ +++(nādhyayanakāmaḥ)+++ ।  
tasyācāryaka-kāmanāyā abhāvē  
'dhyayanāsiddhēḥ ॥ 

adhyāpaka bāhulyāt tat-siddhiriti cēt — na;  
adhyāpakēbhyō 'py adhyētr̥-bāhulya-darśanāt । 

[[32]] 
ādhānasyōttara-kratu-vidhi-prayuktatvē'pi  
na kāmya-vidhi-mātra-prayuktatvam ;  
"vasantē vasantē jyōtiṣā yajēta",  
"yāvajjīvamagnihōtraṁ juhōti"  
iti nitya-vidhi-sadbhāvād  
ity ēvamādi anusandhēyam ।  
atō yathōkta ēvārthaḥ ॥ 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> śrāvaṇyāṁ prauṣṭhapadyāṁ vā  
upākr̥tya yathā-vidhi।  
yuktaś chandāṁsy adhīyīta  
māsān viprō 'rdhapañcamān॥  
(manusmr̥.4.65)

ity-ādi-vrata-niyama-viśēṣōpadēśaiś  
cāpēkṣitāni vidhīyantē॥

**English**—
and certain rules about special observances and restrictions--  
such as 

> 'having performed the upākarman on the full moon of Śravaṇa or Praushṭḥapada according to prescription,  
> he is to study the sacred verses for four months and a half--  
> which enjoin all the required details.

###### svarūpam
**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvaṁ sat-santāna-prasūta--  
sadācāra-niṣṭha-  
+ātma-guṇōpēta-  
vēda-vid-ācāryōpanītasya  
vrata-niyama-viśēṣa-yuktasya  
ācāryōccāraṇānūccāraṇa-rūpam  
akṣara-rāśi-grahaṇa-phalam  
**adhyayanam** ity avagamyatē॥+++(5)+++

**English**—
From all these it is understood that the study enjoined has for its result the apprehension of the aggregate of syllables called Veda, on the part of a pupil who has been initiated by a teacher sprung from a good family, leading a virtuous life, and possessing purity of soul; who practises certain special observances and restrictions; and who learns by repeating what is recited by the teacher.

###### saṁskāratā
**vi॰pra॰**—
adhyayanaṁ ca svādhyāya+++(-pāṭha)+++-saṁskāraḥ,  

> svādhyāyō'dhyētavyaḥ (yajurāraṇyakē.2.pra.15.anu.) 

iti svādhyāyasya +++(adhyayana-kriyāyāṁ)+++ karmatvāvagamāt। 

**English**—
And this study of the Veda is of the nature of a saṁskāra of the text,  
since the form of the injunction 'the Veda is to be studied' shows that the Veda is the object (of the action of studying). 

**vi॰pra॰**—
saṁskārō hi nāma kāryāntara-yōgyatā-karaṇam। +++(4)+++

**English**—
By a saṁskāra is understood an action whereby something is fitted to produce some other effect; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
saṁskāryatvaṁ ca svādhyāyasya yuktam,  
dharmārtha-kāma-mōkṣa-rūpa-- puruṣārtha-catuṣṭaya-- tat-sādhanāvabōdhitvāt,  
japādinā svarūpēṇāpi tat-sādhanatvāc ca।

**English**—
and that the Veda should be the object of such a saṁskaāra is quite appropriate, since it gives rise to the knowledge of the four chief ends of human action – viz. religious duty, wealth, pleasure, and final release – and of the means to effect them; and since it helps to effect those ends by itself also, viz. by mere mechanical repetition (apart from any knowledge to which it may give rise).

**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvam adhyayana-vidhir  
mantravan-niyamavad--akṣara-rāśi-grahaṇa-mātrē paryavasyati।

**English**—
The injunction as to the study of the Veda thus aims only at the apprehension of the aggregate of syllables (constituting the Veda) according to certain rules; it is in this way analogous to the recital of mantras.

##### 3 svatō mīmāṁsā-śravaṇam

**vi॰pra॰**—
adhyayana-gr̥hītasya svādhyāyasya  
svabhāvata ēva prayōjanavad-arthāvabōdhitva-darśanāt,  
gr̥hītāt svādhyāyād avagamyamānān prayōjanavatō 'rthān āpātatō dr̥ṣṭvā  
tat--sva-rūpa--prakāra-viśēṣa-- nirṇaya-phala-- vēda-vākya-vicāra-rūpa-- mīmāṁsā-śravaṇē  
adhīta-vēdaḥ puraṣas svayam ēva pravartatē। 

**English**—
It is further observed that the Veda thus apprehended through reading spontaneously gives rise to the ideas of certain things subserving certain purposes. A person, therefore, who has formed notions of those things immediately, i.e. on the mere apprehension of the text of the Veda through reading, thereupon naturally applies himself to the study of the Mimāṁsa, which consists in a methodical discussion of the sentences constituting the text of the Veda, and has for its result the accurate determination of the nature of those things and their different modes. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tatra karma-vidhi--sva-rūpē nirūpitē  
karmaṇām alpāsthira-phalatvaṁ dr̥ṣṭvā  
adhyayana-gr̥hīta-svādhyāyaika-dēśōpaniṣad-vākyēṣu ca  
a-mr̥tatva--rūpānanta-sthira-phalāpāta-pratītēḥ  
tan-nirṇaya-phala-- vēdānta-vākya--vicāra-rūpa-- śārīraka-mīmāṁsāyām adhikarōti।

**English**—
Through this study the student ascertains the character of the injunctions of work which form part of the Veda, and observes that all work leads only to non-permanent results; and as, on the other hand, he immediately becomes aware that the Upanishad sections – which form part of the Veda which he has apprehended through reading – refer to an infinite and permanent result, viz. immortality, he applies himself to the study of the Sārīraka-Mīmāṁsā, which consists in a systematic discussion of the Vedānta-texts, and has for its result the accurate determination of their sense. 

###### karma-kṣaya-śrutayaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
tathā ca vēdāntavākyāni kēvalakarmaphalasya kṣayitvaṁ brahmajñānasya cākṣayaphalatvaṁ ca darśayanti-  
tad yathā - 

**English**—
That the fruit of mere works is transitory, while the result of the knowledge of Brahman is something permanent, the Vedanta-texts declare in many places--

**vi॰pra॰**—
> tad yathēha karmacitō lōkaḥ kṣīyatē,  
> ēvam ēvāmutra puṇya-citō lōkaḥ kṣīyatē  
> (chāndōgyē.8.1.6) 

**English**—
> 'And as here the world acquired by work perishes, so there the world acquired by merit perishes' (Cḥ. Up. VIII, 1,6); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> antavad ēvāsya tad bhavati (br̥.5.8.10) 

**English**—
> 'That work of his has an end' (Br̥. Up. III, 8, 10); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> na hy a-dhruvaiḥ prāpyatē +++(dhruvam)+++ (kaṭha.2.10) 

**English**—
> 'By non-permanent works the Permanent **is not obtained**' (Ka. Up. I, 2, 10); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> plavā hy ētē a-dr̥ḍhā yajña-rūpāḥ (mu.1.2.7) 

**English**—
> 'Frail indeed are those boats, the sacrifices' (Mu. Up. I, 2, 7); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> parīkṣya lōkān karmacitān  
brāhmaṇō nirvēdam āyāt।  
nāsty a-kr̥taḥ kr̥tēna।  
tad-vijñānārthaṁ sa gurum ēvābhigacchēt samit-pāṇiś śrōtriyaṁ brahmaniṣṭham।+++(5)+++  

**English**—
> 'Let a Brāhmaṇa, after he has examined all these worlds that are gained by works, acquire freedom from all desires. What is not made cannot be gained by what is made.  
To understand this, let the pupil, with fuel in his hand, go to a teacher who is learned and dwells entirely in Brahman. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> tasmai sa vidvān upasannāya samyak-praśānta-cittāya śamānvitāya,  
yēnākṣaraṁ puruṣaṁ vēda  
satyaṁ prōvāca  
tāṁ tattvatō brahmavidyām । (mu.1.2.12-13) 

**English**—
> To that pupil who has approached him respectfully, whose mind is altogether calm, the wise teacher truly told that knowledge of Brahman through which he knows the imperishable true Person' (Mu. Up. I, 2, 12, l3).  
('Told' here means 'he is to tell.')

###### akṣayya-brahma-śrutayaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
> brahmavidāpnōti param (tai.ānanda.2.1anu.1) 

**English**—
On the other hand, 

> 'He who knows Brahman attains the Highest' (Taitt. Up. II, 1, 1); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> na punar mr̥tyavē tad ēkaṁ paśyati  
na paśyō mr̥tyuṁ paśyati (br̥.7.26.2) 

**English**—
> 'He who sees this does not see death' (Cḥ. Up. VII, 26, 2); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> sa svarāḍ bhavati (chāṁ.7.25.2) 

**English**—
> 'He becomes a self-ruler' (Cḥ. Up. VII, 25, 2); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> tam ēvaṁ vidvān amr̥ta iha bhavati  
nānyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyatē (pu.sū.17) 

**English**—
> 'Knowing him he becomes immortal here' (Taitt. Ār. III, 12, 7);  
> 'Having known him he passes over death;  
there is no other path to go' (Śvet. Up. VI, 15); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> pr̥thag ātmānaṁ prēritāraṁ ca matvā  
juṣṭas tatas tēnāmr̥tatvam ēti  
(śvē.1.6)  

ityādīni॥

**English**—
> 'Having known as separate his Self and the Mover,  
pleased thereby he goes to immortality'  
(Śvet. Up. I, 6).

###### karma-mīmāṁsāpēkṣā brahma-mīmāṁsāpēkṣēva
**vi॰pra॰**—
> nanu ca –  
sāṅga-vēdādhyayanād ēva karmaṇāṁ svargādi-phalatvam,  
svargādīnāṁ ca kṣayitvaṁ,  
brahmōpāsanasyāmr̥tatva-phalatvaṁ ca jñāyata ēva।  
anantaraṁ mumukṣur brahma-jijñāsāyām ēva pravartatām;  
kimarthā dharma-vicārāpēkṣā? 

**English**—
But – an objection here is raised--

> the mere learning of the Veda with its auxiliary disciplines gives rise to the knowledge that the heavenly world and the like are the results of works, and that all such results are transitory, while immortality is the fruit of meditation on Brahman. Possessing such knowledge, a person desirous of final release may at once proceed to the enquiry into Brahman; and what need is there of a systematic consideration of religious duty (i.e. of the study of the Purva Mimāṁsā)? 

**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvaṁ tarhi śārīraka-mīmāṁsāyām api na pravartatām,  
sāṅgādhyayanādēva kr̥tsnasya jñātatvāt। 

**English**—
--If this reasoning were valid, we reply, tin – person desirous of release need not even apply himself to the study of the Sārīraka Mīmāṁsā, since Brahman is known from the mere reading of the Veda with its auxiliary disciplines.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> satyam;  
āpāta-pratītir vidyata ēva,  
tathāpi nyāyānugr̥hītasya vākyasyārtha-niścāyakatvād  
āpāta-pratītō'py arthas  
saṁśaya-viparyayau nātivartatē;  
atas tan-nirṇayāya vēdānta-vākya-vicāraḥ kartavya 

iti cēt; 

**English**—
> True. Such knowledge arises indeed immediately (without deeper enquiry). But a matter apprehended in this immediate way is not raised above doubt and mistake. Hence a systematic discussion of the Vedānta-texts must he undertaken in order that their sense may be fully ascertained--

**vi॰pra॰**—
tathaiva dharmavicārō'pi kartavya  
iti paśyatu bhavān ॥

**English**—
We agree. But you will have to admit that for the very same reason we must undertake a systematic enquiry into religious duty!

**vistāraḥ**—
iti savimarśaḥ pūrvācāryasammatādyasūtrākṣaravyākhyāghaṭṭaḥ॥

##### 4 sādhana-catuṣṭayēnālam? laghu-pūrva-pakṣaḥ

###### paricayaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
nanu ca – brahma-jijñāsā yad ēva niyamēnāpēkṣatē,  
tad ēva pūrvavr̥ttaṁ vaktavyam।  
na dharma-vicārāpēkṣā brahma-jijñāsāyāḥ,  
adhīta-vēdāntasyānadhigata-karmaṇō'pi  
vēdānta-vākyārtha-vicārōpapattēḥ। 

**English**—
But – a further objection is urged--

> as that which has to precede the systematic enquiry into Brahman we should assign something which that enquiry necessarily presupposes.  
The enquiry into the nature of duty, however, does not form such a prerequisite,  
since a consideration of the Vedanta-texts may be undertaken by any one who has read those texts,  
even if he is not acquainted with works.

###### upāsanōpadēśaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
> karmāṅgāśrayāṇi udgīthādy-upāsanāny  
atraiva cintyantē;  
tad-anadhigata-karmaṇō na śakyaṁ kartum, 

iti cēt –

**English**—
> But in the Vedanta-texts there are enjoined meditations on the Udgītha and the like which;uc matters auxiliary to works; and such meditations are not possible for him who is not acquainted with those works!--

**vi॰pra॰**—
anabhijñō bhavān śārīraka-śāstra-vijñānasya। 

**English**—
You who raise this objection clearly are ignorant of what kind of knowledge the Śārīraka Mīmāṁsā is concerned with! 

**vi॰pra॰**—
asmin śāstrē  
an-ādy--a-vidyā-kr̥ta-- vividha-bhēda-darśana-nimitta-- janma-jarā-maraṇādi-- sāṁsārika-duḥkha-sāgara-nimagnasya  
nikhila-duḥkha-mūla-- mithyā-jñāna-nibarhāṇāya  
ātmaikatva-vijñānaṁ pratipipādayiṣitam। 

**English**—
What that śāstra aims at is to destroy completely that wrong knowledge which is the root of all pain, for man, liable to birth, old age, and death, and all the numberless other evils connected with transmigratory existence – evils that spring from the view, due to beginningless Nescience, that there is plurality of existence; and to that end the śāstra endeavours to establish the knowledge of the unity of the Self. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
asya hi bhēdāvalambi karma-jñānaṁ kvōpayujyatē? pratyuta viruddhamēva। 

**English**—
Now to this knowledge, the knowledge of works – which is based on the assumption of plurality of existence – is not only useless but even opposed. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
udgīthādi-vicāras tu  
karma-śēṣa-bhūta ēva  
jñāna-rūpatvāviśēṣād ihaiva kriyatē। 

**English**—
The consideration of the Udgītha and the like, which is supplementary to works only, finds a place in the Vedānta-texts, only because like them it is of the nature of knowledge; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
sa tu na sākṣāt-saṅga-taḥ। 

**English**—
but it has no direct connexion with the true topic of those texts. 

###### karma-samuccita-jñānān mōkṣaḥ?
**vi॰pra॰**—
atō yat pradhānaṁ śāstraṁ,  
tad-apēkṣitam ēva pūrva-vr̥ttaṁ kim api vaktavyam॥

**English**—
Hence some prerequisite must be indicated which has reference to the principal topic of the śāstra.

###### pūrvapakṣaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
> bāḍham; tad-apēkṣitaṁ ca karmavijñānamēva, karmasamuccitāt jñānād apavargaśrutēḥ। 

**English**—
> --Quite so; and this prerequisite is just the knowledge of works;  
for scripture declares that final release results from knowledge with works added. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> vakṣyati ca –  
> 
>> sarvāpēkṣā ca yajñādi-śrutēr aśvavat  
(bra.sū.3.4.26) 
> 
> iti। 

**English**—
> The Sūtra-writer himself says further on  
> 
> > 'And there is need of all works,  
on account of the scriptural statement of sacrifices and the like' (Ve. Sū. III, 4, 26). 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> apēkṣitē ca karmaṇy a-jñātē  
kēna samuccayaḥ, kēna nēti vibhāgō  
na śakyatē jñātum।  
atas tad ēva pūrvavr̥ttam॥

**English**—
> And if the required works were not known,  
one could not determine which works have to be combined with knowledge and which not.  
Hence the knowledge of works is just the necessary prerequisite.

###### avidyā-nivr̥ttēr mōkṣaḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
naitad yuktaṁ;  
sa-kala--viśēṣa-pratyanīka- cin-mātra-brahma-vijñānād ēvāvidyā-nivr̥ttēḥ;  
avidyā-nivr̥ttir ēva hi mōkṣaḥ। 

**English**—
--Not so, we reply. That which puts an end to Nescience is exclusively the knowledge of Brahman, which is pure intelligence and antagonistic to all plurality. For final release consists just in the cessation of Nescience; 

###### karma mōkṣa-virōdhi
**vi॰pra॰**—
varṇāśrama-viśēṣa-sādhya-- sādhanētikartavyatādy- ananta-vikalpāspadaṁ karma  
sa-kala--bhēda-darśana-nivr̥tti-rūpa- --a-jñāna-nivr̥ttēḥ  
katham iva sādhanaṁ bhavēt?

**English**—
how then can works – to which there attach endless differences connected with caste, āśrama, object to be accomplished, means and mode of accomplishment, &c.--ever supply a means for the cessation of ignorance, which is essentially the cessation of the view that difference exists? 

###### śrutayaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
śrutayaś ca karmaṇām a-nitya-phalatvēna mōkṣa-virōdhitvaṁ,  
jñānasyaiva mōkṣa-sādhanatvaṁ ca darśayanti – 

**English**—
That works, the results of which are transitory, are contrary to final release, and that such release can be effected through knowledge only, scripture declares in many places; compare all the passages quoted above (p. 7).

**vi॰pra॰**—
> antavad ēvāsya tadbhavati (br̥.5.8.10), 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> tad yathēha karmacitō lōkaḥ kṣīyatē।  
ēvam ēvāmutra puṇyacitō lōkaḥ kṣīyatē  
(chā.8.1.6), 

**vi॰pra॰**—
brahma-vid āpnōti param (tai.u.āna.2.1.1), 

**vi॰pra॰**—
brahma vēda brahmaiva bhavati (mu.3.2.9), 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> tam ēva viditvā'timr̥tyum ēti (śvē.3.8) – 

ityādyāḥ॥

###### vividiṣōtpattiḥ, cittaśuddhiḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
yad api cēdam uktaṁ  
"yajñādi-karmāpēkṣā vidyē"ti, 

**English**—
As to the assertion that knowledge requires sacrifices and other works,  
we remark that--

**vi॰pra॰**—
tad-vastu-virōdhāt śruty-akṣara-paryālōcanayā ca  
antaḥ-karaṇa-nairmalya-dvārēṇa vividiṣōtpattāv upayujyatē,  
na phalōtpattau,  
"vividiṣanti" iti śravaṇāt। 

**English**—
as follows from the essential contrariety of knowledge and works,  
and as further appears from an accurate consideration of the words of scripture--  
pious works can contribute only towards the rise of the desire of knowledge,  
in so far namely as they clear the internal organ (of knowledge),  
but can have no influence on the production of the fruit, i.e. knowledge itself.  
For the scriptural passage concerned runs as follows 

> Brāhmaṇas desire to know him  
by the study of the Veda, by sacrifice, by gifts,' &c. (Br̥. Up. IV, 4, 22).

According to this passage, the desire only of knowledge springs up through works; 

###### śamādīnām ēvāntaraṅgōpāyatā
**vi॰pra॰**—
vividiṣāyāṁ jātāyāṁ  
jñānōtpattau śamādīnām ēvāntaraṅgōpāyatāṁ śrutir ēvā'ha – 

**English**—
while another text teaches that calmness, self-restraint, and so on, are the direct means for the origination of knowledge itself. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> śāntō dānta uparatas titikṣus samāhitō bhūtvā  
''tmany ēvā'tmānaṁ paśyēt –  
(br̥.6.4.23) 

iti॥

**English**—
> Having become tranquil, calm, subdued, satisfied, patient, and collected,  
he is to see the Self within the Self (Br̥. Up. IV, 4,23).

###### vākya-janya-jñānād a-vidyā-nivr̥ttiḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
tad ēvaṁ janmāntara-śatānuṣṭhita- +anabhisaṁhita-phala-viśēṣa-- karma-mr̥dita-kaṣāyasya  
vividiṣōtpattau satyāṁ 

**English**—
The process thus is as follows. After the mind of a man has been cleaned of all impurities through works performed in many preceding states of existence, without a view to special forms of reward, there arises in him the desire of knowledge, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> sad ēva sōmyēdam agra āsīd  
ēkam ēvādvitīyam (chā.u.6.2.1) 

**English**—
> 'Being only, this was in the beginning, one only without a second' (Cḥ. Up. VI, I, 2); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> satyaṁ jñānam anantaṁ brahma (tai.āna.2.1.1) 

**English**—
> 'Truth, Knowledge, the Infinite, is Brahman' (Taitt. Up. II, 1); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> ??

**English**—
> 'Without parts, without actions, calm, without fault, without taint' (Śvet. Up. VI, 19); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> ayam ātmā brahma (br̥.6.4.5) 

**English**—
> 'This Self is Brahman' (Br̥. Up. II, 5, 19); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> tat tvam asi (chāṁ.6.8.7) 

**English**—
> 'Thou art that' (_Kh._ Up. VI, 9, 7),  

**vi॰pra॰**—
ity-ādi-vākya-janya-jñānād avidyā nivartatē।

**English**—
and thereupon--  
through knowledge itself originated by certain scriptural texts (above)--  
Nescience comes to an end. 

###### śravaṇa-manana-nididhyāsanāni

**vi॰pra॰**—
vākyārtha-jñānōpayōgīni ca śravaṇa-manana-nididhyāsanāni। 

**English**—
Now, 'Hearing,' 'reflection,' and 'meditation,' are helpful towards cognising the sense of these Vedic texts. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
**śravaṇaṁ** nāma  
vēdānta-vākyāni ātmaikatva-vidyā pratipādakānīti  
tattva-darśina ācāryāt  
nyāya-yuktārtha-grahaṇam। 

**English**—
'Hearing' (śravaṇa) means the apprehension of the sense of scripture, together with collateral arguments, from a teacher who possesses the true insight, viz. that the Vedānta-texts establish the doctrine of the unity of the Self. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvam ācāryōpadiṣṭasyārthasya  
svātmany "ēvam ēva yuktam"  
iti hētutaḥ pratiṣṭhāpanaṁ mananam। 

**English**—
'Reflection' (mananam) means the confirmation within oneself of the sense taught by the teacher, by means of arguments showing it alone to be suitable. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
ētad-virōdhy-- anādi-bhēda-vāsanā-nirasanāya  
asyaivārthasyānavarata-bhāvanā nididhyāsanam।

**English**—
'Meditation' (nididhyāsanam) finally means the constant holding of that sense before one's mind, so as to dispel thereby the antagonistic beginningless imagination of plurality. 

###### śravaṇāya sādhana-catuṣṭayam

**vi॰pra॰**—
śravaṇādibhir nirasta-samasta-bhēda-vāsanasya  
vākyārtha-jñānam avidyāṁ nivartayati  
ity-ēvaṁ-rūpasya śravaṇasyāvaśyāpēkṣitam ēva  
pūrvavr̥ttaṁ vaktavyam।

**English**—
In the case of him who through 'hearing,' 'reflection,' and meditation,' has dis-dispelled the entire imagination of plurality, the knowledge of the sense of Vedānta-texts puts an end to Nescience; and what we therefore require is a statement of the indispensable prerequisites of such 'hearing,' 'reflection,' and so on. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tac ca – nityānitya-vastu-vivēkaḥ, 

**English**—
Now, those are -  
discrimination of what is permanent and what is non-permanent; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
śama-damādi-sādhana-sampat, 

**English**—
the full possession of calmness of mind, self-restraint and similar means; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
ihāmutra-phala-bhōga-virāgaḥ, 

**English**—
the renunciation of all enjoyment of fruits here below as well as in the next world; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
mumukṣutvaṁ ca  

**English**—
and the desire of final release.

**vi॰pra॰**—
ity ētat sādhanacatuṣṭayam। 

**English**—
- these four prerequisites.  

**vi॰pra॰**—
anēna vinā jijñāsānupapattēḥ,  
artha-svabhāvād ēvēdam ēva pūrvavr̥ttam  
iti jñāyatē ॥

**English**—
Without these the desire of knowledge cannot arise; and they are therefore known, from the very nature of the matter, to be necessary prerequisites. 

###### bandha-mōkṣayōḥ karmānapēkṣā

**vi॰pra॰**—
ētad uktaṁ bhavati –  
brahma-svarūpācchādikā'vidyā-mūlam  
apāramārthikaṁ bhēda-darśanam ēva  
bandha-mūlam। 

**English**—
To sum up: The root of bondage is the unreal view of plurality which itself has its root in Nescience that conceals the true being of Brahman. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
bandhaś cāpāramārthikaḥ। 

**English**—
Bondage itself thus is unreal, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
sa ca sa-mūlō  
'pāramārthikatvād ēva  
jñānēnaiva nivartyatē। 

**English**—
and is on that account cut short, together with its root, by mere knowledge. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
nivartakaṁ ca jñānaṁ  
"tat tvam asy"-ādi-vākya-janyam । 

**English**—
Such knowledge is originated by texts such as 'That art thou'; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tasyaitasya vākya-janyasya jñānasya svarūpōtpattau kāryē vā  
karmaṇāṁ nōpayōgaḥ। 

**English**—
and work is of no help either towards its nature, or its origination, or its fruit (i.e. release). 

**vi॰pra॰**—
vividiṣāyām ēva tu karmaṇām upayōgaḥ। 

**English**—
It is on the other hand helpful towards the desire of knowledge, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
sa ca  
pāpa-mūla-- rajas-tamō-nibarhāṇa-dvārēṇa  
sattva-vivr̥ddhyā bhavati 

**English**—
which arises owing to an increase of the element of goodness (sattva) in the soul, due to the destruction of the elements of passion (rajas) and darkness (tamas) which are the root of all moral evil. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
itīmam upayōgam abhiprētya  
"brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti" ityuktamiti॥

**English**—
This use is referred to in the text quoted above, 'Brāhmaṇas wish to know him,' &c.  

###### nigamanam

**vi॰pra॰**—
ataḥ karma-jñānasyānupayōgāt  
uktam ēva sādhana-catuṣṭayaṁ pūrva-vr̥ttam  
iti vaktavyam।

**English**—
As, therefore, the knowledge of works is of no use towards the knowledge of Brahman, we must acknowledge as the prerequisite of the latter knowledge the four means mentioned above.

**viṣayaḥ**—
iti laghupūrvapakṣaḥ॥  
**laghusiddhāntaḥ**

**English**—
THE SMALL SIDDHĀNTA.

##### 5 sādhana-catuṣṭayēna nālam

###### avidyā-nivartaka-jñānam

**vi॰pra॰**—
atrōcyatē –  
yad uktam 

> a-vidyā-nivr̥ttir ēva mōkṣaḥ;  
sā ca brahma-vijñānād ēva bhavati 

iti, tad abhyupagamyatē। 

**English**—
To this argumentation we make the following reply. We admit that release consists only in the cessation of Nescience, and that this cessation results entirely from the knowledge of Brahman. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> a-vidyā--nivr̥ttayē  
vēdānta-vākyair vidhitsitaṁ jñānaṁ kiṁ-rūpam 

iti vivēcanīyam – 

**English**—
But a distinction has here to be made regarding the nature of this knowledge which the Vedānta-texts aim at enjoining for the purpose of putting an end to Nescience. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> kiṁ vākyād vākyārtha-jñāna-mātram,  
uta tan-mūlam upāsanātmakaṁ jñānam? 

\– iti; 

**English**—
Is it merely the knowledge of the sense of sentences which originates from the sentences?  
or is it knowledge in the form of meditation (upāsana) which has the knowledge just referred to as its antecedent? 

###### na vākyārtha-mātram
**vi॰pra॰**—
na tāvad vākya-janyaṁ jñānaṁ,  
tasya vidhānam antarēṇāpi  
vākyād ēva siddhēḥ; tāvan-mātrēṇāvidyā-nivr̥tty-anupalabdhēś ca।

**English**—
It cannot be knowledge of the former kind: for such knowledge springs from the mere apprehension of the sentence, apart from any special injunction,  
and moreover we do not observe that the cessation of Nescience is effected by such knowledge merely. 

###### vāsanā
**vi॰pra॰**—
na ca vācyaṁ – 

> bhēda-vāsanāyām anirastāyāṁ  
vākyam a-vidyā-nivartakaṁ jñānaṁ na janayati,  

**English**—
Our adversary will perhaps attempt to explain things in the following way. 

> The Vedānta-texts do not, he will say, produce that knowledge which makes an end of Nescience, so long as the imagination of plurality is not dispelled. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> jātē'pi sarvasya sahasaiva bhēda-jñānānivr̥ttir na dōṣāya,  
candraikatvē jñātē'pi  
dvi-candra--jñānānivr̥ttivat।  

**English**—
> And the fact that such knowledge, even when produced, does not at once and for every one put a stop to the view of plurality by no means subverts my opinion; for, to mention an analogous instance, the double appearance of the moon – presenting itself to a person affected with a certain weakness of vision – does not come to an end as soon as the oneness of the moon has been apprehended by reason. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> a-nivr̥ttam api chinna-mūlatvēna  
na bandhāya bhavati – 

iti- 

**English**—
> Moreover, even without having come to an end, the view of plurality is powerless to effect further bondage, as soon as the root, i.e. Nescience, has once been cut.

###### utpatti-balam
**vi॰pra॰**—
satyāṁ sāmagryāṁ jñānānutpatty-anupapattēḥ; 
**English**—
(But this defence we are unable to admit.)  
It is impossible that knowledge should not arise when its means, i.e. the texts conveying knowledge, are once present. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
satyām api viparīta-vāsanāyām  
āptōpadēśa-liṅgādibhir bādhaka-jñānōtpatti-darśanāt ।

**English**—
And we observe that even when there exists an antagonistic imagination (interfering with the rise of knowledge), information given by competent persons, the presence of characteristic marks (on which a correct inference may be based), and the like give rise to knowledge which sublates the erroneous imagination. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> saty api vākyārtha-jñānē  
anādi-vāsanayā mātrayā  
bhēda-jñānam anuvartata  

iti bhavatā na śakyatē vaktum;  
bhēda-jñāna-sāmagryā api vāsanāyā mithyā-rūpatvēna  
jñānōtpattyaiva nivr̥ttatvāt । 

**English**—
Nor can we admit that even after the sense of texts has been apprehended, the view of plurality may continue owing to some small remainder of beginningless imagination. 

For as this imagination which constitutes the means for the view of plurality is itself false, it is necessarily put an end to by the rise of true knowledge. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
jñānōtpattāv api  
mithyā-rūpāyās tasyā anivr̥ttau  
nivartakāntarābhāvāt  
kadācid api nāsyā vāsanāyā nivr̥ttiḥ।+++(5)+++

**English**—
If this did not take place, that imagination would never come to an end, since there is no other means but knowledge to effect its cessation. 

###### na chinna-mūlasyānuvr̥ttiḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
vāsanā-kāryaṁ bhēda-jñānaṁ chinna-mūlam  
atha cānuvartata iti bāliśa-bhāṣitam॥ +++(5)+++

**English**—
To say that the view of plurality, which is the effect of that imagination, continues even after its root has been cut, is mere nonsense. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
dvi-candra-jñānādau tu  
bādhaka-sannidhāv api  
mithyā-jñāna-hētōḥ paramārtha-timirādi-dōṣasya jñāna-bādhyatvābhāvēnāvinaṣṭatvāt  
mithyā-jñānānivr̥ttir aviruddhā। 

**English**—
The instance of some one seeing the moon double is not analogous. For in his case the non-cessation of wrong knowledge explains itself from the circumstance that the cause of wrong knowledge, viz. the real defect of the eye which does not admit of being sublated by knowledge, is not removed, although that which would sublate wrong knowledge is near. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
prabala-pramāṇa-bādhitatvēna  
bhayādi-kāryaṁ tu nivartatē।+++(4)+++

**English**—
On the other hand, effects, such as fear and the like, may come to an end because they can be sublated by means of knowledge of superior force. 

###### bhēda-vāsanā'pākr̥tir asambhavā

**vi॰pra॰**—
api ca bhēda-vāsanā-nirasana-dvārēṇa  
jñānōtpattim abhyupagacchatāṁ  
kadācid api jñānōtpattir na sētsyati; +++(4)+++

**English**—
Moreover, if it were true that knowledge arises through the dispelling of the imagination of plurality, the rise of knowledge would really never be brought about. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
bhēda-vāsanāyā anādikālōpacitatvēnāparimitatvāt,+++(5)+++

**English**—
For the imagination of plurality has through gradual growth in the course of beginningless time acquired an infinite strength, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tad-virōdhi-bhāvanāyāś cālpatvād  
anayā tan-nirasanānupapattēḥ।

**English**—
and does not therefore admit of being dispelled by the comparatively weak conception of non-duality. 

###### nigamanam, śrutayaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
atō vākyārthajñānād anyad ēva  
dhyānōpāsanādi-śabda-vācyaṁ jñānaṁ  
vēdānta-vākyair vidhitsitam। 

**English**—
Hence we conclude that the knowledge which the Vedānta-texts aim at inculcating is a knowledge other than the mere knowledge of the sense of sentences, and denoted by 'dhyāna,' 'upāsanā' (i. e. meditation), and similar terms.

**vi॰pra॰**—
tathā ca śrutayaḥ – 

> vijñāya prajñāṁ kurvīta (br̥.6.4.21) 

**English**—
With this agree scriptural texts such as 

> 'Having known it, let him practise meditation' (Br̥. Up. IV, 4, 21); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> anuvidya vijānāti (chāṁ.8.12.6) 

**English**—
> 'He who, having searched out the Self, knows it' (Cḥ. Up. VIII, 7, 1); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> ōm ity ēvātmānaṁ dhyāyatha (mu.2.2.6) 

**English**—
> 'Meditate on the Self as Om' (Mu. Up. II, 2, 6); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> nicāyya taṁ mr̥tyu-mukhāt pramucyatē (ka.1.3.15) 

**English**—
> 'Having known that,  
he is freed from the jaws of death' (Ka. Up. I, 3, 15); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> ātmānam ēva lōkam upāsīta (br̥.3.4.14) 

**English**—
> 'Let a man meditate on the Self only as his world' (Br̥. Up. I, 4, 15); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> ātmā vā arē draṣṭavyaś śrōtavyō mantavyō nididhyāsitavyaḥ (br̥.6.4.6) 

**English**—
> 'The Self is to be seen, to be heard, to her reflected on, to be meditated on' (Br̥. Up. IV, 5, 6); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> sō'nvēṣṭavyas sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ (chāṁ.8.7.1) 

ityēvamādyāḥ॥

**English**—
> 'That we must search out,  
that we must try to understand' (Cḥ. Up. VIII, 7, 1).

###### arthajñānānuvādaḥ, dhyāna-vidhiḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
atra "nididhyāsitavyaḥ" ity-ādinaikārthyāt  

> anuvidya vijānāti,  

> vijñāya prajñāṁ kurvīta 

ity-ēvam-ādibhir vākyārtha-jñānaṁ dhyānōpakārakatvāt  
"anuvidya", "vijñāya" ity anūdya  

"prajñāṅ kurvīta", "vijānāti"  
iti dhyānaṁ vidhīyatē। 

**English**—
(According to the principle of the oneness of purport of the different śākhās) all these texts must be viewed as agreeing in meaning with the injunction of meditation contained in the passage quoted from the Br̥. Up.; and what they enjoin is therefore meditation. In the first and second passages quoted, the words 'having known' and 'having searched out' (vijñāya; anuvidya) contain a mere reference to (not injunction of) the apprehension of the meaning of texts, such apprehension subserving meditation; while the injunction of meditation (which is the true purport of the passages) is conveyed by the clauses 'let him practise meditation' (prajñāṁ kurvīta) and 'he knows it.' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
"śrōtavyaḥ" iti cānuvādaḥ -  

svādhyāyasyārtha-paratvēna  
adhīta-vēdaḥ puruṣaḥ prayōjanavad-arthāvabōdhitva-darśanāt  
tan-nirṇayāya svayam ēva śravaṇē pravartata  
iti śravaṇasya prāptatvāt। 

**English**—
In the same way the clause 'the Self is to be heard' is a mere anuvāda,  
i.e. a mere reference to what is already established by other means; for a person who has read the Veda observes that it contains instruction about matters connected with certain definite purposes, and then on his own account applies himself to methodical 'hearing,' in order definitely to ascertain these matters; 'hearing' thus is established already. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
śravaṇa-pratiṣṭhārthatvān mananasya  
mantavya iti cānuvādaḥ । 

**English**—
In the same way the clause 'the Self is to be reflected upon' is a mere anuvāda of reflection which is known as a means of confirming what one has 'heard.' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tasmād dhyānam ēva vidhīyatē । 

**English**—
It is therefore meditation only which all those texts enjoin. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
vakṣyati ca 

> āvr̥ttir asakr̥d upadēśāt (bra.sū.4.1.1) 

iti।

**English**—
In agreement with this a later Sūtra also says, 

> 'Repetition more than once, on account of instruction' (Ve. Sū. IV, I, I). 

###### vēdanōpāsanē dhyānam

**vi॰pra॰**—
tad idam  
apavargōpāyatayā vidhitsitaṁ vēdanam  
upāsanam ity avagamyatē  
vidy-upāsyōr vyatikarēṇa upakramōpasaṁhāra-darśanāt -

**English**—
That the knowledge intended to be enjoined as the means of final release is of the nature of meditation,  
we conclude from the circumstance that the terms 'knowing' and'meditating' are seen to be used in place of each other in the earlier and later parts of Vedic texts. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> manō brahmēty upāsīta (chāṁ.3.18.1) 

ityatra 

**English**—
Compare the following passages: 

> 'Let a man meditate on mind as Brahman,' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasēna  
ya ēvaṁ vēda, (chāṁ.3.18.5) 

**English**—
and 

> 'he who knows this shines and warms through his celebrity, fame, and glory of countenance'  
(Cḥ. Up. III, 18, 1; 6). 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> na sa vēda  
akr̥tsnō hy ēṣaḥ …  
ātmēty ēvōpāsīta, (br̥.3.4.7) 

**English**—
And 'He does not know him, for he is not complete,'  
and 'Let men meditate on him as the Self (Br̥. Up. I, 4, 7). 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> yas tad vēda  
yat sa vēda …  
sa mayaitad uktaḥ (chā.4.1.4) 

ityatra 

**English**—
And 

> 'He who knows what he knows,' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> anu ma ētāṁ bhagavō dēvatāṁ śādhi  
yāṁ dēvatām upāssē (chāṁ.4.2.2) 

iti॥

**English**—
and 

> 'Teach me the deity on which you meditate' (Cḥ. Up. IV, 1,6; 2, 2).

###### dhyāna-svarūpam

**vi॰pra॰**—
dhyānaṁ ca taila-dhārāvad a-vicchinna-smr̥ti-santāna-rūpam -  

> dhruvā smr̥tiḥ। smr̥ti-lambhē sarva-granthīnāṁ vipramōkṣaḥ (chā.7.26.2) 

iti dhruvāyās smr̥tēr apavargōpāyatva-śravaṇāt। 

**English**—
'Meditation' means steady remembrance, i.e. a continuity of steady remembrance, uninterrupted like the flow of oil; in agreement with the scriptural passage which declares steady remembrance to be the means of release, 'on the attainment of remembrance all the ties are loosened' (Cḥ. Up. VII, 26, 2). 

###### darśana-rūpatā
**vi॰pra॰**—
sā ca smr̥tir darśana-samānākārā 

> bhidyatē hr̥daya-granthiś  
chidyantē sarvasaṁśayāḥ ।  
kṣīyantē cāsya karmāṇi  
tasmin dr̥ṣṭē parāvarē॥ (mu.2.1.8) 

ity anēnaikārthyāt । 

**English**—
Such remembrance is of the same character (form) as seeing (intuition); for the passage quoted has the same purport as the following one, 'The fetter of the heart is broken, all doubts are solved, and all the works of that man perish when he has been seen who is high and low' (Mu. Up. II, 2, 8). 

**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvaṁ ca sati 

> ātmā vā arē draṣṭavyaḥ (br̥.64.6) 

ity-anēna nididhyāsanasya darśana-samānākāratā vidhīyatē । 

**English**—
And this being so, we conclude that the passage 'the Self is to be seen' teaches that 'Meditation' has the character of 'seeing' or 'intuition.' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
bhavati ca smr̥tēr bhāvanā-prakarṣād darśana-rūpatā। 

**English**—
And that remembrance has the character of 'seeing' is due to the element of imagination (representation) which prevails in it. 

###### vākyakārōktiḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
vākya-kārēṇaitat sarvaṁ prapañcitam –  

> vēdanam upāsanaṁ syāt - tadviṣayē śravaṇāt 

iti। 

**English**—
All this has been set forth at length by the Vākyakāra. 'Knowledge (vedana) means meditation (upāsana), scripture using the word in that sense';  

**vi॰pra॰**—
sarvāsūpaniṣatsu mōkṣa-sādhanatayā vihitaṁ vēdanam  
upāsanam ity uktam। 

**English**—
i.e. in all Upanishads that knowledge which is enjoined as the means of final release is Meditation.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> sakr̥t pratyayaṁ kuryāc  
chabdārthasya kr̥tatvāt prayājādivat 

iti pūrvapakṣaṁ kr̥tvā 

**English**—
The Vākyakāra then propounds a pūrvapaksha (primā facie view), 

> 'Once he is to make the meditation, the matter enjoined by scripture being accomplished thereby, as in the case of the prayājas and the like'; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
"siddhaṁ tūpāsanaśabdād" iti  
vēdanam asakr̥d āvr̥ttaṁ  
mōkṣa-sādhanam  
iti nirṇītam । 

**English**—
and then sums up against this in the words 'but (meditation) is established on account of the term meditation'; that means – knowledge repeated more than once (i.e. meditation) is determined to be the means of Release.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> upāsanaṁ syād dhruvānusmr̥tir - darśanān nirvacanāc ca 

iti tasyaiva vēdanasyōpāsana-rūpasyāsakr̥d-āvr̥ttasya  
dhruvānusmr̥titvam upavarṇitam॥

**English**—
The Vākyakāra then goes on 'Meditation is steady remembrance, on the ground of observation and statement.' 

That means – this knowledge, of the form of meditation, and repeated more than once, is of the nature of steady remembrance.

###### pratyakṣāpattiḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
sēyaṁ smr̥tir darśanarūpā pratipāditā । 

**English**—
Such remembrance has been declared to be of the character of 'seeing,' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
darśanarūpatā ca pratyakṣatāpattiḥ ।

**English**—
and this character of seeing consists in its possessing the character of immediate presentation (pratyakshatā). 

###### śravaṇādi-sādhanatva-nirākr̥tiḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvaṁ pratyakṣatāpannām apavarga-sādhana-bhūtāṁ smr̥tiṁ viśinaṣṭi –

**English**—
With reference to remembrance, which thus acquires the character of immediate presentation and is the means of final release, scripture makes a further determination, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> nāyam ātmā pravacanēna labhyō  
> na mēdhayā na bahunā śrutēna।  
> yam ēvaiṣa vr̥ṇutē tēna labhyas  
> tasyaiṣa ātmā vivr̥ṇutē tanūṁ svām ॥  
> (mu.3.2.3)

iti। 

**English**—
viz. in the passage Ka. Up. I, 2, 23, 'That Self cannot be gained by the study of the Veda ("reflection"), nor by thought ("meditation"), nor by much hearing. Whom the Self chooses, by him it may be gained; to him the Self reveals its being.' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
anēna kēvala-śravaṇa-manana-nididhyāsanānām ātma-prāpty-anupāyatvam uktvā  

> "yam ēvaiṣa ātmā vr̥ṇutē  
tēnaiva labhya" 

ityuktam ।  

**English**—
This text says at first that mere hearing, reflection, and meditation do not suffice to gain the Self, and then declares, 'Whom the Self chooses, by him it may be gained.' 

###### yuktānāṁ varaṇīyatā

**vi॰pra॰**—
priyatama ēva hi varaṇīyō bhavati।  

**English**—
Now a 'chosen' one means a most beloved person; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
yasyāyaṁ niratiśayapriyas  
sa ēvāsya priyatamō bhavati।
