daharavidyāyāṁ – **tadya ihātmānamanuvidya vrajantyētāṁśca satyānkāmān** (chā.8.1.6) iti daharākāśasya paramātmana upāsanamuktvā
**ētāṁśca satyānkāmān** (chāṁ.8.1.6) iti guṇānāmapi pr̥thagupāsanaṁ vihitam ।

#### vicāraupayikassaṁśayaḥ

tatra saṁśayaḥ – guṇacintanē'pi tattadguṇaviśiṣṭatayā daharasyātmanaścintanamāvartanīyam, uta nēti।

#### pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ

daharākāśasyaiva apahatapāpmatvādīnāṁ guṇitvāttasya ca sakr̥dēvānusandhātuṁ śakyatvādguṇārthaṁ taccintanaṁ nāvartanīyam –

#### sadr̥ṣṭāntōpapattikaḥ siddhāntaḥ

iti prāptē ucyatē pradānavadēva – iti। pradānavadāvartanīyamēvētyarthaḥ । yadyapi daharākāśa ēka ēvāpahatapāpmatvādiguṇānāṁ guṇī; sa ca prathamaṁ cintitaḥ; tathā'pi svarūpamātrādguṇaviśiṣṭākārasya bhinnatvāt **apahatapāpmā vijaraḥ** (chā.8.1.5) ityādinā guṇaviśiṣṭatayā cōpāsyatvēna vihitatvātpūrvaṁ svarūpēṇānusaṁhitasyāpahatapāpmatvādiviśiṣṭatayā'nusandhānārthamāvr̥ttiḥ kartavyā, yathā indrāya rājñē purōḍāśamēkādaśakapālaṁ nirvapēt , indrāyādhirājāya, **indrāya svarājñē** (yaju.2.3.6) itīndrasyaiva rājatvādiguṇaviśiṣṭatvē'pi tattadguṇasambandhyākārasya bhinnatvātpradānāvr̥ttiḥ kriyatē; taduktaṁ sāṅkarṣaṇē **nānā vā dēvatā pr̥thaktvāt** (saṅka.kāṇḍē) iti ॥42॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē pradānādhikaraṇam॥18॥**

### 19 liṅgabhūyastvādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē liṅgabhūyastvādhikaraṇam॥19॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
taittarīyakagatasya sahasraśīrṣakamityanuvākasya sarvavēdāntōditaparavidyōpāsyaviśēṣanirdhāraṇaparatvam, na tu daharavidyāmātraśēṣatvam

**397. liṅgabhūyastvāttaddhi balīyastadapi ॥ 3–3–43 ॥**

#### vicāraṇīyaviṣayanirdēśaḥ

taittirīyā daharavidyānantaramadhīyatē sahasraśīrṣaṁ dēvaṁ viśvākṣaṁ viśvaśambhuvam । viśvaṁ nārāyaṇaṁ dēvamakṣaraṁ paramaṁ prabhum ityārabhya sō'kṣaraḥ paramassvarāṭ (tai.nā.1) ityantam।

#### vicāraupayikaḥ saṁśayaḥ

tatra saṁśayaḥ- kiṁ pūrvaprakr̥tavidyaikavidyātvēna tadupāsyaviśēṣanirdhāraṇamanēna kriyatē, uta sarvavēdāntōditaparavidyōpāsyaviśēṣanirdhāraṇam – iti।

#### sahētukaḥ pūrvaḥpakṣaḥ

kiṁ yuktam? daharavidyōpāsyaviśēṣanirdhāraṇamiti। kutaḥ? prakaraṇāt। pūrvasminnanuvākē daharavidyā hi prakr̥tā **dahraṁ vipāpmaṁ paravēśmabhūtaṁ yatpuṇḍarīkaṁ puramadhyasaṁstham। tatrāpi dahraṁ gaganaṁ viśōkastasminyadantastadupāsitavyam** (tai.nā.10) iti। asmiṁścānuvākē padmakōśapratīkāśaṁ hr̥dayaṁ cāpyadhōmukham (tai.nā.11) ityādinā hr̥dayapuṇḍarīkābhidhānamasya nārāyaṇānuvākasya daharavidyōpāsyanirdhāraṇārthatvamupōdbalayatīti॥

#### sūtrārthavivr̥tyā siddhāntārthaḥ

ēvaṁ prāptē pracakṣmahē liṅgabhūyastvāt – iti। asya nikhilaparavidyōpāsyaviśēṣa nirdhāraṇārthatvē bhūyāṁsi liṅgāni dr̥śyantē; tathā hi paravidyāsvakṣaraśivaśambhuparabrahmaparajyōtiḥ paratattvaparamātmādiśabdanirdiṣṭamupāsyaṁ vastviha tairēva śabdairanūdya tasya nārāyaṇatvaṁ vidhīyatē; bhūyasīṣu vidyāsu śrutānanūdya nārāyaṇatvavidhānabhūyastvaṁ nārāyaṇa ēva sarvavidyāsūpāsyamasthūlatvādiviśēṣitānandādiguṇakaṁ paraṁ brahmēti viśēṣanirṇayē bhūyaḥ bahutaraṁ liṅgaṁ bhavati। atra liṅgaśabdaḥ cihnaparyāyaḥ। cihnabhūtaṁ vākyaṁ bahutaramastītyarthaḥ।

#### liṅgasya balīyastvōpapattiḥ

taddhi prakaraṇādbalīyaḥ। tadapyuktaṁ prathamakāṇḍē – śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāṁ **samavāyē pāradaurbalyamarthaviprakarṣāt** (jai.mī.sū.3.3.14) iti।

#### daharamātraśēṣatāyā nirāsaḥ

yattūktaṁ **padmakōśapratīkāśam** (tai.nā.11) ityādivacanaṁ daharaśēṣatvamasyōpōdbalayati – iti; tanna, balīyasā pramāṇēna sarvavidyōpāsyanirdhāraṇārthatvē'vadhr̥tē sati daharavidyāyāmapi tasyaiva nārāyaṇasyōpāsyatvēna tadvacanōpapattēḥ। na ca **sahasraśīrṣam** (tai.nā.11) ityādi dvitīyānirdēśēna pūrvānuvākōditōpāsinā sambandhaśśaṅkanīyaḥ,
**tasminyadantastadupāsitavyam** (tai.nā.10) ityupāsigatēna kr̥tpratyayēnōpāsyasya karmaṇō'bhihitatvāttadupāsyē dvitīyānupapattēḥ। **viśvamēvēdaṁ puruṣaḥ** (tai.nā.11.anu) **tattvaṁ nārāyaṇaḥparaḥ** (tai.nā.11) ityādi prathamānirdēśācca prathamārthē dvitīyā vēditavyā । **antarbahiśca tatsarvaṁ vyāpya nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ** (tai.nā.11) **tasyāśśikhāyā madhyē paramātmā vyavasthitaḥ sa brahmā sa śivassēndraḥ sō'kṣaraḥ paramassvarāṭ** (tai.nā.11) iti nirdēśaissarvasmātparō nārāyaṇa ēva sarvatrōpāsya iti nirṇīyamānatvācca prathamārthē dvitīyēti niścīyatē ॥43॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē liṅgabhūyastvādhikaraṇam॥19॥**

### 20 pūrvavikalpādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē pūrvavikalpādhikaraṇam॥20॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
agnirahasyabrāhmaṇōktānāṁ manaścidādīnāṁ vidyāmayakratvanupraviṣṭatā

**398. pūrvavikalpaḥ prakaraṇātsyātkriyā mānasavat ॥ 3–3–44 ॥**

#### vicāraṇīyaviṣayōpasthāpanam

vājasanēyakē agnirahasyē manaścitādayō'gnayaḥ śrūyantē – manaścitō vākcitaḥ prāṇacitaḥ cakṣuścitaḥ śrōtracitaḥ karmacitō'gnicitaḥ (agnirahasyaṁ) iti ।

#### vicāraupayikassaṁśayaḥ

tatra saṁśayaḥ – kimētē manaścitādayassāmpādikatvēna vidyārūpā agnayaḥ kriyāmayakratvanupravēśēna kriyārūpāḥ, āhōsvidvidyāmayakratvanupravēśēna vidyārūpā ēva – iti viśayē

#### pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ sūtrata ēva

kriyārūpatvaṁ tāvadāha – pūrvavikalpaḥ – ityādinā। cityāgnitvēna sampāditānāmēṣāṁ manaścitādīnāṁ kratvanupravēśasākāṅkṣāṇāṁ svadēśē kratuvidhyabhāvātpūrvatra **asadvā idamagra āsīt** (agnirahasyaṁ) ityādinēṣṭakacitasyāgnēḥ prakr̥tatvāt tasya ca kriyāmayakratvavyabhicāritvēna tatra kratusannidhānāttatprakaraṇagr̥hītā manaścitādayastēnēṣṭakacitēnāgninā vikalpyamānāḥ kriyārūpā ēva syuḥ। vidyārūpāṇāmapi kriyāmayakratvanupravēśēna kriyārūpatvaṁ mānasagrahavadupapadyatē। yathā dvādaśāhē avivākyē daśamē'hani mānasagrahasya manōniṣpādyagrahaṇāsādanastōtra-śastrapratyāharaṇabhakṣaṇatvēna vidyārūpasyāpi kriyāmayakratvaṅgatayā kriyārūpatvam; tathēhāpi ॥ 44॥

#### uktārthadr̥ḍhīkaraṇam

**399. atidēśācca ॥ 3–3–45 ॥**

itaścēṣṭakacitēnāgninā manaścitādīnāṁ vikalpaḥ kriyārūpatvaṁ cāvagamyatē;
**tēṣāmēkaika ēva tāvān yāvānasau pūrvaḥ** (agnirahasyam) iti pūrvasyēṣṭakacitasyāgnērvīryaṁ manaścitādiṣvatidiśyatē; tēna tulyakāryatvādvikalpaḥ। tataścēṣṭakacitavattatkratunirvartanēna tadaṅgabhūtāḥ manaścitādayaḥ kriyāmayakratvanupravēśēna kriyārūpā ēvēti ॥ 45॥

#### siddhāntasūtrāṇi

ēvaṁ prāptē pracakṣmahē –

**400. vidyaiva tu nirdhāraṇāddarśanācca ॥ 3–3–46 ॥**

tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṁ vyāvartayati; yaduktaṁ manaścitādayaḥ kriyāmayakratvanupravēśēna kriyārūpā ēvēti; naitadasti; vidyārūpā ēvaitē- vidyārūpakratvanvayina ityarthaḥ। kutaḥ? nirdhāraṇāddarśanācca; nirdhāraṇaṁ tāvat **tē haitē vidyācita ēva vidyayā haivaita ēvaṁvidaścitā bhavanti** (agnirahasyam 10.5.3) iti; vāṅmanaścakṣurādivyāpārāṇāmiṣṭakādivaccayanānupapattērmanasā sampāditāgnitvēna vidyārūpatvē siddhē'pi vidyācita ēva, **vidyayā haivaitē** (agnirahasyam 10.5.3) iti cāvadhāraṇaṁ vidyāmayakratvanvayēna vidyārūpatvajñāpanārthamiti niścīyatē ।

#### darśanāccēti sautrabhāgavyākhyānam

dr̥śyatē cātraivaiṣāṁ śēṣī vidyārūpaḥ kratuḥ **tē manasaivādhīyanta manasaivācīyanta manasaiṣu grahā agr̥hyanta manasā stuvanta manasā śaṁsan yatkiñca yajñē karma kriyatē, yatkiñca yajñīyaṁ karma manasaiva tēṣu manōmayēṣu manaścitsu manōmayamakriyata** (agnirahasyam 10.5.3.3) iti। iṣṭakacitēṣvagniṣu yatkriyāmayaṁ yajñīyaṁ karma kriyatē; tanmanōnirvartyēṣu manaścitādyagniṣu manōmayamēvākriyatēti vacanāt kraturapi vidyāmayō'tra pratīyatē ॥46॥

#### vidyārūpatvasya bādhaśaṅkātatparihārau

nanvatra vidhipadāśravaṇāt phalasambandhāpratītēścēṣṭakacitāgnyupasthāpitakriyāmayakratu-prakaraṇādvidyāmayakratvanvayēna vidyārūpataiṣāṁ bādhyatē, nētyāha –

**401. śrutyādibalīyastvācca na bādhaḥ ॥ 3–3–47 ॥**

śrutiliṅgavākyānāṁ prakaraṇādbalīyastvēna śrutyādyavagataḥ kraturēṣāṁ tadanvayaśca durbalēna prakaraṇēna bādhituṁ na śakyatē; śrutistāvat – **tē haitē vidyācita ēva** (agnirahasyaṁ) iti। tāṁ vivr̥ṇōti **vidyayā haivaita ēvaṁvidaścitā bhavanti** (agnirahasyaṁ) iti। vidyayā vidyāmayēna kratunā sambaddhā manaścitādayaścitā bhavantītyarthaḥ । **tān haitānēvaṁvidē sarvadā sarvāṇi bhūtāni cinvantyapi svapatē** (agnirahasyaṁ) iti liṅgam। vākyaṁ ca
**ēvaṁvidē cinvanti** (agnirahasyaṁ) iti । samabhivyāhārō vākyam । ēvaṁvidē vidyāmayakratumatē sarvadā sarvāṇi bhūtāni cinvantītyarthaḥ । sarvabhūtakartr̥kaṁ sarvakālavyāpi cayanaṁ manasā sampāditaṁ parimitakartr̥kālakriyāmayēṣṭakacitakāryadvārēṇa kratvanupravēśasambhavamalabhamānaṁ vidyāmayakratvanupravēśē liṅgaṁ bhavati ॥47॥

#### pūrvōktapūrvapakṣahētvanuvādapūrvakaṁ sūtratō nirāsaḥ

yaccēdamuktaṁ – vidhipratyayāśravaṇātphalasambandhāpratītēśca kriyāmayātkratōranyō'tra vidyāmayaḥ kraturna sambhavati – iti, tatrāha –

**402. anubandhādibhyaḥ prajñāntarapr̥thaktvavaddr̥ṣṭaśca taduktam ॥ 3–3–48 ॥**

iṣṭakacitānvayinaḥ kriyāmayātkratōrvidyāmayō'yaṁ kratuḥ pr̥thaktvēna anubandhādibhyaḥ pr̥thaktvahētubhyō'vagamyatē। anubandhāḥ yajñānubandhinō grahastōtraśastrādayaḥ **manasaiṣu grahā agr̥hyanta manasāstuvanta manasāśaṁsan** (agnirahasyaṁ) ityādinā pratipāditāḥ। ādiśabdēna śrutyādayaḥ pūrvōktā gr̥hyantē। śrutyādibhissānubandhairvidyāmayakratuḥ pr̥thagavagamyata ityarthaḥ। prajñāntarapr̥thaktvavat – yathā prajñāntaraṁ daharavidyādi kriyāmayātkratōḥ pr̥thagbhūtaṁ śrutyādibhiravagamyatē, ēvamayamapi । ēvaṁ cānubandhādibhiḥ pr̥thagbhūtē vidyāmayē yajñē'vagatē sati vidhiḥ parikalpyatē । dr̥ṣṭaścānuvādasarūpēṣu kalpyamānō vidhiḥ । taduktaṁ – **vacanāni tvapūrvatvāt** (jai.sū.3.5.21) iti । phalaṁ ca **tēṣāmēkaika ēva tāvān yāvānasau pūrvaḥ** (agnirahasyaṁ) ityatidēśāt svakratudvārēṇēṣṭakacitasyāgnēḥ yatphalam, tadēva manaścitādīnāmapi svakratudvārēṇa phalamityavagamyatē ॥48॥

#### atidēśasya pūrvapakṣōpaṣṭambhakatānirāsaḥ

yatpunaratidēśēna tulyakāryatvāvagamātkriyāmayakratvanupravēśō'vagamyata ityuktam, tatrāha –

**403. na sāmānyādapyupalabdhērmr̥tyuvanna hi lōkāpattiḥ ॥ 3–3–49 ॥**

nāvaśyamatidēśādavāntaravyāpārasyāpi tulyatayā bhavitavyam, yēna kriyāmayakratvanupravēśa ēṣāṁ syāt, yasmātkasmāccitsāmānyamātrādatidēśōpalabdhēḥ; upalabhyatē hi **sa ēṣa ēva mr̥tyurya ēṣa ētasminmaṇḍalē puruṣaḥ** (agnirahasyaṁ – 30-5-2) ityādiṣu saṁhartr̥tvādisāmānyamātrādatidēśaḥ; na hi tatra maṇḍalapuruṣasya mr̥tyuvat tallōkāpattiḥ – taddēśaprāptirapi bhavati; ēvamihāpi manaścitādīnāmiṣṭakacitāgnivadbhāvātidēśamātrēṇēṣṭakacitāgnidēśarūpakriyāmayakratvanupravēśēnāpi na bhavitavyam। ata iṣṭakacitāgnēḥ svakratudvārēṇa yatphalaṁ tadēva manaścitādīnāmapi vidyāmayakatudvārēṇa phalamityati-dēśādavagamyatē **॥49 ॥**

#### anantaraśrutasya brāhmaṇasya siddhāntōpaṣṭambhakatvōpapādanam

**404. parēṇa ca śabdasya tādvidhyaṁ bhūyastvāttvanubandhaḥ ॥ 3–3–50 ॥**

parēṇa ca brāhmaṇēnāsyāpi manaścitādyabhidhāyinaḥ śabdasya tādvidhyaṁ –
tadvidhatvam, vidyāmayapratipāditvamavagamyatē; parēṇa hi brāhmaṇēna ayaṁ vāva lōka ēṣō'gnicitastasyāpa ēva pariśritāḥ (agnirahasyaṁ) ityādinā sa yō haitadēvaṁ vēda lōkaṁ pr̥ṇānāmēnaṁ bhūtamētatsarvamabhisampadyatē (agnirahasyaṁ) iti pr̥thakphalā vidyaiva vidhīyatē, tathā vaiśvānaravidyādau ca vidyaiva vidhīyatē। atō'gnirahasyasya kriyaikaviṣayatvaṁ nāsti । ēvaṁ tarhi vidyāmayāḥ manaścitādayō br̥hadāraṇyakē'nubaddhavyāḥ kimarthamihānubadhyantē, tatrōcyatē – bhūyastvāttvanubandhaḥ – iti। manaścitādiṣu sampādanīyānāmagnyaṅgānāṁ bhūyastvāt sannidhāvihānubandhaḥ kr̥taḥ॥ 50॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē pūrvavikalpādhikaraṇam॥20॥**

### 21 śarīrēbhāvādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē śarīrēbhāvādhikaraṇam॥21॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
upāsakakartr̥kaṁ pratyagātmabhūtasya svātmanō'nusandhānam āvirbhūyamānaguṇāṣṭakavatvēna

**405. ēka ātmanaśśarīrē bhāvāt ॥ 3–3–51 ॥**

#### vicāraṇīyaviṣayōpasthāpanam

sarvāsu paravidyāsūpāsyōpāsanasvarūpavadupāsakasvarūpasyāpi jñātavyatvamuktaṁ – **trayāṇāmēva caivamupanyāsaḥ praśnaśca** (bra.sū.1.4.3) iti। vakṣyati cāsya pratyagātmanaḥ paramātmātmakatvēna anusandhānam **ātmēti tūpagacchanti grāhayanti ca** (bra.sū.4.1.3) iti ।

#### vicāraupayikaḥ saṁśayaḥ

kimayaṁ pratyagātmā jñātā kartā bhōktēhāmutra sañcārakṣamō'nusandhēyaḥ, uta prajāpativākyōditāpahatapāpmatvādisvarūpaḥ? ॥

#### sahētukaḥ pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ

kiṁ yuktam? jñātr̥tvādyākāramātra ityēkē manyantē ॥

kutaḥ? asyōpāsakasyātmanaḥ śarīrē bhāvāt; śarīrē vartamānasya tādr̥śamēva rūpam; tāvataivānusandhānēna tatphalasiddhyupapattēśca ॥

#### uktārthē kāmyakarmānuṣṭhātr̥dr̥ṣṭāntīkaraṇam

na hi karmasvadhikr̥tānāṁ svargādiphalārthināṁ jñātr̥tvādyatirēkēṇa phalānubhavadaśāyāṁ yādr̥śaṁ rūpam, tādr̥śaṁ rūpaṁ sādhanānuṣṭhānadaśāyāmanusandhātavyam, tāvataiva sādhanānuṣṭhānatatphalayōssiddhēḥ atiriktānusandhānē prayōjanābhāvāt; tadaviśēṣādihāpi tathaiva।

#### phalasiddhēḥ anupapattiśaṅkāparihārau

nanu cātra **yathākraturasminlōkē puruṣō bhavati tathētaḥ prētya bhavati** (chāṁ.3.14.1) iti viśēṣavacanādapahatapāpmatvādyākāra ēvānusandhātavya ityavagamyatē; naivam, taṁ yathāyathōpāsatē (mudgala.upa.3) ityupāsyaviṣayatvāttasya॥

#### siddhāntaparaṁ sūtraṁ tadvivaraṇaṁ ca

**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvaṁ prāptē pracakṣmahē - 

**406. +++(dhyēyaḥ saṁsārāvasthā-)+++vyatirēkas tad bhāva-bhāvitvān, na tu +++(saṁsārāvasthā)+++, +++(yathāvasthita-brahma-)+++upalabdhivat ॥ 3–3–52 ॥**

**vi॰pra॰**—
**na tv** ētad asti –  
yaj jñātr̥tvādy-ākāra ēvānusandhēya iti; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
asyātmanas saṁsāra-daśāyāḥ mōkṣa-daśāyāṁ yō vyatirēkaḥ,  
sō'pahata-pāpmatvādikō 'nusandhēyaḥ; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
asya mōkṣa-daśāyāṁ yādr̥śaṁ rūpaṁ,  
tādr̥g-rūpa ēvōpāsana-vēlāyām ātmā 'nusandhēya ityarthaḥ। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
kutaḥ? **tad-bhāva-bhāvitvāt** = tad-rūpāpattēḥ; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
**yathākraturasmin lōkē puruṣō bhavati tathētaḥ prētya bhavati** (chā.3.14.1)  

**vi॰pra॰**—
**taṁ yathā-yathōpāsatē tathaiva bhavati** (mudgala.upa.3.1) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
iti yathōpāsanam ēva hi prāptiḥ śrūyatē। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
na ca "para--sva-rūpa-mātra-viṣayam ēvēdam"  
iti vaktuṁ śakyatē,   
pratyag-ātmanō 'py upāsya-bhūta--para-brahma-śarīratayōpāsyakōṭi-nikṣiptatvāt । 

**vi॰pra॰**—
ataḥ prajā-pati-vākyōdita- -+apahata-pāpmatvādi-guṇaka- pratyag-ātma-śarīra-paramātmōpāsanasya  
tathā-rūpam ēva prāpyam  
ity usktaṁ bhavati।

#### prāpyākārasyaivā'nusandhēyatā

**vi॰pra॰**—
ata ēva 

> ēvaṁ-kratur hāmuṁ lōkaṁ prētyābhisambhavitāsmi (agnirahasyaṁ) 

ity ucyatē। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tasmāt pratyag-ātmā prāpyākāra ēvānusandhēyaḥ। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
**upalabdhivat** –  

> yathā brahmōpalabdhir vihitā  
yathāvasthita-brahma--sva-rūpa-viṣayā,  
tathā''tmōpalabdhir api  
yathā'vasthitātma-svarūpa-viṣayā 

ity arthaḥ ।

#### kāmyānuṣṭhātuḥ dr̥ṣṭāntatvasya vaiṣamyam

karmasvātmasvarūpānusandhānaṁ karmāṅgam; **yajēta svargakāmaḥ** (yaju.2.5.5) iti karmānuṣṭhānamēva hi phalāya cōpadyatē। dēhātiriktajñātr̥tvādyākārātmāvagatiḥ kālāntarabhāviphalasādhana-karmādhikārārthēti tāvanmātramēva tatrāpēkṣitamiti na kiñcidapahīnam ॥ 52॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē śarīrēbhāvādhikaraṇam॥21॥**

### 22 aṅgāvabaddhādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē aṅgāvabaddhādhikaraṇam ॥22॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
udgīthādyaṅgāśrayāṇām upāsanānām udgīthādivat sarvaśākhāsthakratuṣvapyanvayaḥ

**407. aṅgāvabaddhāstu na śākhāsu hi prativēdam ॥ 3–3–53 ॥**

#### vicāraṇīyaviṣayōpasthāpanam

**ōmityētadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta** (chā.1.1.1) lōkēṣu **pañcavidhaṁ sāmōpāsīta** (chā.2.2.1) **ukthamukthamiti vai prajā vadanti tadidamēvōktham iyamēva pr̥thivī** (aitarēya ā.2.1.2) **ayaṁ vāva lōka ēṣō'gnicitaḥ** (agnirahasyaṁ) ityēvamādyāḥ kratvaṅgāśrayāḥ upāsanāḥ bhavanti ।

#### vicāraupayikaḥ saṁśayaḥ

tāḥ kiṁ yāsu śākhāsu śrūyantē, tāsvēva niyatāḥ, uta sarvāsu śākhāsūdgīthādiṣu sambadhyanta iti vicāraḥ।

#### adhikaraṇārambhākṣēpaśaṅkānirāsaḥ

sarvavēdāntapratyayatvē sthitē'pi prativēdaṁ svarabhēdādudgīthādayō bhidyanta iti tatra tatra vyavatiṣṭhēranniti yuktā śaṅkā ।

#### sayuktikaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ

kiṁ yuktam? vyavatiṣṭhēranniti । kutaḥ? **udgīthamupāsīta** (chāṁ.1.1.1) iti sāmānyēnōdgīthasambandhitayā śrutāyāstasyāmēva śākhāyāṁ svaraviśēṣayuktasya udgīthaviśēṣasya sannidhānāttasminnēva viśēṣē paryavasānaṁ yuktamiti । ēvamādyāstāsvēva śākhāsu vyavatiṣṭhēranniti॥

#### siddhāntārthaḥ sūtrārthavivr̥tyā

ēvaṁ prāptē pracakṣmahē – aṅgāvabaddhāstu – iti। tu śabdaḥ pakṣaṁ vyāvartayati; nahyudgīthādyaṅgāvabaddhā upāsanāstāsvēva śākhāsu vyavatiṣṭhēran, api tu prativēdaṁ sambadhyēran; sarvāsu śākhāsvityarthaḥ । hi śabdō hētau। yasmācchrutyaivōdgīthādyaṅgamātrāvabaddhāḥ, tasmādyatrōdgīthādayaḥ, tatra sarvatra sambadhyēran।

#### svarabhēdāyattōdgīthabhēdatō vyavasthāyā nirāsaḥ

yadyapi svarabhēdēnōdgīthavyaktayō bhidyantē; tathāpi sāmānyēnōdgīthaśrutyā sarvā vyaktayassannihitā iti na kvacidvyavasthāyāṁ pramāṇamasti । sarvaśākhāpratyayanyāyēna ca sarvāsu śākhāsu kraturēkaḥ। atassarvāsu śākhāsvēkasya kratōssannidhānāt kratvaṅgabhūtōdgīthādayō'pi sannihitā iti naikasya sannidhiviśēṣō'stīti na vyavasthā ॥ 53॥

#### mantrādidr̥ṣṭāntēna śāstrāntarīyakratvaṅgōdgīthādiṣvapyupāsanānvayaḥ

**408. mantrādivadvā'virōdhaḥ ॥ 3–3–54 ॥**

vāśabdaścārthē; ādiśabdēna jātiguṇasaṅkhyāsādr̥śyakramadravyakarmāṇi gr̥hyantē; yathā mantrādīnāmēkaikaśākhāsvāmnātānāmapi śēṣiṇaḥ kratōssarvaśākhāsvēkatvēna yathāyathaṁ śrutyādibhissarvāsu śākhāsu viniyōgō na virudhyatē; tadvadihāpyavirōdhaḥ ॥54॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē aṅgāvabaddhādhikaraṇam॥22॥**

### 23 bhūmajyāyastvādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē bhūmajyāyastvādhikaraṇam॥23॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
vaiśvānaravidyāyāṁ trailōkyaśarīrasya vaiśvānarātmanaḥ upāsanaṁ, samastasyaiva

**409. bhūmnaḥ kratuvajjyāyastvaṁ tathā hi darśayati ॥ 3–3–55 ॥**

#### vaiśvānaravidyāyāṁ vicāraṇīyō viṣayaḥ

**prācīnaśālā aupamanyavaḥ** (chāṁ.5.11.1) ityārabhya vaiśvānaravidyā āmnātā। tatra vaiśvānaraḥ paramātmā trailōkyaśarīra upāsyaśśrutaḥ svarlōkādityavāyvākāśāppr̥thivyavayavaḥ; tatra dyaurmūrdhā, ādityaścakṣuḥ, vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ, ākāśassandēhaḥ – madhyakāya ityartha; āpō vastiḥ; pr̥thivī pādāvityavayavaviśēṣāḥ।

#### vicāraupayikaḥ saṁśayaḥ

tatra saṁśayaḥ – kimasya trailōkyaśarīrasya vyastasyōpāsanaṁ kartavyam, uta vyastasya samastasya ca, atha samastasyaivēti।

#### sayuktikaḥ pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ

kiṁ yuktam? vyastasyēti; kutaḥ? upakramē vyastōpāsanōpadēśāt। tathāhyupadiśyatē aupamanyavādayaḥ kilōddālakaṣaṣṭhāḥ kēkayamaśvapatimupasadya
**ātmānamēvēmaṁ vaiśvānaraṁ sampratyadhyēṣi tamēva nō brūhi** (chāṁ.5.11.6) iti prapacchuḥ। sa ca tēbhyaḥ pratyēkaṁ svōpāsyān dyuprabhr̥tīnuktavadbhyō mūrdhādiṣu vyastēṣūpāsanaṁ tatra tatra phalaṁ cōktavān attyannaṁ, paśyati priyaṁ, bhavatyasya brahmavarcasaṁ kulē**, ya ētamēvamātmānaṁ vaiśvānaramupāstē mūrdhā tvēṣa ātmana iti ēṣa vai sutējā ātmā vaiśvānaraḥ** (chāṁ.5.12.2) ityādinā । tēṣutēṣūpāsanēṣūpāsyasya vaiśvānaratvaṁ cāha। atō vyastasyōpāsanaṁ kartavyam। paratra **yastvētamēvaṁ prādēśamātramabhivimānamātmānaṁ vaiśvānaramupāstē** (chā.5.18.1) iti। dyuprabhr̥tipradēśāvacchinnamātrē vaiśvānarē uktasya mūrdhādyupāsanasya samāsēnōpasaṁhāra ityavagantavyam।

#### vikalpitadvitīyāṁśasya upapādanam

apara āha – ēvamēva samastasyāpyupāsanaṁ kāryamiti, pr̥thakphalanirdēśāt – **yastvētamēvaṁ prādēśamātramabhivimānamātmānaṁ vaiśvānaramupāstē sa sarvēṣu lōkēṣu sarvēṣu bhūtēṣu sarvēṣvātmasvannamatti** (chā.5.18.1) iti । nacaitāvatā vākyabhēdaḥ; yathā bhūmavidyōpakramē nāmādyupāsanaṁ tattatphalañcābhidhāya ēṣa tu vā **ativadati yassatyēnātivadati** (chā.7.1.1) ityādinā bhūmavidyāmupadiśya
**sa svarāḍ bhavati tasya sarvēṣu lōkēṣu kāmacārō bhavati** (chā.7.25.2) iti tatphalañca vyapidaśati; tatra bhūmavidyāparatvē'pi vākyasya nāmādyavāntarōpāsanaṁ tattatphalaṁ cāṅgīkriyatē, tathā ihāpīti ॥

#### sūtrārthavivr̥tyā siddhāntavarṇanam

ēvaṁ prāptē'bhidhīyatē – bhūmnō jyāyastvamiti । bhūmnaḥ – vipulasya samastasyaiva, jyāyastvaṁ prāmāṇikatvamityarthaḥ; ēkavākyatvāvagatēḥ। tathā hi **prācīnaśālā aupanyavaḥ** (chā.5.11.1,2) ityupakramya **uddālakō ha vai bhagavantō'yamāruṇissamprati imamātmānaṁ vaiśvānaramadhyēti taṁ hantābhyāgacchāma** (chāṁ.5.11.2) iti vaiśvānarātmabr̥ubhutsayā aupamanyavādayaḥ pañca maharṣayaḥ tamuddālakamupētya tatra vaiśvānarātmavēdanamalabhamānāstēna ca sahāśvapatiṁ kēkayaṁ vaiśvānarātmavēdinamupasaṅgamya **ātmānamēvēmaṁ vaiśvānaraṁ sampratyadhyēṣi tamēva nō brūhi** (chā.5.11.6) iti pr̥ṣṭvā tatsakāśāt paramātmānaṁ vaiśvānaraṁ svarlōkādipr̥thivyantaśarīramupāsyamavagamya tatphalaṁ ca sarvalōkasarvabhūtasarvātmānnabhūtabrahmānubhavamavagatavanta ityupasaṁhāratō vākyasyaikatvamavagamyatē । ēvamēkavākyatvē'vagatē satyavayavaviśēṣēṣūpāstivacanaṁ phalanirdēśaśca samastōpāsanaikadēśānuvādamātram iti niścīyatē।

#### sūtrōktadr̥ṣṭāntavarṇanam

kratuvat – yathā **vaiśvānaraṁ dvādaśakapālaṁ nirvapēt putrē jātē** (yaju.2.2.5u) iti vihitasyaiva kratōrēkadēśāḥ
**yadaṣṭākapālō bhavati** (yaju.2.2.5 anu) ityādibhiranūdyantē; tathā samastōpāsanamēva nyāyyam, na vyastōpāsanam । tathā hi darśayatīyaṁ śrutiḥ vyastōpāsanē anarthaṁ bruvatī **mūrdhā tē vyapitaṣyadyanmāṁ nāgamiṣyaḥ** (chā.5-12-2) iti **andhō'bhaviṣyō yanmāṁ nāgamiṣyaḥ** (chāṁ.5.13.2) ityādikā ।

#### pūrvapakṣōktabhūmavidyāgataikadēśōpāsanasāmyanirāsaḥ

ata idamapyapāstaṁ, yannāmādyupāsanasāmyamuktam । tatra hi nāmādyupāsanēṣvanarthō na śrutaḥ, nāmādyupāsanēbhyō bhūmōpāsanasyātiśayitaphalatvaṁ śrutam **ēṣa tu vā ativadati yassatyēnātivadati** (chā.7.16.1) iti। tata ēva tatra bhūmavidyāparatvē'pi vākyasya nāmādyupāsanānāṁ saphalānāṁ vivakṣitatvam; anyathā'tiśayitaphalatvanimittātivādēna bhūmavidyāstutyanupapattēḥ, atassamastōpāsanamēva nyāyyam ॥55॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē bhūmajyāyastvādhikaraṇam॥23॥**

### 24 śabdādibhēdādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē śabdādibhēdādhikaraṇam॥24॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
brahmaprāptyēkaphalānāmapi vēdāntōditānāṁ vidyānāṁ śabdādibhēdataḥ svarūpabhēdaḥ

**410. nānā śabdādibhēdāt ॥ 3–3–56 ॥**

#### vicāraṇīyārthōpasthāpanam

iha brahmavidyāssarvāḥ brahmaprāptirūpamōkṣaikaphalāḥ sadvidyābhūmavidyādaharavidyōpakōsala-vidyāśāṇḍilyavidyāvaiśvānaravidyānandamayavidyākṣaravidyādikā ēkaśākhāgatāśśākhāntaragatāśca udāharaṇam; anyāḥ prāṇādyēkaviṣayaphalāśca ।

#### vicāraupayikaḥ saṁśayaḥ

kimatra vidyaikyam, uta vidyābhēda iti saṁśayyatē।

#### karmakāṇḍōktanyāyataḥ paunaruktyaśaṅkāyā nirāsaḥ

atraivāsāṁ parasparabhēdē samarthitē satyēkasyā daharavidyādikāyāssarvavēdāntapratyayanyāyaḥ।

#### pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ sayuktikaḥ

kiṁ yuktam? vidyaikyamiti। kutaḥ? vēdyasya brahmaṇa ēkatvāt; vēdyaṁ hi vidyāyā rūpam; atō rūpaikyādvidyaikyamiti॥

#### sūtrārthavivaraṇataḥ siddhāntaḥ

ēvaṁ prāptē'bhidhīyatē nānā – iti। nānābhūtā vidyāḥ; kutaḥ? śabdādibhēdāt – ādiśabdēnābhyāsasaṅkhyāguṇaprakriyānāmadhēyāni gr̥hyantē; śabdāntarādibhiratra vidhēyabhēdahētavaḥ anubandhabhēdāḥ dr̥śyantē ।

#### sarvēṣāmupāsanānāṁ pratyayaisvarūpatvē'pi vidyānāṁ bhēdōpapattiḥ

yadyapi vēdōpāsītētyādayaḥ śabdāḥ pratyayāvr̥ttyabhidhāyinaḥ; pratyayāśca brahmaikaviṣayāḥ; tathā'pi tattatprakaraṇōditajagadēkakāraṇatvāpahatapāpmatvādi-viśēṣaṇaviśiṣṭabrahmaviṣayapratyayāvr̥ttya-vabōdhinaḥ pratyayāvr̥ttirūpāḥ vidyāḥ bhindanti। brahmaprāptirūpaphalasambandhyupāsana-viśēṣābhidhāyīni ca nirākāṅkṣāṇi vākyāni pratiprakaraṇaṁ vilakṣaṇavidyābhidhāyīnīti niścīyatē।

#### pūrvakāṇḍatō'vagatasya punarabhidhānaucityam

asminnarthē **śabdāntarē karmabhēdaḥ** (jai.sū.1-1-2) ityādibhiḥ pūrvakāṇḍōditaissūtraissiddhē'pi punariha pratipādanaṁ vēdāntavākyāni
avadhēyajñānaparāṇīti kudr̥ṣṭinirasanāya। atō vidyābhēda iti sthitam ॥ 56 ॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē śabdādibhēdādhikaraṇam ॥24॥**

### 25 vikalpādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē vikalpādhikaraṇam ॥25॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
brahmaprāptyartham ēkaikasyā ēva vidyāyāḥ vikalpēnānuṣṭhēyatā,na samuccayēna sarvasyā api 

**411. vikalpō'viśiṣṭaphalatvāt ॥ 3–3–57 ॥**

#### saṅgatisaṁśayayōḥ pradarśanam

brahmaprāptiphalānāṁ sadvidyādaharavidyādīnāṁ nānātvamuktam; idānīmāsāṁ vidyānāmēkasmin puruṣē prayōjanavattvēna samuccayō'pi sambhavati, uta prayōjanābhāvādvikalpa ēvēti viśayē –

#### sayuktikaḥ pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ

kiṁ yuktam? samuccayō'pi sambhavatīti; kutaḥ ēkaphalānāṁ bhinnaśāstrārthānāmapi samuccayadarśanāt। dr̥śyatē hyēkasyaiva svargādēssādhanānāmagnihōtradarśapūrṇamāsādīnāṁ tasyaiva svargasya bhūyastvāpēkṣayaikatra puruṣē samuccayaḥ; ēvamihāpi brahmānubhavabhūyastvāpēkṣayā samuccayō'pi sambhavatīti॥

#### sūtratassiddhāntōpapādanam

ēvaṁ prāptē pracakṣmahē – vikalpa ēva; na samuccayassambhavatīti। kutaḥ?
aviśiṣṭaphalatvāt – sarvāsāṁ hi brahmavidyānāmanavadhikātiśayānandabrahmānubhavaḥ phalamaviśiṣṭaṁ śrūyatē – brahmavidāpnōti param (tai.āna.1.1) **sa ēkō brahmaṇa ānandaḥ śrōtriyasya cākāmahatasya** (tai.āna.8.4) **yadā paśyaḥ paśyatē rukmavarṇaṁ kartāramīśaṁ puruṣaṁ brahmayōnim । tadā vidvān puṇyapāpē vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṁ sāmyamupaiti** (mu.3.1.3) ityādibhyaḥ।

#### brahmānandasya phalatvadarśanam

brahma hi svasya parasya ca svayamanubhūyamānamanavadhikātiśayānandaṁ bhavati । sa ca tādr̥śō brahmānubhava ēkayā vidyayā'vāpyatē cēt – kimanyayēti na samuccayasambhavaḥ। svargādērhi dēśataḥ kālataḥ svarūpataśca parimitatvēna tatra dēśādyapēkṣayā bhūyastvasambhavāt tadarthinassamuccayassambhavati; iha tu
tadviparītasvarūpē brahmaṇi tanna sambhavati। sarvāśca vidyāḥ brahmānubhavavirōdhyanādi-karmāvidyānirasanamukhēna brahmaprāptiphalā ityaviśiṣṭaphalatvātsarvāsāṁ vikalpa ēva ॥57॥

#### kāmyaphalāsu kriyāsu samuccayasambhavaḥ

brahmaprāptivyatiriktaphalāstu vidyāssvargādiphalakarmavadyathēṣṭaṁ vikalpēran, samuccayēranvā, tāsāṁ parimitaphalatvēna bhūyastvāpēkṣāsambhavāt । tadāha –

**412. kāmyāstu yathākāmaṁ samuccīyēranna vā pūrvahētvabhāvāt ॥ 3–3–58 ॥**

aparimitaphalatvābhāvādityarthaḥ ॥58॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē vikalpādhikaraṇam॥25॥**

### 26 yathāśrayabhāvādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē yathāśrayabhāvādhikaraṇam॥26॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
udgīthādyaṅgāśritānāmupāsanānāṁ pr̥thakphalatāyāḥ udgīthādyanaṅgatāyāśca darśanāt kratuṣūpādānāniyamō dr̥ḍhaiva

**413. aṅgēṣu yathāśrayabhāvaḥ ॥ 3–3–59 ॥**

#### viṣayasaṁśayayōḥ pradarśanam

udgīthādikratvaṅgēṣvāśritāḥ **ōmityētadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta** (chā.1.1.1) ityādikāḥ vidyāḥ kimudgīthādivatkratvarthatayā kratuṣu niyamēnōpādēyāḥ, uta gōdōhanādivatpuruṣārthatayā yathākāmamiti viśayē –

#### pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ

niyamēnōpādēyā iti yuktam ।

#### adhikaraṇasyāsya kr̥takaratvaśaṅkāparihāraḥ

nanu cāsāṁ puraṣārthatvēnāniyamaḥ pratipāditaḥ
**tannirdhāraṇāniyamastaddr̥ṣṭēḥ pr̥thagdhyapratibandhaḥ phalam** (śārī.3.3.41) ityatra । satyam; tadēva draḍhayituṁ kaiścilliṅgadarśanairyuktyā cākṣipyatē । tatra hi **tēnōbhau kurutaḥ** (chā.1.1.10) ityaniyamadarśanāt pr̥thakphalatvamuktam; upāsanāśrayabhūtōdgīthādivat upāsanānāmapyaṅgatayōpādānaniyamē bahavō hētava upalabhyantē; na hyatra gōdōhanēna paśukāmasya praṇayēt ityādivadupāsanāvidhivākyē phalasambandhaḥ śrūyatē; **udgīthamupāsīta** (chā.1.1.1) ityudgīthādisambandhitayaivōpāsanaṁ pratīyatē।

#### svavākyē phalasambandhāśravaṇaspaṣṭīkaraṇam

**yadēva vidyayā karōti śraddhayōpaniṣadā tadēva vīryavattaram** (chā.1.1.10) iti vartamānōpadēśarūpavākyāntarāddhi phalasambandhō jñāyatē; svavākyēnaivāvyabhicarita-kratusambandhi udgīthādisambandhēna nirjñātakratvaṅgabhāvasya vākyāntarasthavartamānaphalasambandhanirdēśaḥ arthavādamātraṁ syāt, apāpaślōkaśravaṇādivat।

atō yathōdgīthādaya upāsanāśrayāḥ kratvaṅgatayā prayōgavidhinā niyamēnōpādīyantē; tathā tadāśritāścōpāsanāstanmukhēna kratvaṅgabhūtā iti niyamēnōpādēyā ēva॥59॥

#### uktārthē śrautasya vidhānasya niyāmakatvam

**414. śiṣṭēśca ॥ 3–3–60 ॥**

śiṣṭiḥ – śāsanam, vidhānamityarthaḥ। **udgīthamupāsīta** (chāṁ.1.1.1) ityudgīthāṅgatayōpāsana-vidhānāccōpādānaniyamaḥ। gōdōhanēna paśukāmasya praṇayēt ityādivadvidhivākyē adhikārāntarāśravaṇāt udgīthāṅgabhāva ēva hi vidhēya iti gamyatē ॥60॥

#### śrautasya durudgīthasamādhānavacanasya niyamajñāpakatvam

**415. samāhārāt ॥ 3–3–61 ॥**

hōtr̥ṣadanāddhaivāpi **durudgīthamanusamāharati** (chāṁ.1.5.5) ityupāsanasya samāhāraniyamō dr̥śyatē। durudgīthaṁ vēdanavihīnamudgītham । vēdanahānāvanyēna samādhānaṁ bruvattasya niyamēnōpādānaṁ darśayati ॥61॥

#### sōpāsanapraṇavānuvr̥ttēḥ upāsanānuvr̥ttijñāpakatvam

**416. guṇasādhāraṇyaśrutēśca ॥ 3–3–62 ॥**

upāsanaguṇasya upāsanāśrayasya praṇavasya sōpāsanasya **tēnēyaṁ trayī vidyā vartatē ōmityāśrāvayatyōmiti śaṁsatyōmityudgāyati** (chā.1-1-9) iti sādhāraṇyaśrutēśca upāsanasamāhārō gamyatē । **tēna** (chā.1.1.9) iti prakr̥taparāmarśātsōpāsana ēva praṇavassarvatra sañcarati । ata upāsanasya praṇavasahabhāvaniyamadarśanācca udgīthādyupāsanānām udgīthādivat niyamēnōpādānam॥

#### siddhāntasūtrārambhaḥ

iti prāpta ucyatē –

**417. na vā tatsahabhāvāśrutēḥ ॥ 3–3–63 ॥**

na caitadasti – yadudgīthādyupāsanānāṁ kratuṣūdgīthādivadupādānaniyamaḥ – iti। kutaḥ? tatsahabhāvāśrutēḥ – udgīthāṅgabhāvāśrutērityarthaḥ। aṅgabhāvē hi sahabhāvaniyamō bhavati ।

#### aṅgatvavirōdhyaṁśōpapādanam

yadyapi **udgīthamupāsīta** (chā.1.1.1) ityasmin padasamudāyē'dhikārāntaraṁ na pratīyatē; tathāpi tadanantaramēva **yadēva vidyayā karōti śraddhayōpaniṣadā tadēva vīryavattaraṁ bhavati** (chā.1.1.10) iti vidyāyāḥ kratuvīryavattaratvaṁ prati sādhanabhāvaḥ pratipādyatē । tēna kratuphalātpr̥thagbhūtaphalasādhanabhūtā vidyā **udgīthamupāsīta** (chā.1.1.1) iti kartavyatayā vidhīyatē। kratuphalātpr̥thagbhūtaphalasādhanatayā avagatasyōpāsanasya kratvaṅgabhūtōdgīthāṅgatayā viniyōgō nōpapadyatē।

#### upāsanaṁ pratyudgīthasya āśrayatāmātram

atha upāsanasyāśrayāpēkṣāyāṁ sannihitaḥ udgīthaḥ āśrayamātraṁ bhavati। udgīthaśca kratvaṅgabhūta iti kratuprayuktōdgīthādyāśrayē upāsanē kratvadhikāriṇa ēva kratōrvīryavattaratvēcchā-nimittamidamadhikārāntaramiti na kratuṣu tadupādānaniyamaḥ। vīryavattaratvaṁ ca kratuphalasya prabalakarmāntaraphalēnāpratibandha ityuktam। kratōravilambitaphalatvamityarthaḥ।

#### parṇatāvidhivailakṣaṇyasya śrutyā spaṣṭīkaraṇam

parṇatādīnāṁ tu **yadēva vidyayā karōti tadēva vīryavattaraṁ bhavati** (chāṁ.1.2.10) iti vidyāyāḥ phalasādhanatvavadapāpaślōkaśravaṇādiphalaṁ prati sākṣātsādhanabhāvō na śruta iti kratvaṅgabhūtajuhvādyaṅgatayā viniyōgāvirōdhāttadaṅgabhūtānāṁ phalāntarasādhanabhāvakalpanānupapattēstatra phalaśrutirarthavādamātraṁ syāt ॥63॥

#### upāsanōpādānāniyamasya śrutyā spaṣṭīkaraṇam

**418. darśanācca॥ 3–3–64 ॥**

darśayati ca śrutirupāsanōpādānāniyamam, **ēvaṁ viddha vai brahmā yajñaṁ yajamānaṁ sarvāścartvijō'bhirakṣati** (chā.4.17.10) iti brahmaṇō vēdanēna sarvēṣāṁ rakṣaṇaṁ bruvatī । udgātr̥prabhr̥tīnāṁ vēdanasyāniyamē satyētadupapadyatē। anēna liṅgēna pūrvōktānāṁ samāhārādiliṅgānāṁ prāyikatvamavagamyatē। atō'niyama ēvēti sthitam ॥64॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē yathāśrayabhāvādhikaraṇam ॥26॥**

**iti śrībhagavadrāmānujaviracitē śārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē tr̥tīyasyādhyāyasya tr̥tīyaḥ pādaḥ॥3॥**

## +4 aṅgāni

**śrībhagavadrāmānujaviracitēśrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē**

**tr̥tīyē sādhanādhyāyē – caturthaḥ aṅgapādaḥ**

### pādārthaḥ – mōkṣōpāyatayā vēdāntavihitavidyāṅgabhūtakarmādiviṣayiṇī cintā
### 01 puruṣārthādhikaraṇam

**puruṣārthādhikaraṇam॥1॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
karmāṅgakādupāsanādēva paramapuruṣārthāvāptiḥ, na tu vēdanāṅgakāt karmaṇaḥ॥

īśāvāsyavidyāvicāraḥ 3-4-33।

**vi॰pra॰**—
**419. puruṣārthō 'taś +++(←vidyātaḥ)+++ - śabdād iti bādarāyaṇaḥ ॥ 3–4–1 ॥**

**English**—
1. The benefit to man results from thence, on account of scriptural statement; thus Bādarāyaṇa thinks.

#### saṅgatiḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
guṇōpasaṁhārānupasaṁhāra-phalā vidyaikatva-nānātva-cintā kr̥tā; 

**English**—
We have concluded the investigation into the oneness or diverseness of meditations – the result of which is to indicate in which cases the special points mentioned in several meditations have to be combined, and in which not. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
idānīṁ vidyātaḥ puruṣārthaḥ,  
uta vidyāṅgakātkarmaṇa iti cintyatē।

**English**—
A further point now to be investigated is whether that advantage to the meditating devotee, which is held to accrue to him from the meditation, results from the meditation directly, or from works of which the meditations are subordinate members.

#### vidyātaḥ puruṣārthaḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
kiṁ yuktam? ataḥ – vidyātaḥ puruṣārtha  
iti bhagavān bādarāyaṇō manyatē;

**English**—
--The Reverend Bādarāyaṇa holds the former view. The benefit to man results from thence, i.e. from the meditation,

**vi॰pra॰**—
kutaḥ? śabdāt – 

**English**—
because Scripture declares this to be so. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
dr̥śyatē hyaupinaṣadaśśabdō vidyātaḥ puruṣārthaṁ bruvan 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **brahmavidāpnōti param** (tai.ā.1.anu)

**English**—
'He who knows Brahman reaches the Highest' (Taitt. Up. II, 1, 1); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **vēdāhamētaṁ puruṣaṁ mahāntamādityavarṇaṁ tamasaḥ parastāt। tamēvaṁ vidvānamr̥ta iha bhavati। nānyaḥ panthā vidyatē'yanāya** (pu.sū.) 

**English**—
'I know that great Person of sun-like lustre beyond the darkness. A man who knows him truly passes over death; there is no other path to go' (Śvet. Up. III, 8); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **yathā nadyaḥ syandamānās samudrē  
> astaṁ gacchanti nāmarūpē vihāya।  
> tathā vidvān nāmarūpād vimuktaḥ  
> parātparaṁ puruṣam upaiti divyam**   
> (mu.3.28) 

ityādi॥1॥

**English**—
> 'As the flowing rivers disappear in the sea, losing their name and their form,  
> thus a man who possesses knowledge, freed from name and form, goes to the divine Person who is greater than the great' (Mu. Up. III, 2, 8).

#### pūrvapakṣaḥ 

##### vidyātaḥ kartr̥-saṁskārō 'rthavādaḥ, śēṣatvāt

**vi॰pra॰**—
atra pūrvapakṣī pratyavatiṣṭhatē –

**English**—
Against this view the Pūrvapakshin raises an objection.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> 420. śēṣatvāt puruṣārthavādō  
yathā 'nyēṣv 

iti jaiminiḥ ॥ 3–4–2 ॥

**English**—
2\. On account of (the Self) standing in a complementary relation, they are arthavādas, as in other cases; thus Jaimini opines.

**vi॰pra॰**—
naitadēvam – yad vidyātaḥ puruṣārthāvāptiś śabdād avagamyatē – iti। 

**English**—
What has been said as to Scripture intimating that a beneficial result is realised through the meditations by themselves is untenable. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
na hy ēṣaḥ 

> **brahmavid āpnōti param** (tai.ā.1) 

ity-ādi-śabdō  
vēdanāt puruṣārthāvāptim avagamayati,  
karmasu kartr̥-bhūtasyā'tmanō yāthātmya-vēdana-pratipādana-paratvāt। 

**English**—
For texts such as 'he who knows Brahman reaches the Highest' do not teach that the highest aim of man is attained through knowledge; their purport rather is to inculcate knowledge of Truth on the part of a Self which is the agent in works prescribed. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
ataḥ kartus saṁskāra-dvārēṇa  
vidyāyāḥ kratu-śēṣatvāt,  
tatra phala-śrutir arthavāda-mātram;  
yathā'nyēṣu dravyādiṣu –  
iti jaiminir ācāryō manyatē। 

**English**—
Knowledge, therefore, stands in a complementary relation to sacrificial works, in so far as it imparts to the acting Self a certain mystic purification; and the texts which declare special results of knowledge, therefore, must be taken as mere arthavādas. 'As in the case of other things; so Jaimini thinks,' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tad uktaṁ 

> **dravya-guṇa-saṁskāra-karmasu  
> parārthatvāt phala-śrutir arthavādas syāt**  
> (jai.mī.sū.4.3.1) 

iti।

**English**—
i.e. as Jaimini holds that in the case of substances, qualities, and so on, the scriptural declaration of results is of the nature of arthavāda.

##### kartrupadēśa-para ēva
###### ākṣēpaḥ - na kartrupadēśaparāḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
> nanu ca karmasu kartur jīvād anyō  
> mumukṣubhiḥ prāpyatayā vēdāntēṣu vēdya upidaśyata  
> iti prāgēvōpapāditaṁ 

**English**—
> -- But it has been shown before that  
> the Vedānta-texts represent as the object to be attained, by those desirous of Release,  
> on the basis of the knowledge imparted by them,  
> something different from the individual Self engaged in action; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **nētarō'nupapattēḥ** (bra.sū..1.1.17) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **bhēdavyapadēśācca** (śārī.1-1-18) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **anupapattēstu na śārīraḥ** (bra.sū.1.2.3) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **itara-parāmarśāt sa iti cēnnāsambhavāt** (śārī.1-3-17) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> ityēvamādibhissūtraiḥ; 

**English**—
> cp. on this point Sū. I, 1, 15; I, 3, 5; I, 2, 3; I, 3, 18. And Sū. II, 1, 22 and others have refuted the view that Brahman is to be considered as non-different from the personal soul, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> tad ēva 
> 
> > brahma "tat tvam asy"-ādi-sāmānādhikaraṇyēna jīvād anatiriktam 
> 
> ity-ētad api  
> **adhikaṁ tu bhēdanirdēśāt** (bra.sū.2.1.22) ity ēvam-ādibhir nirastam; 

**English**—
because in texts such as 'thou art that' it is exhibited in co-ordination with the latter. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> sāmānādhikaraṇya-nirdēśaśca  
> **aitadātmyamidaṁ sarvaṁ** (chā.6.8.7)  
**sarvaṁ khalvidaṁ brahma** (chā.3.14.1)  
> iti cētanācētanasādhāraṇaḥ  
>
> **yaḥ pr̥thivyāṁ tiṣṭhan** (br̥.5.7.3)  
> **ya ātmani tiṣṭhan** (br̥.6.3.22) ity-ādinā 'vagata-tat-tad-ātmatayā 'vasthiti-nibandhanaḥ

**English**—
> And other Sūtras have proved that Brahman must, on the basis of numerous scriptural texts, be recognised as the inner Self of all things material and immaterial. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> iti 
>
> > **avasthitēr iti kāśakr̥tsnaḥ** (bra.sū.6.4.22) 
>
> ityādibhir upapāditam; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> tatkathaṁ karmasu kartur ātmanō yāthātmyōpadēśa-parā vēdānta-śabdā  
> iti vidyāyāḥ karmāṅgatvaṁ pratipādyatē?।

**English**—
> How then can it be said that the Vedānta-texts merely mean to give instruction as to the true nature of the active individual soul, and that hence all meditation is merely subservient to sacrificial works?--

###### parihāraḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
ucyatē – vēdāntavākyēṣv ēva  
vidyāyāḥ karma-prādhānyaṁ sūcayadbhir liṅgaiḥ  
tad-upabr̥ṁhita-+++(jīva-brahma-)+++sāmānādhikaraṇya-nirdēśēna ca  
vēdānta-śabdā dēhātirikta-jīva-svarūpa-yāthātmyōpadēśaparāḥ  
iti balād abhyupagamanīyam

**English**—
On the strength of numerous inferential marks, the Pūrvapakshin replies, which prove that in the Vedānta-texts all knowledge (~~meditation~~) is really viewed as subordinate to meditation (~~knowledge~~),  
and of the declarations of co-ordination of Brahman and the individual soul (which must be taken to imply that the two are essentially of the same nature),  
we cannot help forming the conclusion that the real purport of the Vedānta-texts is to tell us of the true nature of the individual soul in so far as different from its body.

**vi॰pra॰**—
iti pūrvapakṣiṇō'bhiprāyaḥ।

##### vidyā-kr̥ta-saṁskārasya kratunaiva sambandhaḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
> nanu ca kartr̥-saṁskāra-mukhēna  
> vidyāyāḥ kratv-anupravēśō na śakyatē vaktum,  
> kartur laukika-vaidika-sādhāraṇatvēna  
> avyabhicarita-kratu-sambandhitvābhāvāt  
> +++(laukika-karmōcitas syāt vidyā-kr̥taḥ saṁskāraḥ)+++। 

**English**—
--But, again it is objected, 

> the agent is connected no less with ordinary worldly works than with works enjoined by the Veda,  
> and hence is not invariably connected with sacrifices (i.e. works of the latter type); it cannot, therefore, be maintained that meditations on the part of the agent necessarily connect themselves with sacrifices in so far as they effect a purification of the sacrificer's mind!--

**vi॰pra॰**—
naivam, laukikasya karmaṇaḥ  
kartur dēhād avyatiriktatvē 'py  
upapattēr dēhātirakta-nityātma-svarūpasya  
kratāv ēvōpayōgāt  
tat svarūpa-pratipādana-mukhēna  
kratv-anupravēśō na virudhyatē।

**English**—
There is a difference, the Pūrvapakshin rejoins. Worldly works can proceed also if the agent is non-different from the body; while an agent is qualified for sacred works only in so far as he is different from the body, and of an eternal non-changing nature. Meditations, therefore, properly connect themselves with sacrifices, in so far as they teach that the agent really is of that latter nature. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
atō vidyāyāḥ kratuśēṣatvānnātaḥ puruṣārthaḥ॥2॥

**English**—
We thus adhere to the conclusion that meditations are constituents of sacrificial actions, and hence are of no advantage by themselves.

##### karma-prādhānyam

**vi॰pra॰**—
kāni punastāni liṅgāni;  
yad-upabr̥ṁhita-sāmānādhikaraṇya-nirdēśēna  
"vēdānta-śabdā jīva-svarūpa-parā" iti nirṇīyantē। 

**English**—
--But what then are those inferential marks  
which, as you say, fully prove that the Vedānta-texts aim at setting forth the nature of the individual soul?--  

**vi॰pra॰**—
tatrāha –

**English**—
To this the next Sūtra replies.

###### karma-parā brahmavidaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
**421. ācāradarśanāt ॥ 3–4–3 ॥**

**English**—
3. On account of (such) conduct being seen.

**vi॰pra॰**—
brahmavidāṁ prādhānyēna karmasvēvācārō dr̥śyatē 

**English**—
It is seen, viz in Scripture, that those who knew Brahman busied themselves chiefly with sacrifices.

**vi॰pra॰**—
aśvapatiḥ kēkayaḥ kila ātmavittamaḥ  
tad-vijñānāyōpagatāṁs tān r̥ṣīn praty āha –  

> **yakṣyamāṇō ha vai bhagavantō 'ham asmi**  
> (chā.5.11.5) 

iti । 

**English**—
-- Aśvapati Kaikeya had a deep knowledge of the Self; but when three R̥shis had come to him to receive instruction regarding the Self, he told them 'I am about, to perform a sacrifice, Sirs' (Cḥ. Up. V, II). 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tathā janakādayō brahma-vid-agrēsarāḥ karmaniṣṭhāḥ smr̥tiṣu dr̥śyantē, 

**English**—
Similarly we learn from Smr̥ti that Janaka and other princes deeply versed in the knowledge of Brahman applied themselves to sacrificial works, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **karmaṇaiva hi saṁsiddhim  
> āsthitā janakādayaḥ** (bha.gī.3.20) 

**English**—
'By works only Janaka and others attained to perfection'; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **iyāja sō'pi subahūn  
> yajñān jñānavyapāśrayaḥ**  
> (vi.pu.6.6.12) 

iti । 

**English**—
> 'He also, well founded in knowledge, offered many sacrifices.' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
atō brahmavidāṁ karmapradhānatva-darśanād  
vidyāyāḥ kartr̥-svarūpa-vēdana-rūpatvēna  
karmāṅgatvam ēvēti  
na vidyātaḥ puruṣārthaḥ॥3॥

**English**—
And this fact – that those who know Brahman apply themselves to works chiefly – shows that knowledge (or meditation) has no independent value, but serves to set forth the true nature of the active Self, and thus is subordinate to work.--

###### karma-prādhānyē śrutiḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
liṅgam idam;  
prāptir ucyatām ity-atrāha –

**English**—
An even more direct proof is set forth in the next Sūtra.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **422. tacchrutēḥ ॥ 3–4–4 ॥**

**English**—
> 4. On account of direct scriptural statement.

**vi॰pra॰**—
śrutirēva hi vidyāyāḥ karmāṅgatvamāha – 

**English**—
Scripture itself directly declares knowledge to be subordinate to works, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **yad ēva vidyayā karōti  
śraddhayōpaniṣadā  
tad ēva vīryavattaraṁ bhavati**  
(chā.1.1.10) 

iti। 

**English**—
> 'whatever he does with knowledge, with faith, with the Upanishad, that is more vigorous'. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
nēyaṁ śrutiḥ prakaraṇād udgītha-mātra-viṣayēti vyavasthāpayituṁ śakyā;  
yataḥ prakaraṇāc chutir balīyasī;+++(4)+++ 

**English**—
Nor can it be said that this text refers, on the ground of leading subject-matter (prakaraṇa), to the Udgītha only; for direct scriptural statement (śuti) is stronger than subject-matter,

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **yad ēva vidyayā karōti** (chā.1.1.10) 

iti vidyāmātraviṣayā hīyaṁ śrutiḥ ॥4॥+++(5)+++

**English**—
and the words 'whatever he does with knowledge' clearly refer to knowledge in general.

###### vidyā-karma-sācaryam

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **423. +++(vidyākarmabhyām)+++ samanvārambhaṇāt ॥ 3–4–5 ॥**

**English**—
> 5\. On account of the taking hold together.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **taṁ vidyā-karmaṇī samanvārabhētē** (br̥.6.4.2) 

iti vidyā-karmaṇōs sāhityaṁ ca dr̥śyatē । 

**English**—
The text 'then both knowledge and work take hold of him' (Br̥. Up. IV, 4, 2) shows that knowledge and work go together, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
sāhityaṁ cōktēna nyāyēna  
vidyāyāḥ karmāṅgatvē saty ēva bhavati ॥

**English**—
and this going together is possible only if, in the manner stated, knowledge is subordinate to work.

###### vidyāvataḥ karma-vidhiḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
**424. +++(vidyā→)+++tadvatō vidhānāt ॥ 3–4–6 ॥**

**English**—
> 6\. On account of injunction for such a one.

**vi॰pra॰**—
vidyāvataḥ karma-vidhānād  
vidyā karmāṅgamityavagamyatē –

**English**—
That knowledge is subordinate to works follows therefrom also that works are enjoined on him only who possesses knowledge. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **ācārya-kulād vēdam adhītya  
> yathāvidhānaṁ gurōḥ karmātiśēṣēṇābhisamāvr̥tya  
> kuṭumbē śucau dēśē** (chā.8.15.1) 

ityādau । 

**English**—
For texts such as 'He who has learnt the Veda from a family of teachers,' &c. (Cḥ. Up. VIII, 15), 

**vi॰pra॰**—
**vēdam adhītya** (chā.8.15.1)  
ity adhyayanavataḥ karmāṇi vida-tad-arthāvabōdha-paryantādhyayanavata ēva vidadhāti । 

**English**—
enjoin works on him only who has mastered the sacred texts so as fully to understand their meaning-- 

**vi॰pra॰**—
arthāvabōdhaparyantaṁ hyadhyayanamiti sthāpitam । 

**English**—
for this is the sense of the term 'learning' (adhyayana).

**vi॰pra॰**—
atō brahmavidyā 'pi karmasu viniyuktēti  
na pr̥thak-phalāyāvakalpatē ॥6॥

**English**—
Hence the knowledge of Brahman also is enjoined with a view to works only:  
it has no independent result of its own.

###### yāvajjīvaṁ karma

**vi॰pra॰**—
**425. niyamāt +++(yāvajjīvaṁ karma)+++ ॥ 3–4–7 ॥**

**English**—
7\. On account of definite rule.

**vi॰pra॰**—
itaśca na vidyātaḥ puruṣārthaḥ - 

**English**—
Another argument for our conclusion is that 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> kurvannēvēha karmāṇi jijīviṣēcchataṁ samāḥ (īśa.2) 

ityātmavidaḥ, 

**English**—
the text 'Doing works here let a man desire to live a hundred years,' &c. (Is. Up. II), 

**vi॰pra॰**—
puruṣāyuṣasya sarvasya  
karmasu niyamēna viniyōgāt  
karmaṇa ēva phalam  
ity avagamyatē। 

**English**—
expressly enjoins lifelong works on him who knows the Self. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
vidyā tu karmāṅgamiti ॥7॥

**English**—
The general conclusion, therefore, is that knowledge (meditation) is merely auxiliary to works. 

#### brahmōpadēśō vidyāsu

**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvaṁ prāptē pracakṣmahē –

**English**—
Of this view the next Sūtra finally disposes.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **426. +++(brahma→)+++adhikōpadēśāt tu bādarāyaṇasyaivaṁ +++(siddhāntaḥ)+++ - +++(brahma-guṇādi→)+++tad-darśanāt ॥ 3–4–8 ॥**

**English**—
> 8\. But on account of the teaching of the different one, Badarāyaṇa's (view is valid); as this is seen.

**vi॰pra॰**—
tuśabdāt pakṣō vyāvr̥ttaḥ; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
vidyāta ēva puruṣārthaḥ; 

**English**—
Knowledge by itself benefits man; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
kutaḥ? adhikōpadēśāt –  
karmasu kartur jīvāt hēya-pratyanīkānavadhikātiśayāsaṅkhyēya- kalyāṇa-guṇākaratvēnādhikasya  
arthāntarabhūtasya parasya brahmaṇō vēdyatayōpadēśāt  
bhagavatō bādarāyaṇasya  
"vidyātaḥ phalaṁ" ityēvamēva matam । 

**English**—
Knowledge by itself benefits man; since Scripture teaches that the object of knowledge is the highest Brahman which, as it is of an absolutely faultless and perfect nature, is other than the active individual soul.

Badarāyaṇa, therefore, holds that knowledge has an independent fruit of its own. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
liṅgāni tiṣṭhantu;  
vēdyatayōpadēśas tu tāvat kartuḥ pratyag-ātmanō 'dhikasyaiva। 

**English**—
Let the inferential marks (referred to by the Pūrvapakshin) be; the direct teaching of the texts certainly refers to a being different from the Self that acts; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
katham? taddarśanāt – 

**vi॰pra॰**—
pratyag-ātmany a-śuddhē  
śuddhē 'py a-sambhāvanīyānanta-guṇākarasya vēdyasya  
nirasta-nikhila-hēya-gandhasya  
sva-saṅkalpa-kr̥ta-jagad-udaya-vibhava-laya-līlasya sarva-jñasya sarva-śaktēr  
vāṅ-manasā aparicchēdyānandasya  
jīvādhipasya  
kr̥tsnasya praśāsituḥ  
parasya brahmaṇō vēdanōpadēśavākyēṣu darśanāt – 

**English**—
for we clearly see that their object is the highest creative Brahman with all its perfections and exalted qualities, which cannot possibly be attributed to the individual Self whether in the state of Release or of bondage: 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **apahatapāpmā vijarō vimr̥tyur viśōkō  
vijighatsō 'pipāsas satya-kāmas satya-saṅkalpaḥ** (chā.8.1.5) 

**English**—
'Free from evil, free from old age,' &c. &c. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **tadaikṣata bahu syāṁ prajāyēyēti tattējō'sr̥jata** (chā.6.2.3) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **yassarvajñassarvavit** (muṇḍa.1.1.9)

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **parā'sya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyatē  
svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ca** (śvē.6.8) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **sa ēkō brahmaṇa ānandaḥ** (tai.āna.8.4) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **yatō vācō nivartantē  
aprāpya manasā saha  
ānandaṁ brahmaṇō vidvān  
na bibhēti kutaścana** (tai.āna.4.1) 

iti

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **ēṣa sarvēśvara  
ēṣa bhūtādhipatir  
ēṣa bhūtapāla  
ēṣa sētur vidharaṇaḥ**  
(br̥.6.4.22) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **sa kāraṇaṁ karaṇādhipādhipō,  
na cāsya kaścij janitā na cādhipaḥ** (śvē.6-9)

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **ētasya vā akṣarasya praśāsanē gārgi  
sūryā-candramasau vidhr̥tau tiṣṭhataḥ** (br̥.5.7.9) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **bhīṣāsmād vātaḥ pavatē ।  
bhīṣōdēti sūryaḥ।  
bhīṣāsmād agniś cēndraśca।  
mr̥tyur dhāvati pañcamaḥ**  
(tai.ā.8.1) 

ityādiṣu। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tasmād vēdanōpadēśa-śabdēṣu  
kartuḥ pratyag-ātmanaḥ khadyōta-kalpasya  
avidyādi-dēha-sambandha-yōgyasya  
gandhō'pi nāstīti 

**English**—
In all those texts there is not the slightest trace of any reference to the wretched individual soul, as insignificant and weak as a tiny glow-worm, implicated in Nescience and all the other evils of finite existence. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
parama-puruṣa-viṣayāyā vidyāyās  
tat-prāpti-rūpam a-mr̥tatvaṁ  
tatra tatra śrūyamāṇaṁ phalam  
iti vidyātaḥ puruṣārtha iti suṣṭhūktam ॥8॥

**English**—
And the fruit of that knowledge of the highest Person the texts expressly declare, in many places, to be immortality – which consists in attaining to Him. The view of knowledge by itself benefitting man therefore is well founded.--

#### pūrvapakṣōkta-liṅgāni

**vi॰pra॰**—
liṅgānyapi nirasyantē –

**English**—
The Sūtras proceed to dispose of the so-called inferential marks.

##### brahma-vidbhiḥ karma-tyāgaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
> **427. tulyaṁ tu darśanam ॥ 3–4–9 ॥**

**English**—
9\. But the declarations are equal.

**vi॰pra॰**—
yad uktaṁ –  

> brahma-vidāṁ karmānuṣṭhāna-darśanād  
vidyā karmāṅgam – 

iti; 

**English**—
The argument that knowledge must be held subordinate to work because we learn from Scripture that those who know Brahman perform sacrificial works, will not hold good; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tan na - vidyāyā anaṅgatvē'pi tulyaṁ darśanam, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
brahma-vidāṁ karmānuṣṭhāna-darśanam anaikāntikam ityarthaḥ, ananuṣṭhānasyāpi darśanāt । 

**vi॰pra॰**—
dr̥śyatē hi brahmavidāṁ karma-tyāgaḥ -  

> r̥ṣayaḥ kāvaṣēyāḥ kim-arthā vayam adhyēṣyāmahē  
kimarthā vayaṁ yakṣyāmahē 

ityādau। 

**English**—
since, on the other hand, we also see that men knowing Brahman abandoned all work; cp. texts such as 'The R̥shis descended from Kavasha said: For what purpose should we study the Veda? for what purpose should we sacrifice?' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
atō brahmavidāṁ karmatyāgadarśanānna vidyā karmāṅgam ।

**English**—
As it thus appears that those who know Brahman give up works, knowledge cannot be a mere auxiliary to works.

###### vidyāṅga-karma

**vi॰pra॰**—
> katham idam upapadyatē brahma-vidāṁ karmānuṣṭhānam ananuṣṭhānaṁ ca – 

**English**—
> --But how can it be accounted for that those who know Brahman both do and do not perform works?

**vi॰pra॰**—
phalābhisandhirahitasya yajñādi-karmaṇō brahma-vidyāṅgatvāt  
tathā-vidhasya karmaṇō 'nuṣṭhāna-darśanam upapadyatē । 

**English**—
--Works may be performed in so far as sacrifices and the like, if performed by one not having any special wish, stand in subordinate relation to the knowledge of Brahman; hence there is no objection to texts enjoining works. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
vakṣyati ca 

> **sarvāpēkṣā ca yajñādi-śrutēr aśvavat** (śārī.3.4.26) 

iti । 

###### phalārtha-karma-tyāgaḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
phalārthasya tasyaiva yajñādēḥ karmaṇō  
mōkṣaika-phala-brahma-vidyāvirōdhitvāt tasyānanuṣṭhāna-darśanam upapannataram। 

**English**—
And as, on the other hand, sacrifices and such-like works when aiming at results of their own are opposed to the knowledge of Brahman which has Release for its only result, there is all the less objection to texts which suggest the non-performance of works.  

**vi॰pra॰**—
vidyāyāḥ karmāṅgatvē karmatyāgaḥ kathamapi nōpapadyatē ॥ 9॥

**English**—
If, on the other hand, knowledge were subordinate to works, works could on no account be dispensed with.  

#### karmāṅga-vidyā 'sārvatrikī

**vi॰pra॰**—
yad uktaṁ – "śrutyaiva vidyāyāḥ karmāṅgatvam avagamyatē" iti; tatrāha –

**English**—
--Against the assertion that Scripture directly declares knowledge to be subordinate to works the next Sūtra declares itself.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **428. asārvatrikī +++(karmāṅga-vidyā-śrutiḥ)+++ ॥ 3–4–10 ॥**

**English**—
10\. (It is) non-comprehensive.

**vi॰pra॰**—
na sarvavidyāviṣayēyaṁ śrutiḥ; 

**English**—
The scriptural declaration does not refer to all meditations, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
api tūdgītha-vidyā-viṣayaiva

> **yad ēva vidyayā karōti** (chā.1.1.10) 

iti yac-chabdasyānirdhārita-viśēṣasya 

> **udgītham upāsīta** (chā.1.1.1) 

iti prastutōdgītha-viśēṣa-niṣṭhatvāt। 

**English**—
but only to the meditation on the Udgītha. In the clause 'what he does with knowledge,' the 'what' is in itself indefinite, and therefore must be defined as connecting itself with the Udgītha mentioned in the previous clause, 'Let him meditate on the Udgītha.' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
na hi "yat karōti, tad vidyayēti" sambadhyatē; +++(5)+++

**English**—
The sentence cannot be construed to mean 'whatever he does is to be done with knowledge,' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> yad ēva vidyayā karōti,  
tad ēva vīryavattaram 

iti vidyayā kriyamāṇaṁ yac-chabdēna nirdiśya  
tasya hi vīryavattaratvam ucyatē ॥10॥

**English**—
but means 'that which he does with knowledge becomes more vigorous,' and _that which is_ done with knowledge that is the Udgītha. 

#### vidyā-karma-sāhityam

**vi॰pra॰**—
yac cēdam uktaṁ  

> > **taṁ vidyākarmaṇī samanvārabhētē** (br̥.6.4.2) 
> 
> iti vidyā-karmaṇōs sāhitya-darśanāt  
vidyā karmāṅgam – 

iti; tatrāha-

**English**—
The next Sūtra refutes the argument set forth in Sūtra 5.

**vi॰pra॰**—
**429. vibhāgaś śatavat ॥ 3–4–11 ॥**

**English**—
11\. There is distribution, as in the case of the hundred.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **taṁ vidyākarmaṇī samanvārabhētē** (br̥.6.4.2) 

ity-atrōktēna nyāyēna  
vidyā-karmaṇōr bhinna-phalatvāt  
vidyā svasmai phalāya samanvārabhatē,  
karma ca svasmai phalāyēti vibhāgō draṣṭavyaḥ। 

**English**—
As knowledge and work have different results, the text 'of him knowledge and work lay hold' must be understood in a distributive sense, i.e. as meaning that knowledge lays hold of him to the end of bringing about its own particular result, and that so likewise does work. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
**śatavat** –  
yathā "kṣētra-ratna-vikrayiṇaṁ śata-dvayam anvētī"ty  
uktē kṣētrārthaṁ śatam,  
ratnārthaṁ śatam iti vibhāgaḥ pratīyatē;  
tathēhāpi ॥

**English**—
'As in the case of a hundred,' i.e. as it is understood that, when a man selling a field and a gem is said to receive two hundred gold pieces, one hundred are given for the field and one hundred for the gem.

#### avidyāvatō'pi karma-vidhiḥ
##### adhyayanamātravataḥ karma
**vi॰pra॰**—
> **430. adhyayanamātravataḥ ॥ 3–4–12 ॥**

**English**—
> 12\. Of him who has merely read the Veda.

**vi॰pra॰**—
yad uktaṁ 

> "vidyāvataḥ karmavidhānād  
vidyā karmāṅgam" 

\– iti; 

**English**—
In the argument that knowledge is only auxiliary to work because works are enjoined on him who possesses knowledge. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
naitadyuktam,  
**vēdamadhītya** (chā.8.15.1) ity adhyayanamātravatō vidhānāt । 

**English**—
Nor is there any force (in the above) -  

For the text which refers to the man 'who has read the Veda' enjoins works on him who has merely _read_ the texts, 

##### adhyayana-vidhi-paridhiḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
na cādhyayana-vidhir ēvārtha-bōdhē pravartayati,  
ādhānavad+++(=??)+++ adhyayanasyākṣara-rāśi-grahaṇa-mātrē paryavasānāt । 

**English**—
and _reading_ there means nothing more than the apprehension of the aggregate of syllables called Veda, without any insight into their meaning. 

##### arthagrahaṇaṁ rāgataḥ prāptam
**vi॰pra॰**—
gr̥hītasya ca svādhyāyasya phalavat-karmāvabōdhitva-darśanāt  
tan-nirṇaya-phalē tad-artha-vicārē  
puruṣaḥ svayam ēva pravartatē; 

**English**—
A man who has thus mastered the words of the Veda  
apprehends therefrom that  
it makes statements as to works having certain results,  
and then on his own account applies himself to the enquiry into the meaning of those declarations;  

**vi॰pra॰**—
tataḥ karmārthī karmajñānē pravartatē,  
mōkṣārthī ca brahmajñānē 

**English**—
he who is desirous of work applies himself to the knowledge of works; he who is desirous of Release applies himself to the knowledge of Brahman. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
iti na vidyā karmāṅgam । 

##### arthagrahaṇavidhau
**vi॰pra॰**—
yad yapy adhyayana-vidhir ēvārthāvabōdhē pravartayati;  
tathāpi na vidyā karmāṅgam,  
arthajñānād arthāntaratvād vidyāyāḥ। 

**English**—
And even if the injunction of _reading_ were understood as prompting to the understanding of the text also, all the same, knowledge would not be a subsidiary to works.  
For _knowledge_, in the sense of the Upanishads, is something different from mere cognition of sense. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
yathā jyōtiṣ-ṭōmādi--karma-svarūpa-vijñānāt  
phala-sādhana-bhūtaṁ karmānuṣṭhānam arthāntaram; 

**English**—
In the same way as the performance of such works as the Jyotishṭoma sacrifice is something different from the cognition of the true nature of those works; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tathā 'rthajñāna-rūpāt brahma-svarūpa-vijñānāt  
arthāntaram ēva dhyānōpāsanādi-śabda-vācyā puruṣārtha-sādhana-bhūtā vidyā 

**English**—
so that vidyā, which effects the highest purpose of man, i. e. devout meditation (dhyāna, upāsanā), is something different from the mere cognition of the true nature of Brahman. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
iti na tasyāḥ karma-sambandha-gandhō vidyatē ॥12॥

**English**—
Knowledge of that kind has not the most remote connexion even with works.

#### yāvajjīvaṁ karma vidyāṅgabhūtam

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **431. nāviśēṣāt ॥ 3–4–13 ॥**

**English**—
> 13\. Not so, on account of non-specification.

**vi॰pra॰**—
yac cōktaṁ  
**kurvann ēvēha karmāṇi** (īśā.2) ity ātma-vidaṁ jñānād vyāvartya  
yāvaj jīvaṁ karmānuṣṭhānē niyamayatīti; 

**English**—
That the text 'Doing works here,' &c., is meant to divert him who knows the Self from knowledge and restrict him to works. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tannōpapadyatē; aviśēṣāt – 

**English**—
Nor is this true -  

**vi॰pra॰**—
na hy ayaṁ niyamaḥ -  
+++(sa vidhiḥ)+++ phala-sādhana-bhūta--svatantra-karma-viṣaya  
iti +++(mantuṁ)+++ viśēṣa-hētur asti, vidyāṅga-bhūta-karma-viṣayatayā 'py upapattēḥ। 

**English**—
For there is no special reason  
to hold that that text refers to works as independent means of a desirable result:  
it may as well be understood to refer to works merely subordinate to knowledge. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **karmaṇaiva hi saṁsiddhim  
āsthitā janakādayaḥ**  
(bha.gī.3.20)  

iti ca viduṣas tv  
āprayāṇād upāsanasya anuvartamānatvāt ॥13॥

**English**—
As he who knows the Self has to practise meditation as long as he lives, he may also have to practise, for the same period, works that are helpful to meditation. 

##### vidyā-stutayē karmānumatiḥ
**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvam artha-svābhāvyēna cōdyaṁ parihr̥tya  
**kurvannēvēha karmāṇi** (ī.2) ityasya vākyasyārtham āha –

**English**—
Having thus refuted the objection on the ground of the reason of the matter, the Sūtrakāra proceeds to give his own interpretation of the text.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **432. stutayē 'numitar vā ॥ 3–4–14 ॥**

**English**—
> 14\. Or the permission is for the purpose of glorification.

**vi॰pra॰**—
vā-śabdō 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ; 

**English**—
The or has assertive force. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **īśā vāsyim idaṁ sarvam** (īśā.1) 

iti vidyā-prakaraṇād  
vidyā-stutayē sarvadā karmānuṣṭhānānumatir iyam। 

**English**—
The introductory words of the Upanishad, 'Hidden in the Lord is all this,' show knowledge to be the subject-matter; hence the permission of works can aim only at the glorification of knowledge. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
vidyā-māhātmyāt  
sarvadā karma kurvann api  
na lipyatē karmabhir  
iti hi vidyā stutā bhavati । 

**English**—
The sense of the text therefore is – owing to the power of knowledge a man although constantly performing works is not stained by them.

**vi॰pra॰**—
vākya-śēṣaś caivam ēva darśayati,  

> **ēvaṁ tvayi nānyathētō'sti  
na karma lipyatē narē** (īśā.2) 

iti। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
atō na karmāṅgaṁ vidyā ॥ 14॥

#### viduṣā gārhasthya-tyāgaḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **433. kāma-kārēṇa caikē +++(gārhāsthya-tyāgam adhīyatē)+++ ॥ 3–4–15 ॥**

**English**—
> 15\. Some also, by proceeding according to their liking.

**vi॰pra॰**—
api caivam ēkē śākhinaḥ  
kāma-kārēṇa brahma-vidyā-niṣṭhasya gārhāsthya-tyāgam adhīyatē  

> **kiṁ prajayā kariṣyāmō  
yēṣāṁ nō 'yam ātmā 'yaṁ lōkaḥ**  
(br̥.6.4.22) 

iti। 

**English**—
In some śākhās, moreover, we read that  
he who possesses the knowledge of Brahman may,  
according to his liking,  
give up the state of a householder, 

> 'What shall we do with offspring,  
we who have this Self and this world?' (Br̥. Up. V, 4, 22.) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
viduṣō viraktasya kāma-kārēṇa  
gārhāsthya-karma-tyāgaṁ bruvad idaṁ vacanaṁ  
brahma-vidyāyāḥ karmānaṅgatvaṁ darśayati । 

**English**—
This text also proves knowledge not to be subsidiary to works;  
for if it were so subsidiary, it would not be possible for him who knows Brahman to give up householdership (with all the works obligatory on that state) according to his liking.

**vi॰pra॰**—
yajñādi-karmāṅgatvē hi vidyāyāḥ  
vidyā-niṣṭhasya kāma-kārēṇa gārhāsthya-tyāgō  
na sambhavati । 

**vi॰pra॰**—
atō na vidyā karmāṅgam ॥ 15॥

#### karmōpamardaḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **434. +++(sañcita-karma-)+++upamardaṁ ca +++(adhīyatē)+++ ॥ 3–4–16 ॥**

**English**—
> 16\. And destruction.

**vi॰pra॰**—
puṇyāpuṇya-rūpasya samasta-sāṁsārika-duḥkha-mūlasya karmaṇō  
brahma-vidyayōpamardaṁ ca  
prativēdāntam adhīyatē। 

**English**—
There is moreover a Vedānta-text which declares the knowledge of Brahman to destroy work-good and evil- which is the root of all the afflictions of transmigratory existence: 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **bhidyatē hr̥daya-granthiś  
chidyantē sarvasaṁśayāḥ।  
kṣīyantē cāsya karmāṇi  
tasmin dr̥ṣṭē parāvarē**  
(muṇḍa.2.2.8) 

ity-ādikam।

**English**—
> 'The knot of the heart is broken,  
all doubts are solved,  
all his works perish  
when He has been beheld who is high and low'  
(Mu. Up. II, 2, 8). 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tad vidyāyāḥ karmāṅgatvē na saṅgacchatē॥16॥

**English**—
This also contradicts the view of knowledge being subordinate to works.

#### ūrdhvarētassu brahmavidyā

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **435. +++(brahma-vidyā)+++ ūrdhvarētassu ca śabdē hi ॥ 3–4–17 ॥**

**English**—
> 17\. And of him who is chaste; for in Scripture (this is declared).

**vi॰pra॰**—
ūrdhvarētassv āśramēṣu  
brahma-vidyā-darśanāt  
tēṣv agnihōtra--darśa-pūrṇa-māsādi-rkarmābhāvāc ca  
na vidyā karmāṅgam। 

**English**—
The knowledge of Brahman belongs to those who have to observe chastity, and men living in that state have not to perform the Agnihotra, the Darśapūrṇamāsa, and similar works. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> nanūrdhvarētasa āśramā na santy ēva -  
**yāvaj-jīvam agnihōtraṁ juhōti** (āpa.śrauta.3-14-5)  
ityādinā 'gni-hōtra--darśa-pūrṇa-māsādīnāṁ  
yāvaj-jīvādhikāra-śrutēḥ;  
śruti-viruddhānāṁ smr̥tīnāṁ cāprāmāṇyāt।

**English**—
For this reason also knowledge cannot be subsidiary to works.--But, it may be objected, there is no such condition of life; for texts such as 'he is to perform the Agnihotra as long as he lives,' declare men to be obliged to perform sacrifices and the like up to the end of their lives, and Smr̥ti texts contradicting Scripture have no authority.

**vi॰pra॰**—
ata āha – śabdē hi – iti । 

**English**—
--To meet this the Sūtra adds 'for in Scripture.' 

**vi॰pra॰**—
vaidika ēva hi śabdē tē dr̥śyantē 

**English**—
The three stages of life are recognised in Scripture only; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
**trayō dharma-skandhāḥ** (chā.2.23.1) 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> yē cēmē'raṇyē śraddhā tapa ityupāsatē (chā.5.10.1) 

**English**—
cp. texts such as  

> 'Those who in the forest practise penance and faith' (Cḥ. Up. V, 10, 1); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **ētam ēva pravrājinō lōkim icchantaḥ pravrajanti** (br̥ha.6.4.22) 

ityādau। 

**English**—
'Wishing for that world only mendicants wander forth from their homes' (Br̥. Up. IV, 4, 22). 

**vi॰pra॰**—
yāvaj-jīva-śrutis tv a-virakta-viṣayā ॥17॥

**English**—
The text as to the lifelong obligatoriness of the Agnihotra is valid for those only who do not retire from worldly life.

##### ūrdhvarēta-āśrama-sadbhāvaḥ

###### anuvādamātram iti pakṣaḥ

acōdanāc ca, apavadati hi ॥ 3–4–18 ॥**

atas tē +++(ūrdhvarētasa āśramāḥ)+++ santy ēva

iti; 

**English**—
The argument for the three stages of life, founded on their mention in Vedic texts, 

**vi॰pra॰**—

**English**—
has no force, since all those references are only of the nature of anuvāda.

kuta ētat? acōdanāt – avidhānādityarthaḥ। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
na hy atra vidhiśabdaḥ śrūyatē;

**English**—
For none of those texts contain injunctive forms. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **trayō dharmaskandhāḥ** (chāṁ.2.23.1) 

ity-ādinā hi  
prakr̥taṁ praṇavēna brahmōpāsanaṁ stūyatē, 

**English**—
The text 'There are three branches of sacred observance,' &c. (Cḥ. Up. II, 23, 1), is meant to glorify the previous meditation on Brahman under the form of the pranava, 

**vi॰pra॰**—
**brahma-saṁsthō 'mr̥tatvam ēti** (chāṁ.2.23.1)  
ity upasaṁhārāt । 

**English**—
as appears from the concluding clause 'he who is firmly grounded in Brahman obtains immortality';

atō 'nyārtham anuvāda-mātram atra kriyatē  
tēṣām āśramāṇām।  

**English**—
it therefore cannot mean to enjoin the three conditions of life as valid states. 

**vi॰pra॰**—

iti ca dēva-yāna-vidhi-paratvāt

**English**—
In the same way the text 'And those who in the forest practise penance and faith' refers to the statements previously made as to the path of the gods, and cannot therefore be meant to make an original declaration as to another condition of life. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
api cāpavadati hi śrutir āśramāntaraṁ  

> **vīrahā vā ēṣa dēvānāṁ  
yō'gnim udvāsayatē**  
(yaju.1.kāṁ.5.2) 

ity-ādikā ।

**vi॰pra॰**—
ata ūrdhvarētasa āśramā na santīti jaiminirācāryō manyatē ॥18॥

**English**—

**vi॰pra॰**—
**437. +++(gr̥hasthētarāśrama-gatam apy)+++ anuṣṭhēyaṁ +++(iti)+++ bādarāyaṇas - +++(anuṣṭhēyatvē tēṣu)+++ sāmyaśrutēḥ॥ 3–4–19 ॥**

**English**—

**vi॰pra॰**—
kutaḥ?  
**sāmya-śrutēḥ** –

**vi॰pra॰**—
upādēyatayā 'bhimata-gr̥hasthāśrama-sāmyaṁ hi

**vi॰pra॰**—
**trayō dharmaskandhāḥ** (chāṁ.2.23.1) ityārabhya  
brahma-saṁstha-stuty-arthatayā saṅkīrtanaṁ  
gr̥hasthāśramasyētarēṣāṁ ca samānam; 

**English**—
since in the section beginning 'there are three branches of sacred duty' all the three conditions of life are equally referred to,  
with a view to glorifying him who is firmly grounded in Brahman.  

**vi॰pra॰**—
atha 

> gr̥hasthāśramasyānuvādaḥ  
prāptau satyām ēva sambhavatīti  
tasya prāptir avaśyābhyupēyā+++(~~tya~~)+++

iti matam;  
tad-itarēṣām api samānam,  
anyatrābhinivēśāt।

**English**—
The reference there made to the condition of the householder  
necessarily presupposes that condition to be already established and obligatory,  
and the same reasoning then holds good  
with regard to the other conditions mentioned.

###### trayō dharma-skandhāḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
na ca 

> gārhāsthyadharma ēva  
> 
> > **yajñō'dhyayanaṁ dānaṁ tapō brahmacaryam** (chāṁ.2.23.1) 
> 
> iti sarvaiś śabdair abhidhīyatē,  
brahmacarya-tapasōr gr̥hasthasyaiva sambhavād 

iti yuktam, 

**English**—
Nor must it be said that the special duties mentioned at the beginning of the section--  
sacrifice, study, charity, austerity, Brahmacarya--  
all of them belong to the state of the householder  
(in which case the text would contain no reference to the other conditions of life); 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **trayō dharmaskandhāḥ** (chā.2.23.1) 

iti tritvēna saṅgr̥hya  

> +++(yajñō'dhyayanaṁ dānam iti)+++ **prathamaḥ**   
+++(tapa ēva)+++ **dvitīyaḥ**… 
+++(brahmacāryācāryakulavāsī)+++**tr̥tīyaḥ** …. (chāṁ.2.23.11) 

iti vibhāga-vacanānupapattēḥ। 

**English**—
for on that supposition the definite reference to a threefold division of duties, 'Sacrifice, &c. are the first, austerity the second, Brahmacarya the third,' would be unmeaning. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
ataḥ **yajñō'dhyayanaṁ dānam** (chā.2.23.1) iti gr̥hasthāśrama ucyatē। 

**42tamāhōbila-yatiḥ**—
The proper explanation is to take the words ' sacrifice, study, and charity' as descriptive of the condition of the householder; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
adhyayanaśabdō vēdābhyāsaparaḥ। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tapaśśabdēna vaikhānasa-pārivrājyayōr grahaṇam,  
ubhayōḥ tapaḥ-pradhānatvāt। 

**English**—
the word 'austerity' as descriptive of the duties of the Vaikhānasa and the wandering mendicant, who both practise mortification; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tapaśśabdō hi kāyaklēśē rūḍhaḥ, sa ca dvayōrapi samānaḥ। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
brahma-cāri-dharma ēva brahma-carya-śabdēnābhidhīyatē। 

**English**—
and the word 'Brahmacarya' as referring to the duties of the Brahmacarin. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
**brahma-saṁsthō'mr̥tatvam ēti** (chā.2.23.1) 

iti paratra śrūyamāṇō brahma-saṁstha-śabdō yaugikaḥ sarvāśrama-sādhāraṇaḥ,  
sarvēṣāmāśramiṇāṁ brahma-saṁsthā-sambhavāt। 

**English**—
The term 'Brahmasaṁstha' finally, in the concluding clause, refers to all the three conditions of life, as men belonging to all those conditions may be founded on Brahman. 

**vi॰pra॰**—
brahmaṇi saṁsthā – saṁsthitiḥ brahma-saṁsthatvam;  
tac ca sarvēṣāṁ sambhavatyēva। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
brahma-niṣṭhā-vikalāḥ kēvalāśramiṇaḥ puṇya-lōka-bhājaḥ;  
tēṣv ēva brahma-niṣṭhō 'mr̥tatva-bhāg bhavati। 

**English**—
Those, the text means to say, who are destitute of this foundation on Brahman and only perform the special duties of their condition of life, obtain the worlds of the blessed;  
while he only who at the same time founds himself on Brahman attains to immortality.

varṇānām āśramāṇāṁ ca kēvalānāṁ brahma-lōka-prāpty-antaṁ phalam abhidhāya

yadvai paśyanti sūrayaḥ**  
(vi.pu.1.6.39) 

**vi॰pra॰**—

###### nigamanam

**vi॰pra॰**—
atō gr̥hasthāśramatulyāḥ ūrdhvarētasa āśramā api dr̥śyanta iti tē'pyanuṣṭhēyāḥ। 

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **yē cēmē'raṇyē śraddhā tapa ityupāsatē** (chā.5.10.1) 

iti ca  
"araṇyē" iti tapaḥ-pradhānāśrama-prāpty-apēkṣatvād  
dēvayāna-vidhānasya tatrāpi tat-prāptir aṅgīkaraṇīyā ॥ 19॥

**English**—
--In the text 'and those who in the forest,' &c. the mention made of the forest shows that the statement as to the path of the gods has for its presupposition the fact that that stage of life which is especially connected with the forest is one generally recognised.

###### āśrama-vidhir ēva

**vi॰pra॰**—
parāmarśapakṣē vidhānapakṣē ca  
gr̥hasthāśrama-tulyam ēṣām apyanuṣṭhēyatvam ity upapādya  
vidhir ēvāyām āśramāṇāṁ sarvēṣāṁ,  
nānuvāda ityupapādayitumāha –

**English**—
--So far it has been shown that the other stages of life are no less obligatory than that of the householder, whether we take the text under discussion as containing merely a reference to those stages (as established by independent means of proof) or as directly enjoining them. The next Sūtra is meant to show that the latter view is after all the right one.

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **438. vidhir vā +++(anuvādaprāya-vākya-vihita-samid-)+++dhāraṇavat ॥ 3–4–20 ॥**

**English**—
> 20\. Or an injunction, as in the case of the carrying.

**vi॰pra॰**—
vā-śabdō'vadhāraṇārthaḥ । 

**vi॰pra॰**—
vidhir ēvāyam āśramāṇām; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
dhāraṇavat – yathā diṣṭāgnihōtrē,  

> adhastāt samidhaṁ dhārayann anudravēd  
upari hi dēvēbhyō dhārayati  

ity-atrānuvāda-+++(~~sa~~)+++svarūpād api vākyād  
upari dhāraṇasyāprāptatvād  
vidhir āśrīyatē; 

**English**—
As the second part of the text  

> 'Let him approach carrying the firewood below the ladle;  
for above he carries it for the gods'  
(which refers to a certain form of the Agnihotra), 

although having the form of an anuvāda,  
yet must be interpreted as an injunction,  
since the carrying of firewood above is not established by any other injunction;  

**vi॰pra॰**—
taduktaṁ śēṣalakṣaṇē **vidhistu dhāraṇō'pūrvatvāt** (pū.mī.sū.3.4.15) iti; 

**vi॰pra॰**—
tathā'trāpy aprāptatvād  
vidhir ēvāśrayaṇīyaḥ ॥

**English**—
so the text under discussion also must be taken as an injunction of the different stages of life (which are not formally enjoined elsewhere). 

###### jābāla-vidhiḥ

**vi॰pra॰**—
> **brahmacaryaṁ samāpya  
gr̥hī bhavēt  
gr̥hād vanī bhūtvā pravrajēt  
yadi vētarathā brahmacaryād ēva pravrajēt  
gr̥hād vā, vanād vā,  
yadaharēva virajēt tad-aharēva pravrajēt** (jābā.u.4) 

**English**—
'Having completed his studentship he is to become a householder,' &c., 

**vi॰pra॰**—
iti jābālānām āśrama-vidhim asantam iva kr̥tvā,  
ētēṣv anya-parēṣv api vākyēṣv  
āśrama-prāptir avaśyāśrayaṇīyā  
ity upapāditam ।

**English**—
No account being taken of the text of the Jābālas,  
it is thus a settled conclusion that the texts discussed,  
although primarily concerned with other topics,  
must at the same time be viewed as proving the validity of the several conditions of life.  

##### nigamanam

**vi॰pra॰**—
ēvam āśramāntara-vidhānāt  
r̥ṇa-śrutir yāvaj-jīva-śrutir apavāda-śrutiś+++(=??-)+++ cāvirakta-viṣayā ēvēti vēditavyāḥ। 

**English**—
From this it follows that the text enjoining the performance of the Agnihotra up to the end of life, and similar texts, are not universally binding, but concern those only who do not retire from worldly life.--

**vi॰pra॰**—
anyāś ca brahma-vidaḥ  
karmaṇām āprayāṇāt avaśya-kartavyatā-vidhāyinyaḥ śrutayaḥ smr̥tayaś ca  
sva-svāśrama-dharma-viṣayāḥ ।

**English**—
The final conclusion therefore is that as the knowledge of Brahman is enjoined on those who lead a life of austerity (which does not require the performance of sacrifices and the like), it is not subordinate to works, but is in itself beneficial to man.

**vi॰pra॰**—
ata ūrdhvarētassu ca brahma-vidyā-vidhānād  
vidyātaḥ puruṣārtha iti siddham ॥20॥

**vi॰pra॰**—
**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē puruṣārthādhikaraṇam ॥ 1॥**

**English**—
--Here terminates the adhikaraṇa of 'benefit to man.'

### 02 stutimātrādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē stutimātrādhikaraṇam ॥2॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
sa ēṣa rasānām ityādivākyānām udgīthādau rasatamādidr̥ṣṭividhiparatvamēva

**439. stutimātramupādānāditi cēnnāpūrvatvāt ॥ 3–4–21 ॥**

#### vicāraṇīyō viṣayaḥ sasaṁśayaḥ

idamidānīṁ cintyatē **sa ēṣa rasānāṁ rasatamaḥ paramaḥ parārthyō'ṣṭamō yadudgīthaḥ** (chā.1.1.3) iti ēvañjātīyakāni vākyāni kratvavayavabhūtōdgīthādistutimātraparāṇi, āhōsvidudgīthādiṣu rasatamādidr̥ṣṭividhānārthānīti ।

#### tannirdhāraṇāniyamādhikaraṇasya ētadadhikaraṇōpajīvyatvam

atra pratipāditamupāsanaparatvamaṅgīkr̥tyōpāsanasya puruṣārthatvēna kratuṣūpādānāniyama uktaḥ।

#### pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ sayuktikaḥ

kiṁ yuktam? stutimātraparāṇīti ।

kutaḥ? udgīthādyupādānāt। kratvaṅgabhūtāni hyudgīthādīnyupādāya tēṣāṁ rasatamāditvaṁ pratipādatam; yathā juhvādīnāṁ pr̥thivyāditvaṁ pratipādayatō vacanasya iyamēva juhūḥ svargō lōka āhavanīyaḥ ityādikasya tatstutimātraparatvam, tathēhāpi । tadidamāśaṅkatē – stutimātramupādānāditi cēt – iti। udgīthādyupādānāttatstutimātramēvaiṣāṁ vākyānāṁ vivakṣitamiti cēt

#### siddhāntārthaḥ sahētukaḥ

atrōttaraṁ – nāpūrvatvāt – iti। na stutimātratvamupapadyatē; kutaḥ? apūrvatvāt – aprāptatvāt। na hyudgīthādayō rasatamāditayā pramāṇāntarēṇa pratipannāḥ; yēna tatprāśastyabuddhyutpattyarthaṁ rasatamāditvēnānūdyēran। nacōdgīthādividhiratra sannihitaḥ; yēna iyamēva juhūssvargō lōka āhavanīyaḥ ityādivattadēkavākyatvēna yayā kayācanavidhayā tatstutiparatvamāśrīyēta । ataḥ kratuvīryavattaratvādiphalasiddhyartham udgīthādiṣu rasatamādidr̥ṣṭividhānamēva nyāyyam ॥21॥

**440. bhāvaśabdācca ॥ 3–4–22 ॥**

**upāsīta** (chā.1.1.1) ityādibhāvaśabdācca vidhiparatvamēva nyāyyam । vidhipratyayayuktō hi kriyāśabdō vidhēyamēva svārthamavagamayati । tasmādupāsanavidhānārthā ētāśśrutayaḥ ॥22॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē stutimātrādhikaraṇam॥2॥**

### 03 pāriplavārthādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē pāriplavārthādhikaraṇam॥3॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
upaniṣatsūpalabhyamānānām ākhyānānāṁ vidyāvidhyarthatvamēva na tu aśvamēdhāṅgapāriplavanāmakaśastrārthatvam

**441. pāriplavārthā iti cēnna viśēṣitatvāt ॥ 3–4–23 ॥**

#### vicāraṇīyō viṣayaḥ sasaṁśayaḥ

**pratardanō ha vai daivōdāsirindrasya priyaṁ dhāmōpajagāma** (kau.3.1) śvētakēturhāruṇēya āsa (chā.6.1.1) ityēvamādīni vēdāntēṣvākhyānāni kiṁ pāriplavaprayōgārthāni, uta vidyāviśēṣapratipādanārthānīti cintāyām –

#### pūrvapakṣaḥ

**ākhyānāni śaṁsanti** (?) ityākhyānānāṁ pāriplavē viniyōgānna vidyāpradhānatvaṁ nyāyyamiti cēt

#### siddhaāntārthaḥ

na sarvāṇyākhyānāni pāriplavaprayōgē viniyōgamarhānti; kutaḥ? viśēṣitatvādviniyōgasya। ākhyānāni śaṁsanti ityuktvā tatraiva
manurvaivasvatō rājā ityādinā manvādīnāmākhyānāni viśēṣyantē, atastēṣāmēva tatra viniyōga iti gamyatē । tasmānna sarvā vēdāntēṣvākhyānaśrutayaḥ pāriplavaprayōgārthāḥ; api tu vidyāvidhyarthāḥ ॥23॥

#### ākhyānānāṁ darśanavidhyaikavākyāt uktārthasiddhiḥ

**442. tathā caikavākyōpabandhāt ॥ 3–4–24 ॥**

**ātmā vā arē draṣṭavyaḥ** (br̥.6-5-6) ityādividhinaikavākyatayōpabandhāccākhyānānāṁ vidyāvidhyarthānyēva tānīti gamyatē; **yathā sō'rōdīt** (yaju.1-5-1) ityēvamādēḥ karmavidhyarthatvam; na pāriplavārthatvam॥24॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē pāriplavārthādhikaraṇam॥3॥**

### 04 agnīndhanādyadhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē agnīndhanādyadhikaraṇam॥ 4॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
parivrājikānāṁ vidyāsiddhiḥ, svāśramavihitakarmāpēkṣaiva, na tu agnyādhānapūrvakakarmāpēkṣā

**443. ata ēva cāgnīndhanādyanapēkṣā ॥ 3–4–25 ॥**

#### pūrvādhikaraṇayōḥ prāsaṅgikatā, prakr̥tasaṅgatiśca

stutiprasaṅagādavāntarasaṅgativiśēṣēṇārthadvayaṁ cintitam । vidyāvanta ūrdhvarētasa āśramiṇaḥ santītyuktam **ūrdhvarētassu ca śabdē hi** (śārī.3.4.27) ityādibhissūtraiḥ।

#### pūrvapakṣasiddhāntau

idānīmūrdhvarētasō yajñādyabhāvāttadaṅgikā vidyā na sambhavatītyāśaṅkyāha – ata ēva cāgnīndhanādyanapēkṣā – iti । yata ūrdhvarētasa āśramiṇō vidyāsambandhitvēna śrutyā parigr̥hyantē **brahmasaṁsthō'mr̥tatvamēti** (chā.2.23.1) **yē cēmē'raṇyē śraddhā tapa ityupāsatē** (chā.5.10.1) **ētamēva pravrājinō lōkamicchantaḥ pravrajanti** (br̥.6.4.22) **yadicchantō brahmacaryaṁ caranti** (kaṭha.1.2.15) ityādikayā; ata ēvōrdhvarētassu vidyā agnīndhanādyanapēkṣā agnīndhanam – agnyādhānam; ādhānapūrvakāgnihōtradarśapūrṇamāsādikarmānapēkṣā tēṣu vidyā । kēvalasvāśramavihitakarmāpēkṣētyarthaḥ॥25॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē agnīndhanādyadhikaraṇam॥4॥**

### 05 sarvāpēkṣādhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē sarvāpēkṣādhikaraṇam॥5॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
karmādhikr̥tāśramiṇāṁ tu brahmavidyā karmasāpēkṣaiva niṣpannā bhavēt

**444. sarvāpēkṣā ca yajñādiśrutēraśvavat ॥ 3–4–26 ॥**

#### gr̥hiṣvapi karmāpēkṣārāhityaśaṅkā, tannirāsaśca

yadi vidyā yajñādyanapēkṣaivāmr̥tatvaṁ sādhayati; tarhi gr̥hasthēṣvapi tadanapēkṣaiva sādhayitumarhati, **yajñādiśrutirapi vividiṣanti** (br̥.6.4.22) iti śabdātkarmaṇō vēdanāṅgatāṁ na pratipādayatīti –

ata āha – sarvāpēkṣā iti। agnihōtrādisarvakarmāpēkṣaiva vidyā karmavatsu gr̥hasthēṣu; kutaḥ? yajñādiśrutēḥ। tamētaṁ vēdānuvacanēna brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti **yajñēna dānēna tapasā'nāśakēna** (br̥.6.4.22) ityādinā yajñādayō hi vidyāṅgatvēna śrūyantē। yajñādinā vividiṣanti vēditumicchanti, yajñādibhirvēdanaṁ prāptumicchantītyarthaḥ। yajñādīnāṁ jñānasādhanatvē satyēva yajñādibhiḥ jñānaṁ prāptumicchantīti vyapadēśa upapadyatē; yathā asērhānanasādhanatvē sati asinā jighāṁsatīti vyapadēśaḥ। atō yajñādīnāṁ jñānasādhanatvamavagamyatē ॥

#### mōkṣōpāyatayā avagataṁ viśiṣṭaṁ jñānam

jñānaṁ ca vākyārthajñānādarthāntarabhūtaṁ dhyānōpāsanādiśabdavācyaṁ viśadatamapratyakṣatāpanna-smr̥tirūpaṁ niratiśayapriyamaharaharabhyāsādhēyātiśayamāprayāṇādanuvartamānaṁ mōkṣasādhanamityuktamasmābhiḥ pūrvamēva; vakṣyati ca **āvr̥ttirasakr̥dupadēśāt** (bra.sū.4.1.1) ityādinā।

#### jñānaṁ prati karmaṇāṁ sahakāritvaprakāraḥ

ēvaṁ rūpaṁ ca dhyānamaharaharanuṣṭhīyamānairnityanaimittikakarmabhiḥ paramapuruṣārādhanarūpaiḥ paramapuruṣaprasādadvārēṇa jāyata iti yajñādinā vividiṣantīti śāstrēṇa pratipādyatē । ataḥ karmavatsu gr̥hasthēṣu yajñādinityanaimittikasarvakarmāpēkṣā vidyā। aśvavat – yathā gamanasādhanabhūtō'śvaḥ svaparikarabandha-parikarmāpēkṣaḥ; ēvaṁ mōkṣasādhanabhūtā'pi vidyā nityanaimittikakarmaparikarāpēkṣā । tadidamāha svayamēva bhagavān **yajñadānatapaḥ karma na tyājyaṁ kāryamēva tat। yajñō dānaṁ tapaścaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām** (bha.gī.18.5) **yataḥ pravr̥ttirbhūtānāṁ yēna sarvamidaṁ tatam। svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṁ vindati mānavaḥ** (bha.gī.18.46) iti ॥26॥

**iti śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē sarvāpēkṣādhikaraṇam॥ 5॥**

### 06 śamadamadyadhikaraṇam

**śrīśārīrakamīmāṁsābhāṣyē śamadamādyadhikaraṇam॥6॥**

**adhikaraṇārthaḥ**—
gr̥hasthasya yajñādivat vidyāṅgatayā śamadamādayōpyanuṣṭhēyā ēva

**445. śamadamādyupētassyāttathāpi tu tadvidhēḥ**

**tadaṅgatayā tēṣāmapyavaśyānuṣṭhēyatvāt ॥ 3–4–27 ॥**

#### prakr̥tavicārāṅgaḥ saṁśayaḥ, pūrvapakṣaśca
